`UnrealMCP/Source/UnrealMcpEditor/Private/Tools/UnrealMcpGeneratedSkills.h`:

```h
// Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
// See the LICENSE file in the repository root for more information.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

class FUnrealMcpToolRegistry;

/**
 * The registration bus for GENERATED skills — the C++ tool files `unreal-skill-create` writes into
 * `UnrealMCP/Source/UnrealMcpEditor/Private/Tools/Skills/` (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §2.4).
 *
 * WHY a bus instead of patching the coordinator: every hand-written family is wired by an explicit
 * `UnrealMcpXTools::Register(*Registry)` line in UnrealMcpEditorCoordinator.cpp. Having a TOOL rewrite
 * that file on every generated skill would mean machine-patching a hand-maintained source file — not
 * idempotent, merge-hostile, and one bad edit away from breaking the whole plugin's boot path. Instead a
 * generated skill self-registers: each generated .cpp declares a file-scope
 * FUnrealMcpGeneratedSkillRegistrar whose constructor appends its Register function here at static-init
 * time, and the coordinator calls UnrealMcpGeneratedSkills::Register(*Registry) exactly ONCE (added in
 * the same change that introduced this header, never touched again). Adding or deleting a generated
 * skill is then purely "drop / remove a .cpp and rebuild" — UBT picks up new .cpp files in a module
 * automatically.
 *
 * Static-init-order safety: the backing array is a function-local static (constructed on first use), so a
 * registrar in ANY translation unit can run before or after any other and still find a live array. The
 * modules are unity-built, so a generated file's namespace/symbol names must be unique — the generator
 * derives them from the tool id (see UnrealMcpSkillTools::SkillSymbolFromToolId).
 */
namespace UnrealMcpGeneratedSkills
{
	/** Signature of a generated skill's registration entry point (matches a hand-written family's Register). */
	using FRegisterFn = void (*)(FUnrealMcpToolRegistry&);

	/** Append @p Fn to the pending registration list. Called from static init; never null-checked away. */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API void Add(FRegisterFn Fn);

	/** How many generated skills self-registered into this build (0 in a clean checkout). */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API int32 Num();

	/**
	 * Run every self-registered generated skill against @p Registry, in link order, inside an EXTENSION
	 * SCOPE (ExtensionId `generated-skill`) — never the core path. Generated skills are machine-authored
	 * and hand-editable, so they are untrusted: the extension scope validates each entry and rejects a
	 * collision first-wins ("extensions may not shadow core"), which is what actually stops a generated
	 * `actor-create` from replacing the built-in. ORDER IS NOT THE GUARD — the core path replaces any
	 * same-key entry, so committing there would let a generated id win outright (and running LAST would
	 * make that certain). Called once by the editor coordinator after the hand-written core families.
	 */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API void Register(FUnrealMcpToolRegistry& Registry);
}

/**
 * File-scope self-registrar a generated skill declares once:
 *
 *     static const FUnrealMcpGeneratedSkillRegistrar Registrar(&Register);
 *
 * Constructing it enrolls the function; there is nothing to unregister (generated skills live for the
 * module's lifetime, exactly like the hand-written families).
 */
struct UNREALMCPEDITOR_API FUnrealMcpGeneratedSkillRegistrar
{
	explicit FUnrealMcpGeneratedSkillRegistrar(UnrealMcpGeneratedSkills::FRegisterFn Fn)
	{
		UnrealMcpGeneratedSkills::Add(Fn);
	}
};

```

`UnrealMCP/Source/UnrealMcpEditor/Private/Tools/UnrealMcpPythonTools.cpp`:

```cpp
// Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
// See the LICENSE file in the repository root for more information.

#include "UnrealMcpCoreTools.h"
#include "UnrealMcpSchema.h"
#include "UnrealMcpToolArgs.h"
#include "UnrealMcpToolRegistry.h"
#include "Config/UnrealMcpConfig.h"
#include "Tools/UnrealMcpLogCollector.h"

#include "Dom/JsonObject.h"
#include "Dom/JsonValue.h"
#include "Editor.h"
#include "Editor/TransBuffer.h"
#include "IPythonScriptPlugin.h"
#include "Interfaces/IPluginManager.h"
#include "Internationalization/Regex.h"
#include "Misc/Base64.h"
#include "Misc/EngineVersionComparison.h"
#include "Misc/Paths.h"
#include "PythonScriptTypes.h"
#include "Serialization/JsonReader.h"
#include "Serialization/JsonSerializer.h"

namespace UnrealMcpPythonTools
{
	/** <Project>/.ai-game-dev/snippets: where relative `include` paths resolve. */
	static FString PythonIncludeRoot()
	{
		return FPaths::ConvertRelativePathToFull(FPaths::Combine(FPaths::ProjectDir(), TEXT(".ai-game-dev"), TEXT("snippets")));
	}

	/** True when the plugin's Content/Python (glue + vendored runtime) is installed; the engine puts it on sys.path. */
	static bool PythonRuntimeInstalled()
	{
		const TSharedPtr<IPlugin> Plugin = IPluginManager::Get().FindPlugin(TEXT("UnrealMCP"));
		return Plugin.IsValid() && FPaths::DirectoryExists(FPaths::Combine(Plugin->GetContentDir(), TEXT("Python"), TEXT("unreal_mcp")));
	}

	static const TCHAR* PythonLogLevel(EPythonLogOutputType Type)
	{
		return Type == EPythonLogOutputType::Error ? TEXT("error") : Type == EPythonLogOutputType::Warning ? TEXT("warning") : TEXT("info");
	}

	/** Engine warnings / errors returned per call; the rest is counted (the console source has them all). */
	static constexpr int32 PythonMaxEngineLogs = 20;

	static TSharedPtr<FJsonValue> PythonLogEntry(const TCHAR* Level, const FString& Message)
	{
		TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Log = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();
		Log->SetStringField(TEXT("level"), Level);
		Log->SetStringField(TEXT("message"), Message);
		return MakeShared<FJsonValueObject>(Log);
	}

	/**
	 * Warnings and errors other categories logged on the game thread (where the snippet runs; background threads'
	 * lines are not its doing) after @p AfterSequence: a failed LoadAsset, a refused property write. Command.LogOutput
	 * carries only LogPython, so without them a snippet fails silently with a null result. The collector is an
	 * unbuffered GLog device, so it already holds every line logged synchronously: no flush needed.
	 */
	static void PythonAddEngineLogs(int64 AfterSequence, TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>>& Logs)
	{
		static const FName LogPythonCategory(TEXT("LogPython"));
		int32 Matched = 0;
		for (const FUnrealMcpLogEntry& Entry : FUnrealMcpLogCollector::Get().SnapshotAfter(AfterSequence))
		{
			if (!Entry.bGameThread || Entry.Category == LogPythonCategory || Entry.Verbosity > ELogVerbosity::Warning)
				continue;
			if (++Matched <= PythonMaxEngineLogs)
				Logs.Add(PythonLogEntry(Entry.Verbosity == ELogVerbosity::Warning ? TEXT("warning") : TEXT("error"),
					FString::Printf(TEXT("%s: %s"), *Entry.Category.ToString(), *Entry.Message.TrimEnd())));
		}
		if (Matched > PythonMaxEngineLogs)
			Logs.Add(PythonLogEntry(TEXT("warning"), FString::Printf(
				TEXT("%d more engine warning(s)/error(s): read them with rql-query on the console source"), Matched - PythonMaxEngineLogs)));
	}

	/**
	 * Output budget per call (characters): a runaway print loop or a huge value must not flood the agent's context. The
	 * code_exec runtime (Code-Exec contract §6) already clips the value, the error and its own logs to these numbers (the
	 * logs to a little less, see PythonRuntimeLogChars); the
	 * caps here cover what the plugin adds afterwards: unreal.log*() output, engine messages and a failed bootstrap. The
	 * numbers equal the runtime's defaults and are sent explicitly, so both layers read one set.
	 */
	static constexpr int32 PythonMaxValueChars = 20000;
	static constexpr int32 PythonMaxLogChars = 20000;
	static constexpr int32 PythonMaxLogLineChars = 2000;
	static constexpr int32 PythonLogLineOverhead = 12; // the newline and "[warning] " around each message in the text form (as Code-Exec counts)
	// The runtime's own logs get a smaller budget: room for its one "left out" entry (about 120 characters with the 12 of
	// overhead, rounded up), so the plugin cap below never cuts the runtime's output a second time.
	static constexpr int32 PythonRuntimeLogChars = PythonMaxLogChars - 256;

	/**
	 * The snippet's time budget (Code-Exec timeoutMs): what is left of the call's timeout (UNREAL_MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT; the call
	 * may have waited for the game thread or for Python to start) less a margin for the reply, so code_exec's watchdog stops
	 * an endless loop and frees the game thread before the dispatcher gives up on the call. Never 0, which means no bound.
	 */
	static int32 PythonTimeBudgetMs(const FUnrealMcpToolCall& Call)
	{
		const int32 Timeout = Call.TimeoutMs > 0 ? Call.TimeoutMs : FUnrealMcpConfig::DefaultToolTimeoutMs; // none: a direct call (tests)
		const double Waited = Call.ReceivedSeconds > 0.0 ? (FPlatformTime::Seconds() - Call.ReceivedSeconds) * 1000.0 : 0.0;
		const int32 Left = FMath::Max(Timeout - FMath::RoundToInt(Waited), 1);
		const int32 Margin = FMath::Clamp(Timeout / 10, 2000, 15000);
		return FMath::Max(Left - Margin, FMath::Max(Left / 2, 1));
	}

	/** Said when a snippet that calls setters recorded nothing for undo (UE records only objects that were Modify()'d). */
	static const TCHAR* PythonNoUndoNote = TEXT("this run recorded no undo step: direct setters (set_actor_location, set_actor_scale3d ...) "
		"do not record undo or mark the level unsaved, so TRANSACTION UNDO would revert the PREVIOUS edit instead. Call obj.modify() "
		"before changing an object, or use set_editor_property / rql-mutate, when the change must be undoable and saved.");

	/** Whether the code calls a setter-like API (set_*, add_*, attach_*, destroy_*, spawn_*): the no-undo note is only worth it then. */
	static bool PythonLooksMutating(const FString& Code)
	{
		static const FRegexPattern Pattern(TEXT("\\.(set_|add_|attach_|destroy_|spawn_|k2_set)[A-Za-z0-9_]*\\s*\\("));
		FRegexMatcher Matcher(Pattern, Code);
		return Matcher.FindNext();
	}

	/**
	 * The undo-step title of a run: "python-execute: " and the first line of the code that is not an import or a comment
	 * (at most 80 characters), so the Undo History and TRANSACTION UNDO say which run they revert.
	 */
	static FString PythonUndoTitle(const FString& Code)
	{
		static constexpr int32 MaxChars = 80;
		TArray<FString> Lines;
		Code.ParseIntoArrayLines(Lines);
		for (const FString& Raw : Lines)
		{
			const FString Line = Raw.TrimStartAndEnd();
			if (Line.IsEmpty() || Line.StartsWith(TEXT("#")) || Line.StartsWith(TEXT("import ")) || Line.StartsWith(TEXT("from ")))
				continue;
			return TEXT("python-execute: ") + (Line.Len() > MaxChars ? Line.Left(MaxChars - 3) + TEXT("...") : Line);
		}
		return TEXT("python-execute");
	}

	static FString PythonClip(const FString& Text, int32 Max, const TCHAR* Hint)
	{
		return Text.Len() <= Max ? Text : FString::Printf(TEXT("%s... [truncated: %d of %d characters shown; %s]"),
			*Text.Left(Max), Max, Text.Len(), Hint);
	}

	/**
	 * Clips the long lines the plugin added (from FirstOwn on: the runtime's lines are clipped already, and clipping them
	 * again would misreport their length), then keeps the first and the last lines within the budget and says how many
	 * were left out. Returns whether anything was shortened.
	 */
	static bool PythonCapLogs(TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>>& Logs, int32 FirstOwn)
	{
		int32 Total = 0;
		bool bClipped = false;
		TArray<int32> Sizes;
		for (int32 Index = 0; Index < Logs.Num(); ++Index)
		{
			const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Log = Logs[Index]->AsObject();
			FString Message = Log->GetStringField(TEXT("message"));
			if (Index >= FirstOwn && Message.Len() > PythonMaxLogLineChars)
			{
				Message = PythonClip(Message, PythonMaxLogLineChars, TEXT("print less"));
				Log->SetStringField(TEXT("message"), Message);
				bClipped = true;
			}
			Sizes.Add(Message.Len() + PythonLogLineOverhead);
			Total += Sizes.Last();
		}
		if (Total <= PythonMaxLogChars)
			return bClipped;
		const int32 HeadBudget = PythonMaxLogChars * 3 / 4;
		int32 Head = 0, Used = 0;
		while (Head < Logs.Num() && Used + Sizes[Head] <= HeadBudget)
			Used += Sizes[Head++];
		int32 Tail = Logs.Num();
		while (Tail > Head && Used + Sizes[Tail - 1] <= PythonMaxLogChars)
			Used += Sizes[--Tail];
		TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>> Kept(Logs.GetData(), Head);
		Kept.Add(PythonLogEntry(TEXT("warning"), FString::Printf(TEXT("... %d log line(s) left out (output over %d characters): print less, or return a summary"),
			Tail - Head, PythonMaxLogChars)));
		Kept.Append(Logs.GetData() + Tail, Logs.Num() - Tail);
		Logs = MoveTemp(Kept);
		return true;
	}

	/** The EvaluateStatement result is the repr of a base64 string: the payload between the quotes, nothing escaped. */
	static TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> PythonDecodeResponse(const FString& CommandResult)
	{
		FString Payload = CommandResult.TrimStartAndEnd();
		if (Payload.Len() < 2)
			return nullptr;
		Payload = Payload.Mid(1, Payload.Len() - 2);
		TArray<uint8> Bytes;
		if (!FBase64::Decode(Payload, Bytes))
			return nullptr;
		const FString Json = FString(FUTF8ToTCHAR(reinterpret_cast<const ANSICHAR*>(Bytes.GetData()), Bytes.Num()));
		TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Response;
		const TSharedRef<TJsonReader<>> Reader = TJsonReaderFactory<>::Create(Json);
		return FJsonSerializer::Deserialize(Reader, Response) ? Response : nullptr;
	}

	/** Diagnostics + logs as text lines for the human-readable message (the structured response carries them too). */
	static FString PythonDetails(const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject>& Response)
	{
		FString Text;
		for (const TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>& Value : Response->GetArrayField(TEXT("diagnostics")))
		{
			const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> D = Value->AsObject();
			Text += FString::Printf(TEXT("\n%s(%d,%d): %s"), *D->GetStringField(TEXT("file")), (int32)D->GetNumberField(TEXT("line")),
				(int32)D->GetNumberField(TEXT("column")), *D->GetStringField(TEXT("message")));
		}
		const TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>>& Logs = Response->GetArrayField(TEXT("logs"));
		if (Logs.Num() > 0)
			Text += TEXT("\nLogs:");
		for (const TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>& Value : Logs)
		{
			const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> L = Value->AsObject();
			Text += FString::Printf(TEXT("\n[%s] %s"), *L->GetStringField(TEXT("level")), *L->GetStringField(TEXT("message")));
		}
		return Text;
	}

	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API void Register(FUnrealMcpToolRegistry& Registry)
	{
		Registry.Tool(TEXT("python-execute"))
			.Title(TEXT("Execute Python"))
			.Description(TEXT("Run Python inside the Unreal Editor (PythonScriptPlugin, full `unreal` API, pre-imported). Write "
			                  "plain statements; the LAST EXPRESSION is the result (objects come back as their paths). "
			                  "print() and unreal.log*() output is returned as logs; errors point at snippet.py lines. Each "
			                  "call starts from a fresh namespace. Its recorded edits are one undo step (so the snippet itself cannot run TRANSACTION UNDO); only "
			                  "objects that are Modify()'d record (set_editor_property, editor subsystems, obj.modify() first): direct setters such as "
			                  "set_actor_location are neither undoable nor marked unsaved. Engine warnings and errors raised while it "
			                  "runs are returned as logs too. A run that outlives the tool timeout is stopped with a Timeout error "
			                  "(a blocking unreal call finishes first); sys.setrecursionlimit is capped at 3000. Output is capped (~20k characters each for the value and the logs). 'include': helper files/folders (relative to "
			                  "<Project>/.ai-game-dev/snippets): folders are importable, files run before the code. Blueprint "
			                  "graph wiring is not available from Python: add nodes and connect pins with rql-mutate "
			                  "(unreal.asset(path).EventGraph | call AddEvent / AddCallFunction, node | call Connect)."))
			.ParamString(TEXT("code"), TEXT("Python code. Example: \"actors = unreal.get_editor_subsystem(unreal.EditorActorSubsystem)"
			                                "\\nlen(actors.get_all_level_actors())\""), EUnrealMcpParamRequirement::Required)
			.Param(TEXT("include"), TEXT("array"), TEXT(""), EUnrealMcpParamRequirement::Optional,
				FUnrealMcpSchema::StringArray(TEXT("Helper .py files or folders, relative to <Project>/.ai-game-dev/snippets or absolute.")))
			.DestructiveHint(true)
			.OpenWorldHint(true)
			.Handle([](const FUnrealMcpToolCall& Call) -> FUnrealMcpToolResult
			{
				const FString Code = Call.GetString(TEXT("code"));
				if (Code.TrimStartAndEnd().IsEmpty())
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("Missing required 'code'."));

				FString IncludeError;
				const TArray<FString> Include = FUnrealMcpToolArgs::GetStringArray(Call, TEXT("include"), IncludeError);
				if (!IncludeError.IsEmpty())
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(FString::Printf(TEXT("InvalidRequest: %s"), *IncludeError));

				IPythonScriptPlugin* Python = IPythonScriptPlugin::Get();
#if UE_VERSION_OLDER_THAN(5, 6, 0)
				const bool bPythonReady = Python != nullptr && Python->IsPythonAvailable();
#else
				// ForceEnablePythonAtRuntime overrides the "enabled by default" settings, but it returns true even when the
				// interpreter did not come up: IsPythonInitialized afterwards is the real check.
				if (Python != nullptr && !Python->IsPythonInitialized())
				{
					Python->ForceEnablePythonAtRuntime();
					// On a fresh editor Python is configured at the end of engine init and finishes initializing on its
					// first tick. Until then ask the dispatcher to retry on a later tick (bounded by the call's timeout).
					if (!Python->IsPythonConfigured() || (Python->IsPythonAvailable() && !Python->IsPythonInitialized()))
						return FUnrealMcpToolResult::RetryLater(TEXT("Python is still starting."));
				}
				const bool bPythonReady = Python != nullptr && Python->IsPythonInitialized();
#endif
				if (!bPythonReady)
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("NotAvailable: Python is not available in this editor (PythonScriptPlugin disabled or failed to start)."));
				if (!PythonRuntimeInstalled())
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("NotAvailable: the plugin's Content/Python folder (the code_exec runtime) is missing."));

				TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Request = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();
				Request->SetStringField(TEXT("code"), Code);
				Request->SetStringField(TEXT("includeRoot"), PythonIncludeRoot());
				Request->SetBoolField(TEXT("includeOutsideRoot"), true); // the tool documents absolute include paths
				Request->SetNumberField(TEXT("maxValueChars"), PythonMaxValueChars);
				Request->SetNumberField(TEXT("maxLogChars"), PythonRuntimeLogChars);
				Request->SetNumberField(TEXT("maxLogLineChars"), PythonMaxLogLineChars);
				Request->SetNumberField(TEXT("maxErrorChars"), PythonMaxValueChars);
				Request->SetNumberField(TEXT("timeoutMs"), PythonTimeBudgetMs(Call));
				TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>> Imports;
				Imports.Add(MakeShared<FJsonValueString>(TEXT("unreal")));
				Request->SetArrayField(TEXT("imports"), Imports);
				TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>> IncludeValues;
				for (const FString& Path : Include)
					IncludeValues.Add(MakeShared<FJsonValueString>(Path));
				Request->SetArrayField(TEXT("include"), IncludeValues);
				const FTCHARToUTF8 Utf8(*UnrealMcpSerializeCondensed(Request));

				// base64 both ways: agent code is never quoted into Python source, and the response never needs unescaping.
				FPythonCommandEx Command;
				Command.ExecutionMode = EPythonCommandExecutionMode::EvaluateStatement;
				Command.Flags = EPythonCommandFlags::Unattended;
				Command.Command = FString::Printf(TEXT("__import__('unreal_mcp.python_execute', fromlist=['run']).run('%s')"),
					*FBase64::Encode(reinterpret_cast<const uint8*>(Utf8.Get()), Utf8.Length()));
				// One undo step, as rql-mutate (the transaction buffer drops it when a read-only snippet recorded nothing).
				const int64 LogSequence = FUnrealMcpLogCollector::Get().GetLastSequence();
				const int32 Transaction = GEditor ? GEditor->BeginTransaction(TEXT("UnrealMcp"), FText::FromString(PythonUndoTitle(Code)), nullptr) : INDEX_NONE;
				// Only Modify()'d objects with actual changes record: after a run of direct setters (set_actor_location)
				// the transaction is dropped as empty, and an undo would revert the PREVIOUS edit. Our own (top-level)
				// transaction is the last queue entry; whether it survives EndTransaction tells (nested: unknowable).
				FGuid OwnTransaction;
				if (Transaction == 0 && GEditor->Trans && GEditor->Trans->GetQueueLength() > 0)
					if (const FTransaction* Current = GEditor->Trans->GetTransaction(GEditor->Trans->GetQueueLength() - 1))
						OwnTransaction = Current->GetContext().TransactionId;
				const bool bRan = Python->ExecPythonCommandEx(Command);
				if (Transaction != INDEX_NONE)
					GEditor->EndTransaction();
				const bool bRecordedNothing = OwnTransaction.IsValid() && GEditor->Trans->FindTransactionIndex(OwnTransaction) == INDEX_NONE;

				const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Response = bRan ? PythonDecodeResponse(Command.CommandResult) : nullptr;
				if (!Response.IsValid())
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(FString::Printf(TEXT("Python bootstrap failed: %s"),
						*PythonClip(Command.CommandResult, PythonMaxValueChars, TEXT("see the editor log"))));

				// unreal.log*() and engine messages raised during the call bypass sys.stdout: add them to the logs.
				TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>> Logs = Response->GetArrayField(TEXT("logs"));
				const int32 FirstOwn = Logs.Num();
				for (const FPythonLogOutputEntry& Entry : Command.LogOutput)
					Logs.Add(PythonLogEntry(PythonLogLevel(Entry.Type), Entry.Output.TrimEnd()));
				PythonAddEngineLogs(LogSequence, Logs);
				if (bRecordedNothing && Response->GetBoolField(TEXT("success")) && PythonLooksMutating(Code))
					Logs.Add(PythonLogEntry(TEXT("warning"), PythonNoUndoNote));
				if (PythonCapLogs(Logs, FirstOwn))
				{
					// The response says which fields a limit shortened, in the order value, logs, error (contract §6).
					const TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>>* Truncated = nullptr;
					TArray<FString> Fields;
					if (Response->TryGetArrayField(TEXT("truncated"), Truncated))
						for (const TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>& Field : *Truncated)
							Fields.Add(Field->AsString());
					if (!Fields.Contains(TEXT("logs")))
						Fields.Insert(TEXT("logs"), Fields.Contains(TEXT("value")) ? 1 : 0);
					TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>> Values;
					for (const FString& Field : Fields)
						Values.Add(MakeShared<FJsonValueString>(Field));
					Response->SetArrayField(TEXT("truncated"), Values);
				}
				Response->SetArrayField(TEXT("logs"), Logs);
				FString Value; // already clipped by the runtime (maxValueChars), as the error is (maxErrorChars)
				const bool bHasValue = Response->TryGetStringField(TEXT("value"), Value);

				const FString Details = PythonDetails(Response);
				if (!Response->GetBoolField(TEXT("success")))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(FString::Printf(TEXT("%s: %s%s"),
						*Response->GetStringField(TEXT("errorKind")), *Response->GetStringField(TEXT("error")), *Details));

				return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Success((bHasValue ? Value : TEXT("null")) + Details, Response);
			});
	}
}

```

`UnrealMCP/Source/UnrealMcpEditor/Private/Tools/UnrealMcpScreenshotTools.cpp`:

```cpp
// Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
// See the LICENSE file in the repository root for more information.

#include "UnrealMcpCoreTools.h"
#include "UnrealMcpToolRegistry.h"
#include "UnrealMcpLog.h"
#include "Tools/UnrealMcpObjectRef.h"

#include "Dom/JsonObject.h"
#include "Misc/App.h"
#include "Misc/Base64.h"
#include "Misc/ScopeExit.h"
#include "Modules/ModuleManager.h"
#include "UObject/GCObjectScopeGuard.h"

#include "Editor.h"
#include "UnrealClient.h"
#include "ImageUtils.h"
#include "TextureResource.h"

#include "GameFramework/Actor.h"
#include "Engine/World.h"
#include "Engine/TextureRenderTarget2D.h"
#include "Engine/SceneCapture2D.h"
#include "Components/SceneCaptureComponent2D.h"
#include "Camera/CameraComponent.h"

/**
 * The screenshot / viewport-capture tool family (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §10 "screenshot family", issue
 * #17). Four kebab-case CORE tools that return a base64 PNG as MCP image content:
 *
 *  - `screenshot-viewport`   — active editor viewport via FViewport::ReadPixels.
 *  - `screenshot-game-view`  — PIE/game view via the PIE FViewport; structured error when no PIE session.
 *  - `screenshot-camera`     — render from a §3.2-resolved camera actor through a transient
 *                              USceneCaptureComponent2D into a render target, then read back.
 *  - `screenshot-isolated`   — isolated actor render: transient SceneCapture2D + show-only list +
 *                              neutral background (the Godot SubViewport pattern mapped to UE).
 *
 * Every handler runs ON the game thread (the dispatcher guarantees it, §4). Captures are dimension-
 * capped (default 1024, hard cap 2048 per side; width/height clamped). Actual pixel capture needs a
 * GPU — headless `-nullrhi` cannot render, so each capture path validates its arguments first (those
 * branches are GPU-free and headless-spec-covered) and only then attempts the GPU read-back, returning
 * a structured "rendering unavailable" error under `-nullrhi` instead of crashing. The capture paths
 * themselves are LIVE-VERIFIED WINDOWED (issue #17 verification model).
 */
namespace UnrealMcpScreenshotTools
{
	// ---- GPU-free dimension logic (exported in UnrealMcpCoreTools.h for headless specs) -------------

	int32 ResolveCaptureDimension(int64 Requested)
	{
		if (Requested <= 0)
			return DefaultCaptureDimension;
		return (int32)FMath::Clamp<int64>(Requested, (int64)1, (int64)MaxCaptureDimension);
	}

	void CapToMaxDimension(int32 InW, int32 InH, int32& OutW, int32& OutH)
	{
		OutW = FMath::Max(InW, 1);
		OutH = FMath::Max(InH, 1);
		const int32 LongestSide = FMath::Max(OutW, OutH);
		if (LongestSide > MaxCaptureDimension)
		{
			const double Scale = (double)MaxCaptureDimension / (double)LongestSide;
			OutW = FMath::Max(1, FMath::RoundToInt(OutW * Scale));
			OutH = FMath::Max(1, FMath::RoundToInt(OutH * Scale));
		}
	}

	FUnrealMcpToolResult MakeImageResult(const FString& Source, int32 Width, int32 Height, const FString& Base64Png, int32 EncodedBytes)
	{
		// The metadata travels in the text block: SuccessWithImage carries no structured content (see there).
		const FString Message = FString::Printf(TEXT("Captured %s (%dx%d, image/png, %d bytes)."),
			*Source, Width, Height, EncodedBytes);
		UE_LOG(LogUnrealMcp, Log, TEXT("[Unreal-MCP] %s"), *Message);
		return FUnrealMcpToolResult::SuccessWithImage(Message, Base64Png);
	}

	// ---- Local helpers ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

	namespace
	{
		// Keep the encoded payload well under the §1.2 64 MiB IPC line cap (base64 expands ~4/3).
		static constexpr int64 MaxEncodedBytes = 40 * 1024 * 1024;

		/** True when the editor can render; false under headless `-nullrhi`. */
		bool EnsureRenderingAvailable(FString& OutError)
		{
			if (!FApp::CanEverRender())
			{
				OutError = TEXT("Rendering is unavailable (headless/-nullrhi). Screenshot capture requires a "
				                "GPU-backed editor; run the editor windowed and retry.");
				return false;
			}
			return true;
		}

		/** Force every pixel opaque so a viewport/render-target alpha of 0 does not yield a transparent PNG. */
		void ForceOpaque(TArray<FColor>& Pixels)
		{
			for (FColor& Pixel : Pixels)
				Pixel.A = 255;
		}

		/** Resample a captured buffer to (DstW, DstH) when it differs from the source size. */
		void ResizeIfNeeded(TArray<FColor>& Pixels, int32 SrcW, int32 SrcH, int32 DstW, int32 DstH)
		{
			if ((SrcW == DstW && SrcH == DstH) || DstW <= 0 || DstH <= 0)
				return;
			TArray<FColor> Resized;
			Resized.SetNumUninitialized(DstW * DstH);
			FImageUtils::ImageResize(SrcW, SrcH, Pixels, DstW, DstH, Resized, /*bResizeSRGBinLinearSpace*/ false);
			Pixels = MoveTemp(Resized);
		}

		/** Encode a BGRA8 FColor buffer to a base64 PNG (forcing opaque first). */
		bool EncodePngBase64(TArray<FColor>& Pixels, int32 Width, int32 Height,
			FString& OutBase64, int32& OutEncodedBytes, FString& OutError)
		{
			if (Width <= 0 || Height <= 0)
			{
				OutError = TEXT("Capture produced a zero-sized image.");
				return false;
			}
			if (Pixels.Num() < Width * Height)
			{
				OutError = FString::Printf(TEXT("Capture pixel buffer (%d) is smaller than %dx%d."), Pixels.Num(), Width, Height);
				return false;
			}
			ForceOpaque(Pixels);

			TArray64<uint8> Png;
			FImageUtils::PNGCompressImageArray(Width, Height,
				TArrayView64<const FColor>(Pixels.GetData(), (int64)Width * (int64)Height), Png);
			if (Png.Num() == 0)
			{
				OutError = TEXT("PNG encoding produced no bytes.");
				return false;
			}
			if (Png.Num() > MaxEncodedBytes)
			{
				OutError = FString::Printf(
					TEXT("Encoded PNG (%lld bytes) exceeds the %lld-byte cap; request a smaller width/height."),
					(int64)Png.Num(), MaxEncodedBytes);
				return false;
			}
			OutBase64 = FBase64::Encode(Png.GetData(), Png.Num());
			OutEncodedBytes = (int32)Png.Num();
			return true;
		}

		/**
		 * Effective output size for a viewport-style capture. When BOTH width and height are supplied they
		 * are each clamped to [1, 2048]; when only ONE is supplied the other is derived from the native
		 * aspect ratio (so a lone width=512 on a 1920x1080 viewport yields 512x288, not a stretched
		 * 512x1080); when NEITHER is supplied the native size is used. The result is then hard-capped.
		 */
		void EffectiveViewportSize(const FUnrealMcpToolCall& Call, int32 NativeW, int32 NativeH, int32& OutW, int32& OutH)
		{
			const int64 ReqW = Call.GetInt(TEXT("width"), 0);
			const int64 ReqH = Call.GetInt(TEXT("height"), 0);
			int32 W, H;
			if (ReqW > 0 && ReqH > 0)
			{
				W = ResolveCaptureDimension(ReqW);
				H = ResolveCaptureDimension(ReqH);
			}
			else if (ReqW > 0)
			{
				W = ResolveCaptureDimension(ReqW);
				H = NativeW > 0 ? FMath::Max(1, FMath::RoundToInt(W * (double)NativeH / (double)NativeW)) : NativeH;
			}
			else if (ReqH > 0)
			{
				H = ResolveCaptureDimension(ReqH);
				W = NativeH > 0 ? FMath::Max(1, FMath::RoundToInt(H * (double)NativeW / (double)NativeH)) : NativeW;
			}
			else
			{
				W = NativeW;
				H = NativeH;
			}
			CapToMaxDimension(W, H, OutW, OutH);
		}

		/** Read + encode an FViewport (editor or PIE). Called only on the GPU-available path. */
		FUnrealMcpToolResult CaptureFromViewport(const FUnrealMcpToolCall& Call, FViewport* Viewport, const FString& Source)
		{
			const FIntPoint Size = Viewport->GetSizeXY();
			if (Size.X <= 0 || Size.Y <= 0)
				return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(FString::Printf(TEXT("The %s has a zero-sized render area."), *Source));

			Viewport->Draw(); // ensure a current frame is present before the read-back

			TArray<FColor> Pixels;
			if (!Viewport->ReadPixels(Pixels, FReadSurfaceDataFlags(), FIntRect(0, 0, Size.X, Size.Y)))
				return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(FString::Printf(TEXT("Failed to read pixels from the %s."), *Source));

			int32 OutW = 0, OutH = 0;
			EffectiveViewportSize(Call, Size.X, Size.Y, OutW, OutH);
			ResizeIfNeeded(Pixels, Size.X, Size.Y, OutW, OutH);

			FString Base64; int32 Bytes = 0; FString Error;
			if (!EncodePngBase64(Pixels, OutW, OutH, Base64, Bytes, Error))
				return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(Error);

			return MakeImageResult(Source, OutW, OutH, Base64, Bytes);
		}

		/**
		 * Render through a transient SceneCapture2D into a transient render target, then read back. The
		 * capture actor is spawned RF_Transient + hidden from the outliner and destroyed on every path, so
		 * the editor world is never dirtied. Called only on the GPU-available path.
		 */
		FUnrealMcpToolResult CaptureWithSceneCapture(
			UWorld* World, const FTransform& CaptureXform, float FovDeg, int32 Width, int32 Height,
			const FString& Source, const FLinearColor* BackgroundColor, AActor* ShowOnlyActor)
		{
			// Isolated mode (a background was requested) composites the actor over a solid color. A plain
			// SCS_FinalColorLDR capture writes opaque pixels everywhere, overwriting the render target's
			// ClearColor — so an empty region renders as the scene's (black) background, NOT the requested
			// color (verified windowed: a #FF0000 background came back pure black). To honor the background
			// we capture coverage-carrying HDR scene color (SCS_SceneColorHDR, inverse opacity in alpha)
			// into a float target and composite scene-over-background in the read-back. screenshot-camera
			// passes no background and keeps the cheaper tonemapped LDR path.
			const bool bComposite = (BackgroundColor != nullptr);

			UTextureRenderTarget2D* RenderTarget = NewObject<UTextureRenderTarget2D>(GetTransientPackage());
			RenderTarget->RenderTargetFormat = bComposite ? RTF_RGBA16f : RTF_RGBA8;
			RenderTarget->ClearColor = BackgroundColor ? *BackgroundColor : FLinearColor::Black;
			RenderTarget->bAutoGenerateMips = false;
			RenderTarget->InitAutoFormat(Width, Height);
			RenderTarget->UpdateResourceImmediate(true);
			FGCObjectScopeGuard RenderTargetGuard(RenderTarget);

			FActorSpawnParameters SpawnParams;
			SpawnParams.ObjectFlags |= RF_Transient;
			SpawnParams.bTemporaryEditorActor = true;
			SpawnParams.bHideFromSceneOutliner = true;
			SpawnParams.SpawnCollisionHandlingOverride = ESpawnActorCollisionHandlingMethod::AlwaysSpawn;

			ASceneCapture2D* CaptureActor = World->SpawnActor<ASceneCapture2D>(
				ASceneCapture2D::StaticClass(), CaptureXform, SpawnParams);
			if (!CaptureActor)
				return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("Failed to spawn a transient SceneCapture2D actor."));
			ON_SCOPE_EXIT { if (IsValid(CaptureActor)) CaptureActor->Destroy(); };

			USceneCaptureComponent2D* Capture = CaptureActor->GetCaptureComponent2D();
			if (!Capture)
				return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("Transient SceneCapture2D had no capture component."));

			Capture->TextureTarget = RenderTarget;
			Capture->FOVAngle = FovDeg;
			Capture->CaptureSource = bComposite ? SCS_SceneColorHDR : SCS_FinalColorLDR;
			Capture->bCaptureEveryFrame = false;
			Capture->bCaptureOnMovement = false;
			// Pin auto-exposure. A single-shot CaptureScene() never gives eye-adaptation a chance to
			// converge, so the default auto-exposure leaves one-off captures badly under/over-exposed.
			// Locking min == max brightness makes exposure a fixed factor (no adaptation transient), so the
			// capture is deterministic regardless of the scene's prior adaptation state.
			Capture->PostProcessSettings.bOverride_AutoExposureMinBrightness = true;
			Capture->PostProcessSettings.AutoExposureMinBrightness = 1.0f;
			Capture->PostProcessSettings.bOverride_AutoExposureMaxBrightness = true;
			Capture->PostProcessSettings.AutoExposureMaxBrightness = 1.0f;
			if (ShowOnlyActor)
			{
				Capture->PrimitiveRenderMode = ESceneCapturePrimitiveRenderMode::PRM_UseShowOnlyList;
				Capture->ShowOnlyActors.Add(ShowOnlyActor);
				// Include attached child actors (child-actor components, attach hierarchies — common for
				// composed Blueprints) so visually-integral parts are not silently omitted from the render.
				TArray<AActor*> AttachedActors;
				ShowOnlyActor->GetAttachedActors(AttachedActors, /*bResetArray*/ true, /*bRecursivelyIncludeAttachedActors*/ true);
				Capture->ShowOnlyActors.Append(AttachedActors);
			}
			// The capture component is the spawned actor's root (the actor was spawned at CaptureXform), so
			// its world transform already equals CaptureXform — no explicit SetWorldLocationAndRotation needed.
			Capture->CaptureScene();

			FTextureRenderTargetResource* Resource = RenderTarget->GameThread_GetRenderTargetResource();
			if (!Resource)
				return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("Render target resource was not available after capture."));

			TArray<FColor> Pixels;
			if (bComposite)
			{
				// SCS_SceneColorHDR stores inverse opacity in alpha (1 = empty/background visible, 0 = opaque
				// geometry), so compositing scene-over-background recovers the requested solid background:
				//   final = sceneColor + background * alpha   (premultiplied "over", done in linear space).
				TArray<FLinearColor> LinearPixels;
				if (!Resource->ReadLinearColorPixels(LinearPixels))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("Failed to read pixels from the capture render target."));
				const FLinearColor Bg = *BackgroundColor;
				Pixels.SetNumUninitialized(LinearPixels.Num());
				for (int32 Index = 0; Index < LinearPixels.Num(); ++Index)
				{
					const FLinearColor& Scene = LinearPixels[Index];
					const FLinearColor Composited(
						Scene.R + Bg.R * Scene.A,
						Scene.G + Bg.G * Scene.A,
						Scene.B + Bg.B * Scene.A,
						1.0f);
					Pixels[Index] = Composited.ToFColor(/*bSRGB*/ true);
				}
			}
			else
			{
				FReadSurfaceDataFlags ReadFlags(RCM_UNorm, CubeFace_MAX);
				ReadFlags.SetLinearToGamma(false);
				if (!Resource->ReadPixels(Pixels, ReadFlags))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("Failed to read pixels from the capture render target."));
			}

			FString Base64; int32 Bytes = 0; FString Error;
			if (!EncodePngBase64(Pixels, Width, Height, Base64, Bytes, Error))
				return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(Error);

			return MakeImageResult(Source, Width, Height, Base64, Bytes);
		}

		/**
		 * Parse a '#RRGGBB' / '#RRGGBBAA' (bare 6- or 8-digit also accepted) hex color. FColor::FromHex
		 * silently returns black for malformed input, so validate explicitly and surface a structured error
		 * instead — this also gives the headless specs another GPU-free branch. Only the two lengths the
		 * tool advertises are accepted (no 3-digit shorthand) so the contract matches the documentation.
		 */
		bool ParseHexColor(const FString& In, FLinearColor& OutColor, FString& OutError)
		{
			FString Hex = In;
			Hex.RemoveFromStart(TEXT("#"));
			if (Hex.Len() != 6 && Hex.Len() != 8)
			{
				OutError = FString::Printf(
					TEXT("Invalid 'background' hex color '%s'; expected '#RRGGBB' or '#RRGGBBAA'."), *In);
				return false;
			}
			for (const TCHAR Ch : Hex)
			{
				if (!FChar::IsHexDigit(Ch))
				{
					OutError = FString::Printf(
						TEXT("Invalid 'background' hex color '%s'; non-hex character found."), *In);
					return false;
				}
			}
			OutColor = FLinearColor(FColor::FromHex(Hex));
			return true;
		}

		/** Shared description tail documenting the size caps (so each tool advertises them, §10). */
		const TCHAR* SizeCapNote()
		{
			return TEXT(" Returns a base64 PNG as MCP image content. Optional 'width'/'height' are clamped to "
			            "[1, 2048] per side; the default is 1024. Requires a GPU-backed (windowed) editor.");
		}
	}

	// ---- Registration -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API void Register(FUnrealMcpToolRegistry& Registry)
	{
		// screenshot-viewport — active editor viewport.
		Registry.Tool(TEXT("screenshot-viewport"))
			.Title(TEXT("Screenshot Viewport"))
			.Description(FString(TEXT("Capture the active editor viewport. Note: while a Play-In-Editor session "
				"has viewport focus the 'active viewport' is the PIE game view; use screenshot-game-view to "
				"capture the game view explicitly.")) + SizeCapNote())
			.ParamInt(TEXT("width"), TEXT("Optional output width in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); when only 'height' is given the width is derived from the native aspect ratio, and the native viewport width is used when both are omitted."))
			.ParamInt(TEXT("height"), TEXT("Optional output height in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); when only 'width' is given the height is derived from the native aspect ratio, and the native viewport height is used when both are omitted."))
			.ReadOnlyHint(true)
			.Handle([](const FUnrealMcpToolCall& Call) -> FUnrealMcpToolResult
			{
				FString Error;
				if (!EnsureRenderingAvailable(Error))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(Error);

				FViewport* Viewport = GEditor ? GEditor->GetActiveViewport() : nullptr;
				if (!Viewport)
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("No active editor viewport. Focus a level editor viewport and retry."));

				return CaptureFromViewport(Call, Viewport, TEXT("editor viewport"));
			});

		// screenshot-game-view — PIE/game view; structured error when no PIE session is active.
		Registry.Tool(TEXT("screenshot-game-view"))
			.Title(TEXT("Screenshot Game View"))
			.Description(FString(TEXT("Capture the Play-In-Editor game view. Errors when no PIE session is active.")) + SizeCapNote())
			.ParamInt(TEXT("width"), TEXT("Optional output width in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); when only 'height' is given the width is derived from the native aspect ratio, and the native game-view width is used when both are omitted."))
			.ParamInt(TEXT("height"), TEXT("Optional output height in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); when only 'width' is given the height is derived from the native aspect ratio, and the native game-view height is used when both are omitted."))
			.ReadOnlyHint(true)
			.Handle([](const FUnrealMcpToolCall& Call) -> FUnrealMcpToolResult
			{
				// Validate the PIE precondition FIRST (GPU-free, headless-spec-covered).
				const bool bPlaySessionActive = GEditor && GEditor->PlayWorld != nullptr;
				FViewport* PieViewport = GEditor ? GEditor->GetPIEViewport() : nullptr;
				if (!bPlaySessionActive || !PieViewport)
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("No Play-In-Editor session is active. Start PIE before calling screenshot-game-view."));

				FString Error;
				if (!EnsureRenderingAvailable(Error))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(Error);

				return CaptureFromViewport(Call, PieViewport, TEXT("PIE game view"));
			});

		// screenshot-camera — render from a resolved camera actor via SceneCapture2D.
		Registry.Tool(TEXT("screenshot-camera"))
			.Title(TEXT("Screenshot Camera"))
			.Description(FString(TEXT("Render the scene from a chosen camera actor (resolved by label/name/path) and capture it.")) + SizeCapNote())
			.ParamString(TEXT("camera"), TEXT("Camera actor reference (label, object name, or path) to render from."), EUnrealMcpParamRequirement::Required)
			.ParamInt(TEXT("width"), TEXT("Optional output width in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); default 1024."))
			.ParamInt(TEXT("height"), TEXT("Optional output height in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); default 1024."))
			.ParamNumber(TEXT("fov"), TEXT("Optional horizontal field-of-view override in degrees (clamped to [5, 170]); defaults to the camera component's FOV (or 90)."))
			.ReadOnlyHint(true)
			.Handle([](const FUnrealMcpToolCall& Call) -> FUnrealMcpToolResult
			{
				// Validate arguments + resolve the camera FIRST (GPU-free, headless-spec-covered).
				if (!Call.Has(TEXT("camera")))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("'camera' is required."));

				UWorld* World = FUnrealMcpObjectRef::GetEditorWorld();
				if (!World)
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("No editor world is available."));

				const FString CameraRef = Call.GetString(TEXT("camera"));
				AActor* CameraActor = FUnrealMcpObjectRef::ResolveActor(CameraRef, World);
				if (!CameraActor)
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(FString::Printf(TEXT("No actor matched camera reference '%s'."), *CameraRef));

				UCameraComponent* CameraComponent = CameraActor->FindComponentByClass<UCameraComponent>();
				// Clamp once at parse time to a sane perspective range; a degenerate FOV (<= 0 or >= 180)
				// yields a NaN/garbage projection matrix rather than a usable render.
				const float Fov = FMath::Clamp(Call.Has(TEXT("fov"))
					? (float)Call.GetNumber(TEXT("fov"))
					: (CameraComponent ? CameraComponent->FieldOfView : 90.0f), 5.0f, 170.0f);
				const FTransform CaptureXform = CameraComponent
					? CameraComponent->GetComponentTransform()
					: CameraActor->GetActorTransform();

				FString Error;
				if (!EnsureRenderingAvailable(Error))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(Error);

				const int32 Width = ResolveCaptureDimension(Call.GetInt(TEXT("width"), 0));
				const int32 Height = ResolveCaptureDimension(Call.GetInt(TEXT("height"), 0));
				const FString Source = FString::Printf(TEXT("camera '%s'"), *CameraActor->GetActorNameOrLabel());
				return CaptureWithSceneCapture(World, CaptureXform, Fov, Width, Height, Source, nullptr, nullptr);
			});

		// screenshot-isolated — isolated actor render (transient SceneCapture2D + show-only list + background).
		Registry.Tool(TEXT("screenshot-isolated"))
			.Title(TEXT("Screenshot Isolated Actor"))
			.Description(FString(TEXT("Render a single actor in isolation against a neutral background, auto-framed by its bounds.")) + SizeCapNote())
			.ParamString(TEXT("actor"), TEXT("Target actor reference (label, object name, or path) to render in isolation."), EUnrealMcpParamRequirement::Required)
			.ParamInt(TEXT("width"), TEXT("Optional output width in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); default 1024."))
			.ParamInt(TEXT("height"), TEXT("Optional output height in pixels (clamped to [1, 2048]); default 1024."))
			.ParamString(TEXT("background"), TEXT("Optional background color as hex ('#RRGGBB' or '#RRGGBBAA'); the alpha of '#RRGGBBAA' is accepted but ignored (the PNG is always opaque). Defaults to dark grey."))
			.ParamNumber(TEXT("fov"), TEXT("Optional field-of-view override in degrees (clamped to [5, 170]); default 50."))
			.ReadOnlyHint(true)
			.Handle([](const FUnrealMcpToolCall& Call) -> FUnrealMcpToolResult
			{
				// Validate arguments + resolve the actor FIRST (GPU-free, headless-spec-covered).
				if (!Call.Has(TEXT("actor")))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("'actor' is required."));

				UWorld* World = FUnrealMcpObjectRef::GetEditorWorld();
				if (!World)
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT("No editor world is available."));

				const FString ActorRef = Call.GetString(TEXT("actor"));
				AActor* TargetActor = FUnrealMcpObjectRef::ResolveActor(ActorRef, World);
				if (!TargetActor)
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(FString::Printf(TEXT("No actor matched reference '%s'."), *ActorRef));

				// Parse + validate the background BEFORE the GPU guard so malformed hex is a GPU-free error branch.
				FLinearColor Background(0.05f, 0.05f, 0.05f, 1.0f);
				FString Error;
				if (Call.Has(TEXT("background")) && !ParseHexColor(Call.GetString(TEXT("background")), Background, Error))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(Error);

				if (!EnsureRenderingAvailable(Error))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(Error);

				// Auto-frame: place the capture along an isometric-ish offset so the actor's bounding sphere fits the FOV.
				// Clamp once here so the same value drives both the auto-framing distance below and the
				// capture's FOVAngle (an unclamped FOV would frame and render at different angles).
				const float Fov = FMath::Clamp(Call.Has(TEXT("fov")) ? (float)Call.GetNumber(TEXT("fov")) : 50.0f, 5.0f, 170.0f);
				const int32 Width = ResolveCaptureDimension(Call.GetInt(TEXT("width"), 0));
				const int32 Height = ResolveCaptureDimension(Call.GetInt(TEXT("height"), 0));
				FBox Bounds = TargetActor->GetComponentsBoundingBox(/*bNonColliding*/ true);
				FVector Center = Bounds.IsValid ? Bounds.GetCenter() : TargetActor->GetActorLocation();
				const float Radius = Bounds.IsValid ? FMath::Max(Bounds.GetExtent().Size(), 1.0f) : 100.0f;
				const float HalfFovRad = FMath::DegreesToRadians(Fov * 0.5f);
				// FOVAngle is the HORIZONTAL field of view, so for a wider-than-tall output the vertical FOV
				// shrinks by Height/Width (UE's scene-capture projection zooms the minor axis in). Pull the
				// camera back by Max(1, Width/Height) so a wide aspect frames the bounding sphere against the
				// (smaller) vertical FOV instead of clipping the actor off the top and bottom.
				const float AspectPullback = Height > 0 ? FMath::Max(1.0f, (float)Width / (float)Height) : 1.0f;
				const float Distance = (Radius / FMath::Max(FMath::Tan(HalfFovRad), KINDA_SMALL_NUMBER)) * 1.5f * AspectPullback;
				const FVector Offset = FVector(-1.0f, -1.0f, 0.6f).GetSafeNormal() * Distance;
				const FVector CamLocation = Center + Offset;
				const FRotator CamRotation = (Center - CamLocation).Rotation();
				const FTransform CaptureXform(CamRotation, CamLocation);

				const FString Source = FString::Printf(TEXT("isolated actor '%s'"), *TargetActor->GetActorNameOrLabel());
				return CaptureWithSceneCapture(World, CaptureXform, Fov, Width, Height, Source, &Background, TargetActor);
			});
	}
}

```

`UnrealMCP/Source/UnrealMcpEditor/Private/Tools/UnrealMcpSkillTools.cpp`:

```cpp
// Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
// See the LICENSE file in the repository root for more information.

#include "Tools/UnrealMcpSkillTools.h"

#include "UnrealMcpLog.h"
#include "UnrealMcpSchema.h"
#include "UnrealMcpToolRegistry.h"

#include "Dom/JsonObject.h"
#include "Dom/JsonValue.h"
#include "HAL/FileManager.h"
#include "Interfaces/IPluginManager.h"
#include "Misc/FileHelper.h"
#include "Misc/Paths.h"

namespace UnrealMcpSkillTools
{
	const TCHAR* const SkillCreateToolId = TEXT("unreal-skill-create");

	namespace
	{
		// Unity-build ODR rule: every helper below is namespace-private to this file's anonymous namespace,
		// but the module is unity-built, so the names must still be unique across the whole module. The
		// `Skills` prefix is this family's unique stem (see UnrealMCP/AGENTS.md "Unity-build ODR rule").

		/** The generated-file banner. Kept in one place so the specs and the generator cannot drift. */
		const TCHAR* const SkillsGeneratedBanner =
			TEXT("// GENERATED by the `unreal-skill-create` MCP system tool (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §2.4).\n")
			TEXT("// Hand-editing is fine — this file is ordinary plugin source and is never regenerated in place.\n")
			TEXT("// It self-registers through FUnrealMcpGeneratedSkillRegistrar, so NO other file needs editing;\n")
			TEXT("// deleting this file (and rebuilding) removes the tool.\n");

		/** The copyright one-liner every file in this repo starts with (conventions.md). */
		const TCHAR* const SkillsCopyrightHeader =
			TEXT("// Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.\n")
			TEXT("// See the LICENSE file in the repository root for more information.\n");

		/** The fluent builder call that declares one parameter of the given JSON type. */
		FString SkillsParamBuilderCall(const FSkillParamSpec& Param)
		{
			FString Method = TEXT("ParamString");
			if (Param.Type == TEXT("integer"))
				Method = TEXT("ParamInt");
			else if (Param.Type == TEXT("number"))
				Method = TEXT("ParamNumber");
			else if (Param.Type == TEXT("boolean"))
				Method = TEXT("ParamBool");

			FString Call = FString::Printf(TEXT("\t\t\t.%s(TEXT(\"%s\"), TEXT(\"%s\")"),
				*Method, *EscapeCppStringLiteral(Param.Name), *EscapeCppStringLiteral(Param.Description));
			if (Param.bRequired)
				Call += TEXT(", EUnrealMcpParamRequirement::Required");
			Call += TEXT(")\n");
			return Call;
		}

		/** Re-indent a caller-supplied handler body to the generated lambda's depth, preserving blank lines. */
		FString SkillsIndentBody(const FString& Body)
		{
			TArray<FString> Lines;
			// Normalize CRLF first so a Windows-authored body does not leave stray '\r' inside the file.
			FString Normalized = Body;
			Normalized.ReplaceInline(TEXT("\r\n"), TEXT("\n"));
			Normalized.ReplaceInline(TEXT("\r"), TEXT("\n"));
			Normalized.ParseIntoArray(Lines, TEXT("\n"), /*InCullEmpty*/ false);

			FString Out;
			for (const FString& Line : Lines)
			{
				if (Line.TrimStartAndEnd().IsEmpty())
					Out += TEXT("\n");
				else
					Out += FString::Printf(TEXT("\t\t\t\t%s\n"), *Line);
			}
			return Out;
		}

		/** The JSON Schema for the `params` array argument of `unreal-skill-create`. */
		TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> SkillsMakeParamsSchema()
		{
			TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Properties = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();
			Properties->SetObjectField(TEXT("name"), FUnrealMcpSchema::TypedSchema(
				TEXT("string"), TEXT("Parameter name (camelCase), e.g. 'targetName'.")));
			Properties->SetObjectField(TEXT("type"), FUnrealMcpSchema::TypedSchema(
				TEXT("string"), TEXT("JSON type: 'string' (default), 'integer', 'number' or 'boolean'.")));
			Properties->SetObjectField(TEXT("description"), FUnrealMcpSchema::TypedSchema(
				TEXT("string"), TEXT("What the parameter means; shown to the AI in the tool schema.")));
			Properties->SetObjectField(TEXT("required"), FUnrealMcpSchema::TypedSchema(
				TEXT("boolean"), TEXT("Whether the parameter is required. Default false.")));

			TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Items = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();
			Items->SetStringField(TEXT("type"), TEXT("object"));
			Items->SetObjectField(TEXT("properties"), Properties);
			TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>> ItemRequired;
			ItemRequired.Add(MakeShared<FJsonValueString>(TEXT("name")));
			Items->SetArrayField(TEXT("required"), ItemRequired);

			TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Schema = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();
			Schema->SetStringField(TEXT("type"), TEXT("array"));
			Schema->SetStringField(TEXT("description"),
				TEXT("Declared parameters of the new tool. Each entry is { name, type?, description?, required? }."));
			Schema->SetObjectField(TEXT("items"), Items);
			return Schema;
		}

		/** Read the `params` argument into typed specs. Returns false + a reason on a malformed entry. */
		bool SkillsParseParams(const FUnrealMcpToolCall& Call, TArray<FSkillParamSpec>& OutParams, FString& OutError)
		{
			const TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>>* Array = nullptr;
			if (!Call.Arguments->TryGetArrayField(TEXT("params"), Array) || Array == nullptr)
				return true; // absent is fine — a parameterless tool

			for (const TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>& Value : *Array)
			{
				const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject>* Obj = nullptr;
				if (!Value.IsValid() || !Value->TryGetObject(Obj) || Obj == nullptr || !Obj->IsValid())
				{
					OutError = TEXT("Every 'params' entry must be an object like { \"name\": \"x\", \"type\": \"string\" }.");
					return false;
				}

				FSkillParamSpec Spec;
				(*Obj)->TryGetStringField(TEXT("name"), Spec.Name);
				FString Type;
				if ((*Obj)->TryGetStringField(TEXT("type"), Type) && !Type.IsEmpty())
					Spec.Type = Type.ToLower();
				(*Obj)->TryGetStringField(TEXT("description"), Spec.Description);
				bool bRequired = false;
				if ((*Obj)->TryGetBoolField(TEXT("required"), bRequired))
					Spec.bRequired = bRequired;
				OutParams.Add(MoveTemp(Spec));
			}
			return true;
		}
	}

	// --- Pure helpers ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

	FString EscapeCppStringLiteral(const FString& In)
	{
		FString Out = In;
		Out.ReplaceInline(TEXT("\\"), TEXT("\\\\"));
		Out.ReplaceInline(TEXT("\""), TEXT("\\\""));
		Out.ReplaceInline(TEXT("\r\n"), TEXT("\\n"));
		Out.ReplaceInline(TEXT("\r"), TEXT("\\n"));
		Out.ReplaceInline(TEXT("\n"), TEXT("\\n"));
		Out.ReplaceInline(TEXT("\t"), TEXT("\\t"));
		return Out;
	}

	bool IsSupportedSkillParamType(const FString& Type)
	{
		return Type == TEXT("string") || Type == TEXT("integer") || Type == TEXT("number") || Type == TEXT("boolean");
	}

	FString SkillSymbolFromToolId(const FString& ToolId)
	{
		FString Symbol;
		bool bUpperNext = true;
		for (const TCHAR Ch : ToolId)
		{
			if (Ch == TEXT('-'))
			{
				bUpperNext = true;
				continue;
			}
			Symbol.AppendChar(bUpperNext ? FChar::ToUpper(Ch) : Ch);
			bUpperNext = false;
		}
		return Symbol;
	}

	FString DefaultTitleFromToolId(const FString& ToolId)
	{
		TArray<FString> Words;
		ToolId.ParseIntoArray(Words, TEXT("-"), /*InCullEmpty*/ true);
		FString Title;
		for (const FString& Word : Words)
		{
			if (!Title.IsEmpty())
				Title += TEXT(" ");
			Title += Word.Left(1).ToUpper() + Word.RightChop(1);
		}
		return Title;
	}

	FString SkillFileNameFromToolId(const FString& ToolId)
	{
		return FString::Printf(TEXT("UnrealMcpSkill_%s.cpp"), *SkillSymbolFromToolId(ToolId));
	}

	bool ValidateSkillSpec(const FSkillSpec& Spec, FString& OutError)
	{
		// Reuse the registry's OWN kebab-case predicate rather than re-deriving it: a name this rejects would
		// be dropped at registration time anyway, and having two patterns is how they drift apart.
		if (!FUnrealMcpToolRegistry::IsValidToolName(Spec.ToolId))
		{
			OutError = FString::Printf(
				TEXT("'%s' is not a valid tool id. Use kebab-case: lowercase letters/digits with single internal hyphens, e.g. 'my-skill'."),
				*Spec.ToolId);
			return false;
		}
		if (Spec.Description.TrimStartAndEnd().IsEmpty())
		{
			OutError = TEXT("'description' is required — it is what the AI reads to decide whether to call the tool.");
			return false;
		}
		if (Spec.Body.TrimStartAndEnd().IsEmpty())
		{
			OutError = TEXT("'body' is required — the C++ statements of the handler, ending in a `return FUnrealMcpToolResult::...;`.");
			return false;
		}

		TSet<FString> SeenNames;
		for (const FSkillParamSpec& Param : Spec.Params)
		{
			if (Param.Name.IsEmpty())
			{
				OutError = TEXT("Every declared parameter needs a non-empty 'name'.");
				return false;
			}
			// The name is embedded in a TEXT("...") literal AND used as a JSON Schema property key; keep it to a
			// plain identifier so neither the generated C++ nor the schema can be broken by an exotic name.
			for (const TCHAR Ch : Param.Name)
			{
				if (!FChar::IsAlnum(Ch) && Ch != TEXT('_'))
				{
					OutError = FString::Printf(
						TEXT("Parameter name '%s' must contain only letters, digits and underscores."), *Param.Name);
					return false;
				}
			}
			if (FChar::IsDigit(Param.Name[0]))
			{
				OutError = FString::Printf(TEXT("Parameter name '%s' must not start with a digit."), *Param.Name);
				return false;
			}
			if (!IsSupportedSkillParamType(Param.Type))
			{
				OutError = FString::Printf(
					TEXT("Parameter '%s' has unsupported type '%s'. Use string, integer, number or boolean."),
					*Param.Name, *Param.Type);
				return false;
			}
			bool bAlreadySeen = false;
			SeenNames.Add(Param.Name, &bAlreadySeen);
			if (bAlreadySeen)
			{
				OutError = FString::Printf(TEXT("Duplicate parameter name '%s'."), *Param.Name);
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}

	FString BuildSkillSourceCode(const FSkillSpec& Spec)
	{
		const FString Symbol = SkillSymbolFromToolId(Spec.ToolId);
		const FString Title = Spec.Title.IsEmpty() ? DefaultTitleFromToolId(Spec.ToolId) : Spec.Title;

		FString Out;
		Out += SkillsCopyrightHeader;
		Out += TEXT("\n");
		Out += SkillsGeneratedBanner;
		Out += TEXT("\n");
		Out += TEXT("#include \"Tools/UnrealMcpGeneratedSkills.h\"\n");
		Out += TEXT("#include \"UnrealMcpToolRegistry.h\"\n");
		Out += TEXT("\n");
		// A tool-id-derived namespace keeps every generated symbol unique in the unity build (UnrealMCP/AGENTS.md ODR rule).
		Out += FString::Printf(TEXT("namespace UnrealMcpGeneratedSkill_%s\n{\n"), *Symbol);
		Out += TEXT("\tstatic void Register(FUnrealMcpToolRegistry& Registry)\n\t{\n");
		Out += FString::Printf(TEXT("\t\tRegistry.Tool(TEXT(\"%s\"))\n"), *EscapeCppStringLiteral(Spec.ToolId));
		Out += FString::Printf(TEXT("\t\t\t.Title(TEXT(\"%s\"))\n"), *EscapeCppStringLiteral(Title));
		Out += FString::Printf(TEXT("\t\t\t.Description(TEXT(\"%s\"))\n"), *EscapeCppStringLiteral(Spec.Description));
		if (!Spec.SkillDescription.IsEmpty())
		{
			Out += FString::Printf(TEXT("\t\t\t.SkillDescription(TEXT(\"%s\"))\n"),
				*EscapeCppStringLiteral(Spec.SkillDescription));
		}
		for (const FSkillParamSpec& Param : Spec.Params)
			Out += SkillsParamBuilderCall(Param);
		if (Spec.bReadOnlyHint)
			Out += TEXT("\t\t\t.ReadOnlyHint(true)\n");
		if (Spec.bDestructiveHint)
			Out += TEXT("\t\t\t.DestructiveHint(true)\n");
		if (Spec.bIdempotentHint)
			Out += TEXT("\t\t\t.IdempotentHint(true)\n");
		Out += TEXT("\t\t\t.Handle([](const FUnrealMcpToolCall& Call) -> FUnrealMcpToolResult\n\t\t\t{\n");
		Out += TEXT("\t\t\t\t// Runs ON the game thread (the dispatcher guarantees it, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §4).\n");
		Out += TEXT("\t\t\t\t// Read arguments with Call.GetString/GetInt/GetNumber/GetBool/GetVector.\n");
		Out += SkillsIndentBody(Spec.Body);
		Out += TEXT("\t\t\t});\n");
		Out += TEXT("\t}\n\n");
		Out += TEXT("\tstatic const FUnrealMcpGeneratedSkillRegistrar Registrar(&Register);\n");
		Out += TEXT("}\n");
		return Out;
	}

	FString GetGeneratedSkillsDir()
	{
		const TSharedPtr<IPlugin> Plugin = IPluginManager::Get().FindPlugin(TEXT("UnrealMCP"));
		if (!Plugin.IsValid())
			return FString();

		// The editor module's Private/Tools folder is the anchor: if THAT is missing, this install carries no
		// C++ source (a precompiled / Fab install), and writing a .cpp anywhere would be writing into a folder
		// no build will ever compile.
		const FString ToolsDir = FPaths::ConvertRelativePathToFull(
			Plugin->GetBaseDir() / TEXT("Source") / TEXT("UnrealMcpEditor") / TEXT("Private") / TEXT("Tools"));
		if (!FPaths::DirectoryExists(ToolsDir))
			return FString();

		return ToolsDir / TEXT("Skills");
	}

	// --- Registration ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

	void Register(FUnrealMcpToolRegistry& Registry)
	{
		FUnrealMcpToolRegistry* RegistryPtr = &Registry;

		Registry.Tool(SkillCreateToolId)
			.Title(TEXT("Skill (Tool) / Create"))
			.Description(TEXT(
				"Create a new skill (MCP tool) for the Unreal Editor by generating a C++ source file into the "
				"UnrealMCP plugin's editor module. Unlike Unity (which hot-compiles a new .cs on domain reload), "
				"Unreal C++ needs a BUILD: the file is written and self-registers, but the tool is NOT callable "
				"until the editor is rebuilt (Live Coding, or close the editor and rebuild the project). The "
				"result always says so explicitly.\n"
				"\n"
				"'toolId' is the kebab-case id the AI will call ('my-skill'). 'body' is the C++ statements of the "
				"handler; it runs ON the game thread and must end with a `return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Success(...)` "
				"or `::Error(...)`. Read arguments through the `Call` object: Call.GetString(TEXT(\"name\")), "
				"Call.GetInt, Call.GetNumber, Call.GetBool, Call.GetVector, Call.Has. Build structured output with "
				"`TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Structured = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();` and pass it as the second "
				"argument of Success().\n"
				"\n"
				"Sample body:\n"
				"  const FString Name = Call.GetString(TEXT(\"name\"));\n"
				"  if (Name.IsEmpty())\n"
				"    return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT(\"'name' is required.\"));\n"
				"  TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Structured = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();\n"
				"  Structured->SetStringField(TEXT(\"echo\"), Name);\n"
				"  return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Success(Name, Structured);\n"
				"\n"
				"Only the plugin's own editor module is written to — never a game module, because a game module "
				"that depends on UnrealMcpRuntime overrides a consumer's TargetDenyList and drags the plugin into "
				"packaged builds. A precompiled (marketplace) install has no C++ source on disk and is refused."))
			.SkillDescription(TEXT(
				"Create a new skill (MCP tool) for the Unreal Editor by generating a self-registering C++ file into "
				"the UnrealMCP plugin's editor module. The tool becomes callable only after the editor is REBUILT "
				"(Live Coding or a project rebuild) — the result reports that explicitly."))
			.ParamString(TEXT("toolId"), TEXT("Kebab-case tool id the AI will call, e.g. 'my-skill'."), EUnrealMcpParamRequirement::Required)
			.ParamString(TEXT("description"), TEXT("Full tool description shown to the AI."), EUnrealMcpParamRequirement::Required)
			.ParamString(TEXT("body"), TEXT("C++ statements of the handler body; must return a FUnrealMcpToolResult."), EUnrealMcpParamRequirement::Required)
			.ParamString(TEXT("title"), TEXT("Human label. Defaults to a Title-Cased form of 'toolId'."))
			.ParamString(TEXT("skillDescription"), TEXT("Optional SHORT description for the generated SKILL.md front-matter."))
			.Param(TEXT("params"), TEXT("array"), TEXT("Declared parameters."), EUnrealMcpParamRequirement::Optional, SkillsMakeParamsSchema())
			.ParamBool(TEXT("readOnlyHint"), TEXT("Mark the new tool read-only (it does not modify state). Default false."))
			.ParamBool(TEXT("destructiveHint"), TEXT("Mark the new tool destructive. Default false."))
			.ParamBool(TEXT("idempotentHint"), TEXT("Mark the new tool idempotent. Default false."))
			.ParamBool(TEXT("force"), TEXT("Overwrite an existing generated file for the same tool id. Default false."))
			// SYSTEM surface (§2.4), matching Unity's unity-skill-create: skill AUTHORING is host plumbing driven
			// by the CLI / desktop app, not a capability an arbitrary AI agent should find in tools/list.
			.ToolType(EUnrealMcpToolType::System)
			.Handle([RegistryPtr](const FUnrealMcpToolCall& Call) -> FUnrealMcpToolResult
			{
				FSkillSpec Spec;
				Spec.ToolId = Call.GetString(TEXT("toolId")).TrimStartAndEnd();
				Spec.Title = Call.GetString(TEXT("title")).TrimStartAndEnd();
				Spec.Description = Call.GetString(TEXT("description"));
				Spec.SkillDescription = Call.GetString(TEXT("skillDescription"));
				Spec.Body = Call.GetString(TEXT("body"));
				Spec.bReadOnlyHint = Call.GetBool(TEXT("readOnlyHint"), false);
				Spec.bDestructiveHint = Call.GetBool(TEXT("destructiveHint"), false);
				Spec.bIdempotentHint = Call.GetBool(TEXT("idempotentHint"), false);

				FString Error;
				if (!SkillsParseParams(Call, Spec.Params, Error))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(Error);
				if (!ValidateSkillSpec(Spec, Error))
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(Error);

				// Refuse up front: a live collision reported here is far clearer than one surfaced only as a
				// warning at the NEXT boot, when the generated skill's extension scope rejects it first-wins
				// ("extensions may not shadow core") and the tool silently never appears.
				if (RegistryPtr != nullptr && RegistryPtr->HasTool(Spec.ToolId))
				{
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(FString::Printf(
						TEXT("A tool named '%s' is already registered. Pick a different 'toolId'."), *Spec.ToolId));
				}

				const FString SkillsDir = GetGeneratedSkillsDir();
				if (SkillsDir.IsEmpty())
				{
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(TEXT(
						"This Unreal-MCP install has no C++ source on disk (a precompiled / marketplace install), so a "
						"generated skill could never be compiled. Install the plugin from source to author skills."));
				}

				const FString FileName = SkillFileNameFromToolId(Spec.ToolId);
				const FString FullPath = SkillsDir / FileName;
				const bool bExists = FPaths::FileExists(FullPath);
				if (bExists && !Call.GetBool(TEXT("force"), false))
				{
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(FString::Printf(
						TEXT("'%s' already exists. Pass 'force':true to overwrite it."), *FileName));
				}

				if (!IFileManager::Get().DirectoryExists(*SkillsDir)
					&& !IFileManager::Get().MakeDirectory(*SkillsDir, /*Tree*/ true))
				{
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(FString::Printf(
						TEXT("Failed to create the generated-skills folder '%s'."), *SkillsDir));
				}

				const FString Source = BuildSkillSourceCode(Spec);
				if (!FFileHelper::SaveStringToFile(Source, *FullPath, FFileHelper::EEncodingOptions::ForceUTF8WithoutBOM))
				{
					return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Error(FString::Printf(
						TEXT("Failed to write '%s'."), *FullPath));
				}

				UE_LOG(LogUnrealMcp, Log, TEXT("[Unreal-MCP] generated skill '%s' -> %s (rebuild required)."),
					*Spec.ToolId, *FullPath);

				TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Structured = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();
				Structured->SetStringField(TEXT("toolId"), Spec.ToolId);
				Structured->SetStringField(TEXT("file"), FullPath);
				Structured->SetStringField(TEXT("module"), TEXT("UnrealMcpEditor"));
				Structured->SetStringField(TEXT("symbol"), SkillSymbolFromToolId(Spec.ToolId));
				Structured->SetBoolField(TEXT("overwritten"), bExists);
				// The load-bearing field: NEVER report the tool as live. It exists in source only.
				Structured->SetBoolField(TEXT("rebuildRequired"), true);
				Structured->SetBoolField(TEXT("callable"), false);
				Structured->SetStringField(TEXT("nextStep"), TEXT(
					"Rebuild the editor to load the new tool: trigger Live Coding (Ctrl+Alt+F11) or close the editor "
					"and rebuild the project. Until then the tool is NOT registered and calling it will fail."));

				return FUnrealMcpToolResult::Success(FString::Printf(
					TEXT("%s '%s' as %s. REBUILD REQUIRED: the tool exists in C++ source but is NOT callable yet — "
					     "trigger Live Coding or rebuild the editor, then it registers itself automatically."),
					bExists ? TEXT("Regenerated") : TEXT("Generated"), *Spec.ToolId, *FileName),
					Structured);
			});
	}
}
```

`UnrealMCP/Source/UnrealMcpEditor/Private/Tools/UnrealMcpSkillTools.h`:

```h
// Copyright (c) 2026 Ivan Murzak. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
// See the LICENSE file in the repository root for more information.

#pragma once

#include "CoreMinimal.h"

class FUnrealMcpToolRegistry;

/**
 * The SKILL-authoring tool family (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §2.4) — Unreal's answer to Unity's
 * `unity-skill-create`. Registers ONE SYSTEM tool:
 *
 *   - `unreal-skill-create` — generate a new MCP tool as a C++ source file inside the plugin's editor
 *     module and report, honestly and explicitly, that the editor must be REBUILT before the new tool
 *     can be called.
 *
 * (Its sibling `unreal-skill-generate` — regenerate every `SKILL.md` from the registered tool set — is
 * NOT here: SKILL.md generation was deliberately moved sidecar-side in #101, and a C++ tool handler may
 * not synchronously wait on bridge state (§4 / §11 risk 2), so a C++-homed generate tool could only
 * fire-and-forget and misreport completion. It is a bridge-native system tool instead — see
 * `bridge/src/Tools/SkillGenerateTool.cs`.)
 *
 * WHY C++ AND NOT C# (owner ruling 2026-07-25, option (b)). Unity's `skill-create` writes a `.cs` that
 * Unity hot-compiles on domain reload; Unreal has no such path. Emitting C# into the .NET sidecar was
 * evaluated and rejected: `bridge/src` has no Roslyn and no AssemblyLoadContext, and the sidecar ships
 * as a PREBUILT single-file binary an end user cannot recompile. So the generator emits C++ and says so.
 * Auto-triggering Live Coding is deliberately NOT attempted here (a later layer, once the generator is
 * proven) — the tool tells the caller what to do rather than pretending the tool is live.
 *
 * WHY THE PLUGIN'S EDITOR MODULE, not the host project. A generated skill must see the tool registry
 * (`UnrealMcpToolRegistry.h`) and its `UNREALMCPRUNTIME_API` symbols. Putting it in a GAME module means
 * that module takes a hard dependency on `UnrealMcpRuntime`, which — per the plugin's own README/
 * AGENTS.md — OVERRIDES a consumer's `TargetDenyList` and drags Unreal-MCP into packaged game builds.
 * The editor module already depends on the runtime module, is stripped from Game targets by Type, and is
 * rebuilt by the very same UBT invocation the user runs anyway.
 *
 * The generator + validator are pure and exported here so the Automation specs assert the exact emitted
 * text without a live editor or a real compile.
 */
namespace UnrealMcpSkillTools
{
	/** The generated skill's tool id — kept as a named constant so the specs and the docs cannot drift. */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API extern const TCHAR* const SkillCreateToolId;

	/** One declared parameter of a generated skill (mirrors FUnrealMcpParamSpec's declarable subset). */
	struct UNREALMCPEDITOR_API FSkillParamSpec
	{
		FString Name;                 // camelCase parameter name
		FString Type = TEXT("string");// "string" | "integer" | "number" | "boolean"
		FString Description;
		bool bRequired = false;
	};

	/** Everything the generator needs to emit one skill file. Plain data — no engine state. */
	struct UNREALMCPEDITOR_API FSkillSpec
	{
		FString ToolId;               // kebab-case, e.g. "my-skill"
		FString Title;                // human label; defaults to a Title-Cased ToolId when empty
		FString Description;          // the full tool description (becomes the SKILL.md body)
		FString SkillDescription;     // optional SHORT description for the SKILL.md front-matter
		TArray<FSkillParamSpec> Params;
		FString Body;                 // the C++ statements of the handler body (must return a FUnrealMcpToolResult)
		bool bReadOnlyHint = false;
		bool bDestructiveHint = false;
		bool bIdempotentHint = false;
	};

	/** True iff @p Type is one of the four scalar JSON types the generator can declare. */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API bool IsSupportedSkillParamType(const FString& Type);

	/**
	 * Validate @p Spec for generation. Checks the kebab-case tool id (the registry's own pattern), a
	 * non-empty description + body, unique camelCase-ish parameter names, and supported param types.
	 * Returns false with a caller-facing reason in @p OutError on the FIRST problem.
	 */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API bool ValidateSkillSpec(const FSkillSpec& Spec, FString& OutError);

	/** "my-skill" -> "MySkill". The unity-build-safe unique symbol stem for a generated file. */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API FString SkillSymbolFromToolId(const FString& ToolId);

	/** "my-skill" -> "My Skill". The default Title when the caller supplied none. */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API FString DefaultTitleFromToolId(const FString& ToolId);

	/** The generated file's name for @p ToolId, e.g. "UnrealMcpSkill_MySkill.cpp". */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API FString SkillFileNameFromToolId(const FString& ToolId);

	/**
	 * Emit the complete, compilable C++ translation unit for @p Spec. PURE + deterministic (no disk, no
	 * engine state) so a spec can assert the exact text. The caller must have validated the spec first —
	 * every embedded string is escaped, but an invalid tool id would still produce a file the registry
	 * rejects at runtime.
	 */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API FString BuildSkillSourceCode(const FSkillSpec& Spec);

	/** Escape @p In for embedding inside a C++ TEXT("...") literal (backslash, quote, CR/LF, tab). */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API FString EscapeCppStringLiteral(const FString& In);

	/**
	 * Absolute directory generated skills are written into:
	 * `<UnrealMCP plugin>/Source/UnrealMcpEditor/Private/Tools/Skills`. Returns an EMPTY string when the
	 * plugin's C++ source is not on disk (a precompiled / Fab install), which is the honest "cannot
	 * generate here" signal the tool surfaces instead of writing into a folder nothing will compile.
	 */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API FString GetGeneratedSkillsDir();

	/** Register the skill family into @p Registry (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §3.3). */
	UNREALMCPEDITOR_API void Register(FUnrealMcpToolRegistry& Registry);
}
```
