`docs/rql.md`:

```md
# RQL in Unreal-MCP

The editor's data layer is RQL (Reflection Query Language, [IvanMurzak/RQL](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/RQL)): one
query language instead of one tool per operation, as in Unity-MCP 1.0. Agents find actors, components and assets, read
members, filter, aggregate, and change them in one call:

```
actors | where Label contains "Enemy" | select $ref Label Location
actors | get Components | where $ is PointLightComponent | set Intensity = Intensity * 2
editor | call SpawnActor("PointLight", "Lamp", "(0, 0, 300)")
```

## Design

RQL's contract is the QueryPlan, not the text (RQL ADR-0002), and the C++ runtime has no text parser by design
(ADR-0003: "the sidecar parses text with the .NET parser and ships the plan over IPC; the C++ executor validates and
executes plans"). Unreal-MCP follows that split exactly:

```
agent ──query text──▶ unreal-mcp-bridge (sidecar, .NET)          UnrealMCP plugin (C++, game thread)
                      Rql.Parser: text → canonical QueryPlan ──IPC tool-call {query, plan}──▶ rql::Engine.execute(plan)
                      AgentFormat: QueryResult → compact rows ◀──IPC tool-response: QueryResult JSON── over live UObjects
```

- **Sidecar** (`bridge/src/Tools/RqlBridge.cs`, NuGet `com.IvanMurzak.Rql` 0.3.0-dev.2877579 — a temporary pre-release
  packed from RQL main 2877579 and committed under `bridge/prerelease-packages/` until the cascade release): for `rql-query` / `rql-mutate` it
  parses `query` with `RqlParser` and adds `PlanCodec.Serialize(plan)` as the `plan` argument (a syntax error is
  answered without a round trip). The plugin answers with the QueryResult JSON; the sidecar renders it with
  `AgentFormat.Render(…, Table)` — byte-for-byte the agent output of Unity-MCP's rql tools. `rql-schema` answers with
  schema JSON the sidecar renders in RQL's compact schema lines.
- **Plugin** (module `UnrealMcpRql`, `UnrealMCP/Source/UnrealMcpRql/`): the vendored RQL C++ runtime
  (`Source/ThirdParty/RQL/`, unmodified) plus the **Unreal provider** the RQL roadmap describes ("`UClass`/`FProperty`,
  `TArray`/`TMap` adapters, `IsValid` liveness"), built on the runtime's provider seam (`TypeDescriptor` /
  `IListAdapter` / `IMapAdapter`) without changing RQL.
- **Why a separate module**: the runtime reports failures with C++ exceptions internally (its public API is
  `noexcept`), so the module sets `bEnableExceptions`; it is RTTI-free, so UE's `/GR-` / `-fno-rtti` is fine. Exceptions
  never cross a UE frame: UFUNCTIONs report failures through `UnrealMcpRql::Fail`, and RQL types never appear in a
  public header. The vendored sources keep file-local helpers, so the module builds without unity and without PCH;
  each `Private/Vendor/UnrealMcpRqlVendor_<file>.cpp` compiles one RQL source between `THIRD_PARTY_INCLUDES_START/END`.
- **License**: RQL is PolyForm Shield 1.0.0 (same owner; RQL ADR-0007). Its `LICENSE.md` ships next to the vendored
  sources and in the sidecar package; `UnrealMCP/ThirdPartyNotices.txt` lists both.

### The Unreal provider (`UnrealMcpRqlTypes`)

- **Types** are built at runtime from reflection, keyed by the `UClass` / `UScriptStruct` / `UEnum` pointer, and filled
  on first use (a query touches a few of the thousands of classes). Class names are the reflected names (`PointLight`,
  `StaticMeshComponent`, `BP_Enemy_C`, structs `Vector`, enums `EComponentMobility`); `rql-schema` accepts the C++
  spellings too (`APointLight`, `FVector`).
- **Members**: class properties that are EditAnywhere / VisibleAnywhere / BlueprintVisible (writable unless `EditConst`
  or BlueprintReadOnly-only; a Blueprint actor's variable that is not Instance Editable is read-only on placed actors,
  since `AActor::ResetPropertiesForConstruction` resets it to the class default on every construction script run), every struct property, `TArray` / `TSet` / `TMap` as lists and maps, object references
  (instanced sub-objects are owning, others references), soft references as paths. Writes go through the editor's
  `PreEditChange` / `PostEditChangeProperty`, as an edit in the Details panel does (components refresh, Blueprint
  actors rerun their construction script).
- **Blueprint actors' components**: an edit of a placed Blueprint actor's component reruns its construction script,
  which rebuilds the construction-script components; the next writes of the same mutation and the receipt follow the
  rebuilt component. A relative-transform write also updates the component's world transform (some components, e.g.
  Niagara, do not re-register on edit).
- **Computed members** (core module): every object `Id`, `Name`, `Path`; Actor `Label`, `Location`, `Rotation`,
  `Scale`, `Components`, `Children`, `Parent` (writable: attach / detach; a refused attach names the reason, e.g. a Static
  actor under a Movable parent), `Folder`, `Layers` (writable through the Layers subsystem, as the Layers panel
  does: missing layers are created, the actor ends up in exactly the listed ones; refused in World Partition levels, which use data layers),
  `Level`, `HiddenInEditor`, `Selected` (writable: adds to / removes from the
  editor selection; neither it nor `HiddenInEditor` marks the level unsaved); Volume `BrushExtent` (local half-size of its
  brush, null without one; writable: rebuilds it as a box, undoable) and `BrushBounds` (world box); component `Owner` (and `Name`: a Blueprint's
  component templates read under their variable name, without the `_GEN_VARIABLE` suffix); Level `Map`, `Package`, `IsPersistent`, `IsCurrent` (writable), `IsVisible` (writable: the Levels panel's eye), `Actors`; World
  `Map`, `Levels`, `PersistentLevel`, `CurrentLevel`; MaterialInterface `Scalars` / `Vectors` / `Textures` (parameter
  maps, writable on material instances).
- **Methods** (`call`): Actor `Destroy()`, `Duplicate(Offset)`, `AddComponent(ClassName, Name)`; component
  `Destroy()`; every parameterless `CallInEditor` function (the Details panel's buttons); every UFUNCTION of an API class (the `editor` operations, extension
  operations). Parameters and results convert like members; UHT's recorded C++ defaults become RQL defaults.
- **Identity**: `$ref` is `Type#<Id>`, the `Id` of the object's slot in the object array plus that slot's serial number
  (editor-session ids, like Unity's instance ids); `ref(…)` resolves them directly, and a ref to a destroyed object never
  resolves to a new object that reuses the slot. Every object value carries a weak pointer, so destroyed (garbage)
  objects read as null and are never dereferenced.
- **References from text**: an object parameter or member accepts what an edit field accepts — an asset path, a class
  name or path for class references, an actor label / name / path for actors (`FUnrealMcpObjectRef::ResolveReference`,
  the same class resolver as `blueprint-*`). An asset reference that resolves to nothing suggests up to three asset paths
  of that class with a matching name (`no StaticMesh 'Cube' (did you mean /Engine/BasicShapes/Cube, ...?)`).
- **Math structs** (`Vector`, `Vector2D`, `Vector4`, `Rotator`, `Quat`, `LinearColor`, `Color`, `IntPoint`,
  `IntVector`) have RQL type adapters: they print as `(x, y, z)` and accept `"(1, 2, 3)"`, `[1, 2, 3]`, `{X: 1, …}`
  (an object literal builds a new value: members it does not name are zero); colors also `"#ff8800"`. They compare
  with those forms too (`where Location == "(0, 0, 100)"`, components within 1e-5).
- **UE's text form for any other struct**: a string in the form the editor's Copy / `ExportText` writes is imported with
  `UScriptStruct::ImportText` (RQL's `MutationPolicy::coerce_text`), so `set Slot.LayoutData.Anchors =
  "(Minimum=(X=0.5,Y=0),Maximum=(X=0.5,Y=0))"` works on structs without an adapter; text that does not import (an
  unknown member, trailing text) fails with `coercion-failed` and UE's message.
- **Gameplay tags** read and write as text: `FGameplayTag` as `"Ability.Fire"` (`""` = none), `FGameplayTagContainer`
  as `["Ability.Fire", "State.Stunned"]` (or `"A.B, C.D"`), validated against the registered tags (an unknown tag fails
  and names similar ones); containers are rebuilt with `AddTag`, so their parent-tag cache stays right. Members:
  `Tag.Parent`, `Tags.Names`, `Tags.Num`; `==` compares with text / lists (containers as sets). `FGameplayTagQuery`
  shows its `Description` and is read-only.
- **Soft paths** (`FSoftObjectPath`, `FSoftClassPath`: `GameDefaultMap`, classes to spawn) read and write as text
  (`"/Game/Maps/Arena.Arena"`, `""` = none, or an object); they compare with the path or its package
  (`where GameDefaultMap == "/Game/Maps/Arena"`); members `Path`, `Package`.
- **Struct members are known before a value is read**: a struct type's members are filled when a member of that type is
  added (and when an object literal constructs it), so `where Row.Damage > 3` and `set Row = {Damage: 5}` work on a
  struct the session never read.
- **Per-call session**: each tool call builds a fresh engine and type cache (cheap: descriptors fill lazily). A
  Blueprint compile, hot reload or user-defined struct edit recreates `FProperty` / `UFunction` objects, so no
  descriptor may outlive the call that built it.
- **Mutations** run in one editor transaction (one Ctrl+Z step, named `RQL: <query>` in the Undo History, so `TRANSACTION UNDO`
  says which change it reverts; `python-execute` steps are named after the snippet's first statement); owners are `Modify()`d before the first write and
  their packages marked dirty after. The receipt's `new` column is the value read back after the write (what the
  setter and the class's `PostEditChangeProperty` left); `rql-mutate` refuses a query without `set` / `call`, and a
  throwing operation is `call-threw`. Unlike Unity-MCP, `rql-mutate` does **not** save to disk: Unreal edits stay
  unsaved until `editor | call SaveAll()` / `SaveLevel()` / `SaveAsset(…)` (saving in Unreal can raise source-control
  checkouts and Save-As dialogs, which an unattended tool call must not).
- **Batch checks** (RQL's `MutationPolicy::validate_batch`): every planned change of a `set` / `call` stage is checked at
  once before anything runs, dry runs included, and a refusal is `invalid-value` with nothing changed: class default
  objects are read-only (except settings objects and API objects), a settings write must hit a config property, and one
  object reached twice by the same `call` (`actors | get Parent | call Destroy()` over siblings) is refused (`| distinct`
  first) — a call cannot be rolled back, so running it twice would break all-or-nothing. Hints never advise
  `budgets.*` (the tools take no budgets), a `ref("Name")` hint names `unreal.find("…")`, a hint that sends the
  caller to the type list names `rql-schema` (`Engine::schema_hint`), and a `set` / `call` sent to `rql-query` is
  `permission-denied` with a hint naming `rql-mutate` (`Engine::mutate_hint`).
- **Target limit**: `rql-mutate` changes at most 200 targets per call by default (a mutation is one undo step whatever its
  size, RQL spec §8); its `max_targets` argument raises the limit for one call up to the ceiling of 1000
  (`MutationPolicy::limit_argument`, mapped to `Budgets::max_mutation_targets`; passed only when the caller gives it, and
  a value outside 1 … 1000, 0 included, is refused with `invalid-value` before anything runs). Over the limit nothing changes and
  `mutation-limit` names the match count (or "more than 1000") and, while the limit is below 1000, `max_targets`;
  at the ceiling it suggests `first N` / `skip N` batches.
- **Typos in mutations**: when no item reaches `set` / `call` because a member read (`where` / `get`) missed on every
  item and no type declares the name, the `unknown-member` warning is an error (`ok=false`, nothing changed). Streams
  are polymorphic (`actors | get Components`), so the session's `Engine::is_known_member` accepts the exposed property
  names of every loaded class and struct (user-defined struct fields by authored name) and the members hooks add:
  `get Components | where Intensity > 0 | set Intensity = …` over actors without lights stays a no-match (ok, 0
  changes) while `get RootComponnt | set …` fails. A `set` that reaches targets lacking the member is still an
  `unknown-member` error: filter first (`where $ is LightComponentBase`).
- **Receipts** of a `set` list only the assignments that change a value: one whose planned and read-back values equal
  the old value is left out and counted in the result's `unchanged` (the sidecar prints "(N unchanged assignment(s) not
  listed)"); outside a dry run the write still runs and the commit hooks see every record, and a write the editor
  refused or clamped back to the old value stays listed.
- **Conditions** (`where`, `and` / `or` / `not`, `?:`, list predicates) must be booleans: `where StaticMesh` is a
  `type-mismatch` whose hint suggests `StaticMesh != null` or `has(StaticMesh)`; null still counts as false.
  Lists compare by value (`group-by Tags` merges equal tag lists), and group-by rows have `items` for per-group
  aggregates (`group-by $type | select key, avg = items.avg(Intensity)`). A float property used as a number reads as its
  shortest decimal (`Intensity` 4.2f is 4.2, so arithmetic, sums and averages print clean); comparisons keep float precision.
- **Blueprint classes** are named `BP_Door_C` (`$type`); `is BP_Door` matches them too (the asset name, a
  `TypeDescriptor::also_is` alias, inherited by child Blueprints).
- **Enums** read as entry names and accept the entry name, the editor's display name (`UMETA(DisplayName)`, RQL enum
  aliases; one that spells another entry's name is skipped), `Type::Name` or the number.
- **Function sources**: RQL text lets a host function start a query (`unreal.assets("Material") | …`, also with a member
  path after it: `unreal.asset("/Game/BP_Door").EventGraph | …`); the C++ runtime runs a bare function call but not
  the member-path form, so the session evaluates such a call (literal arguments) once and runs the query on a source
  holding its value.

### Sources and functions (core module)

| Source / function | What |
|---|---|
| `actors` | every actor of the editor world's loaded levels |
| `levels`, `world` | the loaded levels, the editor world |
| `selection` | the selected actors (`editor | set Selection = [...]` writes it) |
| `editor` | editor state (`IsPlaying`, `IsPaused` — writable, `Selection`, `World`, `CurrentLevel`; the transaction buffer: `NextUndo`, `NextRedo`, `UndoHistory`, `RedoHistory` — titles, next first — `UndoCount`, `RedoCount`) and operations: `SpawnActor` (a class, Blueprint name or path, or an asset to place: a StaticMesh path gives a StaticMeshActor; a volume class gets the editor's 200 cm box brush, sized with `Scale`; label, location, rotation, parent and scale are optional), `SpawnActorFromAsset` (an asset path only, placed as drag and drop does), `OpenLevel`, `NewLevel`, `SaveLevel`, `SaveAll`, `AddSublevel` (a saved map as a streaming sublevel; not undoable, the current level stays; refused in World Partition worlds), `UnloadSublevel` (a level by its map name), `CreateAsset`, `CopyAsset`, `MoveAsset`, `DeleteAsset`, `CreateFolder`, `RefreshAssets`, `CreateMaterialInstance`, `ImportAsset` (returns every asset the import created: the mesh, then its materials, textures, skeleton), `SaveAsset`, `ClearConsole` |
| `console` | editor log entries (`Sequence`, `Time`, `Verbosity`, `Category`, `Message`) |
| `unreal.find(label)` | an actor by label, name or path |
| `unreal.asset(path)`, `unreal.assets(class, path?)` | one asset; assets of a class (at most 200, loaded as read; without a path: `/Game`, or in rql-query every content root (engine, plugins) when the project has none of the class) |
| `unreal.classes(base?, filter?)` | classes deriving from a base |
| `dataTables` | the project's DataTables (see [DataTables](#datatables)) |
| `gameplayTags` | every registered gameplay tag: `Name`, `Comment`, `Source` (ini), `Parent`, `Children`, `Explicit`, `Restricted` |
| `settings`, `unreal.settings(section)` | Project Settings / Editor Preferences sections and their objects (see [Settings](#settings)) |
| `blueprints` | the project's Blueprints (see [Blueprint graphs](#blueprint-graphs)) |
| `widgetBlueprints` | the project's Widget Blueprints (see [Widget Blueprints](#widget-blueprints)) |
| `levelSequences` | the project's Level Sequences (see [Level Sequences](#level-sequences)) |

**Bulk create.** A source-qualified call runs one `editor` operation per stream item:
`range(0, 300) | call editor.SpawnActor("/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube", "Cube_" + $, [($ % 20) * 150, floor($ / 20) * 150, 50])`
(with `max_targets: 300`), `[["Lamp_A", 0], ["Lamp_B", 400]] | call editor.SpawnActor("PointLight", $[0], [$[1], 0, 300])`, or by parameter name: `range(0, 10) | call editor.SpawnActor({ClassName: "PointLight", Label: "Lamp_" + $, Location: [$ * 300, 0, 300]})`.
Every spawn counts against the target limit, every class / asset name is resolved before the first spawn (a call
validator on `SpawnActor` / `SpawnActorFromAsset`, dry runs too), all spawns are one undo step (the mutation's one
editor transaction), and the receipt has one row per actor carrying its `$ref`.

**Vector arithmetic.** `FVector`, `FVector2D`, `FVector4`, `FLinearColor` and `FRotator` opt in to RQL's component-wise
arithmetic (their adapters' `components` / `from_components`): `set Scale = Scale * 1.5`, `Location + [0, 0, 100]`,
`Location - Other.Location`. A rotator's is per axis (`Rotation + [0, 90, 0]` adds 90 to Yaw), as the Details panel edits
it, not a composed rotation; that is what editor nudges want. `FQuat`, `FTransform`, `FColor` and the integer points
stay out (`type-mismatch`).

**No UObjects from literals.** The session's `can_construct_from_literal` hook refuses every UObject type, so `{}` or
`{Name: ...}` written to an object parameter or member is `coercion-failed` ("an engine object") and nothing is
constructed, on dry runs and while RQL tries overloads. (Unreal marks liveness through the engine-wide `is_alive` hook,
not a per-type adapter, so RQL's own engine-object default would not cover it.)

The `editor` operations also include `CreateDataTable(path, rowStruct)` and, for gameplay tags,
`AddGameplayTag(name, comment?, source?)`, `RemoveGameplayTag(name)`, `RenameGameplayTag(name, newName)` (written to
the tag ini at once through the GameplayTagsEditor plugin, not undoable; a rename leaves a redirector).

### DataTables

`UDataTable::RowMap` is not a `UPROPERTY`, so reflection does not see a table's rows. The core module adds:

- `Rows`: a map from row name (case-insensitive) to the row struct. `set Rows["Sword"].Damage = 12` writes the row in
  place; `set Rows["Bow"] = {Damage: 7}` adds a row (a failing write removes it again); `get Rows | where Value.Damage > 10
  | select Key` streams the rows as entries, and `get Rows | where Value.Damage > 10 | set Value.Damage = Value.Damage * 2`
  writes through the table (each entry is the key-path write `Rows["<row>"].Damage`; the receipt names the table).
- `RowNames`, `RowCount`, `RowStructName` (pass it to `rql-schema` for the row members).
- `call AddRow(name, values?)`, `RemoveRow(name)`, `RenameRow(name, newName)`, `DuplicateRow(name, newName)`: the
  `FDataTableEditorUtils` functions the DataTable editor's buttons call (row names are validated; values that do not fit
  leave no half-made row).

Row writes run in the mutation's transaction (the table is `Modify()`d first, so Ctrl+Z restores the rows), call
`HandleDataTableChanged` and notify open DataTable editors. Composite tables and `UCurveTable` are not covered.

### Settings

`settings` lists the sections of the Project Settings ("Project") and Editor Preferences ("Editor") windows (`Container`,
`Category`, `Section`, `DisplayName`, `Description`) with `Object`, the object the section edits; `unreal.settings(name)`
returns that object by section name, display name or class name (the auto-discovered `UDeveloperSettings` sections
such as Physics, Rendering and Collision are registered first, as the settings window does; UE 5.6+) (`unreal.settings("Maps & Modes") | set GameDefaultMap =
"/Game/Maps/Arena"`). Settings objects are class defaults, read-only elsewhere in RQL; here their **config** properties
are writable (a non-config property is refused: it would be lost on restart) and each mutation is saved the way the
settings editor saves it: one property into `Default<Config>.ini` for project (default-config) classes, the whole section
otherwise; legacy input mappings rebuild their key maps. Config files are not part of the editor transaction: a settings
write is saved at once and Ctrl+Z does not revert it. Source control is not checked out (read-only ini files are made
writable).

### Blueprint graphs

- `UBlueprint`: `Components` (the component templates its Simple Construction Script adds, under their variable names:
  their reflected defaults are writable — `unreal.asset("/Game/BP_Coin").Components | where Name == "Mesh" | set
  StaticMesh = "/Engine/BasicShapes/Sphere"` — and placed actors whose component still holds the old value follow, as
  after an edit in the Components panel; components inherited from a native class or a parent Blueprint are not listed), `Graphs` (event graphs,
  functions, macros), `EventGraph`, `Status` (`UpToDate`, `Dirty`, `Error`, …);
  `call Compile()` returns `{Succeeded, Errors, Warnings, Messages: [{Severity, Message, Node}]}` (a failed compile is a
  result, not an error; `Node` is the node's `$ref`) and `call AddFunction(name)` adds a function graph.
- `UEdGraph`: `Nodes`, `Kind` (`EventGraph`, `Function`, `Macro`, `Delegate`), `Blueprint`; node calls (each returns the
  node; `X` / `Y` place it, default: the editor's next free spot): `AddCallFunction("PrintString" |
  "KismetMathLibrary.Add_IntInt" | a function of the Blueprint; UE 4 float names such as `Add_FloatFloat` find the double
  functions)`, `AddVariableGet(name)`, `AddVariableSet(name)` (another class's variable as `"BP_Player.Score"`: the node
  takes the object on its Target pin), `AddInputKey("SpaceBar")` (a key event: `Pressed` / `Released`),
  `AddEvent("BeginPlay")` (overridable events of the parent class; enables the editor's placeholder node when there is
  one), `AddCustomEvent(name)`, `AddCast(class)`, `AddNode("Branch" | "Sequence" | "Self" | a standard macro such as
  "ForLoop", "ForEachLoop", "DoOnce", "Gate")`.
- `UEdGraphNode`: `Title`, `X`, `Y`, `Comment`, `Enabled` (writable), `Error` (the last compile's message), `Graph`,
  `Pins`; calls `Connect(pin, target, targetPin)`, `Disconnect(…)`, `BreakLinks(pin?)`, `SetPinDefault(pin, value)`,
  `Destroy()`. Pins are named by pin name or display name; `exec` / `out` name the execution pins.
- `EdGraphPin` (a host object, not a UObject: it holds its node and pin id): `Name`, `DisplayName`, `Direction`, `Type`
  (as the editor names it), `IsExec`, `DefaultValue` (writable: text, numbers, bools, `"(1, 2, 3)"`, an asset path for
  object pins), `LinkedTo`, `Node`; calls `Connect(otherPin)`, `Disconnect(otherPin)`, `BreakLinks()`.

Connections go through the K2 schema (`CanCreateConnection` / `TryCreateConnection`, the checks of a drag between pins),
defaults through `IsPinDefaultValid` / `TrySetDefaultValue`. Every change is undoable (one transaction per mutation) and
marks the Blueprint modified; nothing compiles until `call Compile()` (which runs outside the transaction). The
`blueprint-*` tools stay for variables, components, class defaults and spawning.

### Widget Blueprints

A Widget Blueprint's widgets live in its `WidgetTree`, which reflection does not expose; the widgets are UObjects whose
properties (and `Slot`, the widget's layout in its panel: `set Slot.LayoutData.Offsets.Left = 24`) are reflected as usual.

- `UBaseWidgetBlueprint`: `RootWidget`, `Widgets` (every widget of the tree), `call AddWidget(class, name?, parent?)` (into
  a panel, or as the root of an empty tree), and the Blueprint members (`Compile`, `Status`, `Graphs` …).
- `UWidget`: `Parent`, `WidgetBlueprint`, `IsVariable` (writable: the Designer's Is Variable box; text blocks, images
  and panels start unticked, and a graph reads a widget with `AddVariableGet(name)` only once it is ticked), `call AddChild(class, name?)` (panels), `call Destroy()` (with its children);
  `UPanelWidget`: `Children` (so `RootWidget | recurse Children` walks the tree).

New widgets are registered with the Blueprint (a variable only while `IsVariable` is true) and removed ones leave the tree, as the Designer does; structure
changes mark the Blueprint structurally modified and property edits mark it modified (compile to apply them). The
widgets of a Widget Blueprint are templates of its generated class but its design data: writable here, unlike other
class defaults.

### User-defined structs

A user-defined struct (the struct asset a DataTable row or a Blueprint variable uses when the project has no C++ struct)
keeps its fields in the Struct editor's data, which reflection does not expose. `UUserDefinedStruct` gets `Fields`
(`[{Name, Type, Default}]`) and `call AddField(name, type, default?)`, `RemoveField(name)` (a struct keeps at least one
field), `RenameField(name, newName)`, `SetFieldDefault(name, value)`, through `FStructureEditorUtils`: the struct recompiles
and the DataTables and Blueprints using it update, as after an edit in the Struct editor. Types are the tokens of
`blueprint-add-variable` (`UnrealMcpPinTypes`: `bool`, `int`, `float`, `string`, `vector`, a struct such as
`GameplayTag`, a class such as `StaticMesh`). `editor | call CreateAsset(path, "UserDefinedStruct")` makes one (with the
editor's initial `MemberVar_0` field), `CreateDataTable(path, structPath)` a table of it.

### Level Sequences

Frames are at the sequence's display rate (what the Sequencer shows), converted to and from its tick resolution.

- `ULevelSequence`: `DisplayRate`, `Start`, `End` (playback range, writable), `Bindings`, `Tracks` (tracks not bound to an
  object); `call AddActor(actor)` (a possessable binding, like dragging the actor into the Sequencer) and
  `call AddTrack(class)`.
- `SequenceBinding` (a host object: the sequence and the binding's GUID): `Name`, `Guid`, `Kind` (`Possessable` /
  `Spawnable`), `Class`, `Tracks`; `call AddTrack("Transform" | "Visibility" | a track class | a property)` — every new track gets a
  section over the playback range. A property (`"Intensity"`, `"LightColor"`, `"LightComponent0.Intensity"`: an animatable
  — `Interp` — property of the bound actor or of one of its components) gets the property track of its type (float, double,
  bool, color, vector) bound to it, on the component's binding when the property is a component's (made as the
  Sequencer makes it); its single channel is named after the property (`AddKey("Intensity", 60, 5000)`). A bare property
  track class (`MovieSceneFloatTrack`) is refused, since it would animate nothing; `Visibility` keys the actor's
  `bHidden` (a component's `bHiddenInGame`), as the Sequencer's Visibility track does; its channel is `Visible` (true =
  visible).
- `UMovieSceneTrack`: `Sections`, `DisplayName`, `call AddSection()`; `UMovieSceneSection`: `Start`, `End` (writable),
  `Channels` (`[{Name, Type, Keys: [{Frame, Value}]}]`, names as the Sequencer shows them: `Location.X`, `Rotation.Yaw`),
  `call AddKey(channel, frame, value)` (the channel by that name, or by its internal name: `Rotation.Z` is the yaw) (double / float / bool channels; a key outside the section grows it).

Every change is undoable (one transaction per mutation). Spawnables are listed but not created.

## Tools

| Before | Now |
|---|---|
| `actor-find`, `actor-component-get`, `object-get-data`, `level-get-data` | `rql-query` on `actors`, `… | get Components`, `ref("Type#id")`, `unreal.asset(path)`, `levels | get Actors` |
| `actor-modify`, `actor-component-modify`, `object-modify` | `rql-mutate` `set` (transform members, any reflected property, struct paths `Location.Z`) |
| `actor-create`, `actor-destroy`, `actor-duplicate`, `actor-set-parent` | `editor | call SpawnActor(...)`, `call Destroy()`, `call Duplicate(offset)`, `set Parent = ref(...)` |
| `actor-component-add`, `actor-component-destroy`, `actor-component-list-all` | `call AddComponent(class, name)`, `… | get Components | where $ is X | call Destroy()`, `unreal.classes("ActorComponent")` |
| `asset-find`, `asset-get-data` | `unreal.assets("Material", "/Game/...")`, `unreal.asset(path)` |
| `asset-copy` / `-move` / `-delete` / `-create-folder` / `-refresh` / `-import` | `editor | call CopyAsset / MoveAsset / DeleteAsset / CreateFolder / RefreshAssets / ImportAsset` (and `CreateAsset(path, class)` for any asset class) |
| `asset-material-create`, `-modify`, `-get-data` | `editor | call CreateMaterialInstance(path, parent)`, `Scalars["…"]`, `Vectors["…"]`, `Textures["…"]` |
| `level-create` / `-open` / `-save` / `-set-current` / `-unload-sublevel` / `-list-loaded` | `editor | call NewLevel / OpenLevel / SaveLevel / AddSublevel / UnloadSublevel`, `levels` (`set IsCurrent = true`, `set IsVisible = false`) |
| `editor-application-get-state` / `-set-state` | `editor` `IsPlaying`, `IsPaused` (writable) |
| `editor-selection-get` / `-set` | `selection`, `editor | set Selection = [...]` |
| `console-get-logs` / `console-clear-logs` | `console` source (`where Verbosity == "Error"`, `Sequence > N`), `editor | call ClearConsole()` |
| `reflection-method-find` / `-call` | `rql-schema(type)` (members and methods), `call` on `CallInEditor` functions and the exposed operations |

Kept as tools: `blueprint-*` (Blueprint authoring is Unreal's script surface, like Unity-MCP's `script-*`),
`source-*`, `screenshot-*`, `console-run-command`, `python-execute` (code, not data access), and the system tools `ping`, `unreal-skill-create`,
`unreal-skill-generate`. The runtime (packaged game) surface is unchanged: `ping` only.

`reflection-method-call` could invoke any BlueprintCallable function; RQL `call` is an allowlist (as in Unity-MCP):
`CallInEditor` functions, the operations above and those extensions add.

**Tool data layer.** Unity-MCP also routes every other tool's arguments and results through RQL (McpPlugin
`IToolBinding`). That binding hooks C# `[AiTool]` methods; Unreal's tools are C++ tools proxied from the plugin's
manifest (`ProxyTool`, plain JSON-schema parameters), so there is nothing for it to bind and no `ToolFormat` setting —
the kept tools take simple arguments already.

**Descriptor.** The plugin marks its tools in the manifest: `"rql": "query" | "mutate" | "schema"` tells the sidecar
to parse `query` into `plan` (query / mutate) and to render the answer, and rql-query ships the `unreal-rql` skill (the
guide, the live sources and functions, the guides of installed RQL modules) as `"skills": [{name, description,
markdown}]`. `unreal-skill-generate` writes every shipped skill as `<name>/SKILL.md`; skills never reach `tools/list`.
The skill's name, description and body live in the plugin (`UnrealMcpRqlGuide.h`, the session's skill markdown).
The rql-query and rql-mutate descriptions and the skill append RQL's shared language rules (`rql::language_rules()`,
`rql/guide.hpp`), so rules every host states alike (conditions, `?:`, list equality, group items, receipts, `call`,
bulk create, vectors, missing map keys) come from RQL and are not copied into the Unreal guide.

## Extensions

An extension contributes an `IUnrealMcpRqlModule` (`UnrealMCP/Source/UnrealMcpRql/Public/IUnrealMcpRqlModule.h`),
registered as a modular feature. The editor's extension manager runs a module pass in the same rebuild as tool
providers: the Extensions window lists the module's extension (`GetExtensionId`, `GetExtensionVersion`), disabling it
there leaves the module out, and a module coming or going re-registers the rql-* tools (their skill) before the one
manifest push.
Reflection already exposes every type the extension's engine plugin defines, so a module adds what reflection does not:

- sources: `AddObjectSource(name, description, UClass*, getter)`, `AddObjectListSource(name, description, UClass*,
  getter)`, `AddAssetSource(name, description, UClass*)`, `AddClassDefaultsSource(name, description, UClass* base)` —
  the class types the source in `rql-schema`;
- operations: `AddApiSource(name, description, UClass*, "TypeName")` (or `AddApiClass` alone) — every UFUNCTION of the
  class becomes callable (declare them `UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, meta = (BlueprintInternalUseOnly = "true"))` so
  UHT records default arguments; the doc comment is the description; failures via `UnrealMcpRql::Failed<T>`; object
  parameters are required unless their C++ default is `nullptr`);
- members: `ExposeProperties` (properties reflection hides), `AddJsonMember`, `AddObjectMember`, `AddObjectListMember`;
- `AddGuide(topic, markdown)`, rendered into the `unreal-rql` skill.

`IMPLEMENT_MODULE(TUnrealMcpRqlEditorModule<FMyRqlModule>, MyModule)` registers the module for the editor module's
lifetime; `UnrealMcpRql::SpawnActor` / `AddComponent` / `CreateAsset` / `EditorWorld` / `PluginVersion` share the core
operations' rules (docs/EXTENSIONS.md).

## Tests

- `UnrealMcpRqlAdaptersSpec.cpp` (`UnrealMcp.Tools.Rql.Adapters`): every existing adapter on a fixture object with one
  property of each kind (`UnrealMcpRqlSpecFixtures.h`): the nine math structs (text, lists, literals, equality, errors),
  references, arrays / sets / maps, scalars and enums (ranges, rollback, undo), asset and class-defaults lists, the
  console, material parameter maps, the seven class hooks and every registration of the extension seam.
- `UnrealMcpRqlDataModelsSpec.cpp` (`UnrealMcp.Tools.Rql.DataModels`): DataTable rows (edit, add / rename / duplicate /
  remove, validation, undo, save and reload), user-defined struct fields, gameplay tags (tag ini edits, text conversion,
  parent tags and their comments, rows with tags), Blueprint component defaults and Instance Editable variables,
  settings (sections, ini writes, refusals, dry run), Blueprint graphs (nodes, pins, defaults, connections, compile
  errors, undo), Widget Blueprints (tree, properties, slots, removal, compile, undo) and Level Sequences (bindings,
  tracks, sections, keys, ranges, undo).
- `UnrealMCP/Source/UnrealMcpEditorTests/Private/UnrealMcpRqlSpec.cpp` (`UnrealMcp.Tools.Rql`): the tools, queries,
  mutations (set, dry run, read-only, permission), components, calls (spawn, add component, duplicate, destroy), refs,
  selection, levels, console, assets, schema. The C++ runtime has no parser, so each case carries the plan Rql.Parser
  produces for its query (in the comment above it).
- `bridge/tests/RqlBridgeTests.cs`: plans, result and schema rendering, the descriptor fields, the proxy wiring, the
  shipped skill file.
- `UnrealMcpExtensionsSpec.cpp` (`UnrealMcp.Extensions`): the module pass (records, disabled set, enabled ids).
- The connection smoke (`scripts/connection_smoke.py`) and the chain battery call `rql-schema` over MCP.

A local Mac run: build a host project with the plugin (`RunUBT.sh <Host>Editor Mac Development -project=…`), then
`UnrealEditor-Cmd <host>.uproject -nullrhi -unattended -ExecCmds="Automation RunTests UnrealMcp.Tools.Rql; Quit"`.

`extensions/AGENTS.md`:

```md
# extensions/

- Each `UnrealAI<Feature>/` is an optional UE plugin: its own `.uplugin`, module, `extension.json`, tests and license.
- Each contributes an RQL module (`IUnrealMcpRqlModule`, docs/rql.md), not MCP tools: sources, an operations class
  (`Private/UnrealAI<Feature>RqlApi.*`, UFUNCTIONs), computed members and a guide; the plugin README lists them (`extension.json` `tools` stays empty).
- `migration-sources.json` records the original public repo and exact imported commit; preserve provenance.
- New first-party plugins go here, never as nested git submodules. Keep IDs/plugin names stable.
- Source handlers/specs live under each plugin's `Source/`; live checks under `Tests/e2e/tools/`.
- Version source: `.uplugin` `VersionName`; bump with `scripts/extension_release.py bump --plugin ... --version ...`.
- Independent tags/ZIPs and the online index: `docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md`.
- Add test expectations to `tests/automation-inventory.json`; never lower them merely to pass a run.

```

`extensions/README.md`:

```md
# Optional Unreal MCP plugins

Each folder is a separately installable UE plugin with an independent source-ZIP release.
Each is an RQL module ([`docs/rql.md`](../docs/rql.md)): it adds sources, operations, members and a guide to the
editor's `rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema` tools instead of tools of its own. All depend on the UnrealMCP core
`UnrealMcpRql` module; none requires a sibling extension.

| Plugin | Engine subsystem |
| --- | --- |
| UnrealAINiagara | Niagara VFX |
| UnrealAIEnhancedInput | Enhanced Input |
| UnrealAIPCG | Procedural Content Generation |
| UnrealAIGAS | Gameplay Abilities |
| UnrealAILandscape | Landscape / Water |
| UnrealAIControlRig | Control Rig |

Version and dependency metadata live in each `extension.json`; the RQL module itself (sources, operations, members) is listed by `rql-schema` and each README.
See [the monorepo guide](../docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md) for the shared test runner, independent
release workflow, online index and migration compatibility. Original commits/licenses are preserved
in `migration-sources.json` and each plugin's `LICENSE`.

```

`extensions/UnrealAIControlRig/README.md`:

```md
# ControlRig RQL module

RQL module for Unreal's Control Rig: query Control Rig blueprints (element hierarchy, controls, bones) and Control Rig components.

An optional editor plugin in the [Unreal MCP monorepository](../../README.md), with its own module, version and release archive.

## Requirements

- Unreal Engine 5.7 or later (the shared extension suite verifies UE 5.7 and 5.8).
- Unreal MCP 1.0.0 or later (the RQL data layer), installed in the same project.
- Engine plugins: `ControlRig`. The installer enables these dependencies.
- A C++ toolchain for your Unreal Engine installation. Extension releases contain source files and must be compiled for your project and engine.

## Install

With the Unreal Editor closed:

```sh
npm install -g unreal-mcp-cli
unreal-mcp-cli install-plugin "<UEProject>"
unreal-mcp-cli install-extension com.ivanmurzak.unreal-ai-control-rig "<UEProject>"
```

Replace `<UEProject>` with the project directory. The installer selects this extension's latest indexed version independently of the core and other extensions. Use `--version X.Y.Z` to select a published historical version, or `--build` to compile after installation. Otherwise rebuild the project before opening the editor.

The plugin is installed under `Plugins/UnrealAIControlRig/`. Connect Unreal MCP to your AI client to use the RQL module below.

## RQL module

The extension adds its feature to the editor's RQL data layer (`rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema`, [docs/rql.md](../../docs/rql.md)) instead of separate tools; its guide is part of the `unreal-rql` skill.

| Kind | Names |
| --- | --- |
| Sources | `controlRigs` |
| Members | `ControlRigBlueprint.Elements`, `ControlRigBlueprint.Hierarchy`, `ControlRigBlueprint.Controls`, `ControlRigBlueprint.Bones`, `ControlRigComponent.BoundRig` (the running rig) |

```
controlRigs | select Name Elements
controlRigs | where Name == "CR_Mannequin" | select Controls Bones
actors | get Components | where $ is ControlRigComponent | select Owner.Label BoundRig
```

## Releases and development

Each extension has its own versioned source ZIP in [Unreal MCP Releases](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Unreal-MCP/releases). The shared release index records the latest version, historical releases and archive checksums; unchanged extensions are not copied into other component releases.

See the [monorepository and test guide](../../docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md) for independent publication, isolated compilation and the combined one-editor test suite. See [extension development](../../docs/EXTENSIONS.md) for the RQL module API.

Licensed under [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

```

`extensions/UnrealAIControlRig/Source/UnrealAIControlRig/Private/Tests/UnrealAIControlRigSpec.cpp`:

```cpp
// Copyright (c) 2026 IvanMurzak/Unreal-AI-ControlRig. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
// See the LICENSE file in the repository root for more information.

#if WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS

#include "CoreMinimal.h"
#include "Misc/AutomationTest.h"
#include "Dom/JsonObject.h"

#include "IUnrealMcpRqlModule.h"
#include "UnrealMcpRqlTools.h"

// ============================================================================================
//  UE Automation spec for the extension's RQL module (Unreal-MCP docs/rql.md "Extensions").
//
//  The spec discovers THIS extension's live module through IModularFeatures (the path Unreal-MCP uses) and runs RQL
//  QueryPlans through the editor's RQL engine (UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan). The C++ runtime has no text parser, so
//  each plan is the one Rql.Parser produces for the query in the comment above it.
//
//  Run via:  Automation RunTests UnrealAIControlRig
// ============================================================================================

BEGIN_DEFINE_SPEC(FUnrealAIControlRigSpec, "UnrealAIControlRig",
	EAutomationTestFlags::EditorContext | EAutomationTestFlags::ProductFilter)
END_DEFINE_SPEC(FUnrealAIControlRigSpec)

void FUnrealAIControlRigSpec::Define()
{
	Describe("RQL module", [this]()
	{
		It("registers this extension's RQL module as a modular feature", [this]()
		{
			IUnrealMcpRqlModule* Module = UnrealMcpRqlTools::FindModule(TEXT("com.ivanmurzak.unreal-ai-control-rig"));
			if (TestNotNull(TEXT("RQL module is registered"), Module))
			{
				TestEqual(TEXT("module name"), Module->GetRqlModuleName(), FString(TEXT("ControlRig")));
				TestFalse(TEXT("version reported"), Module->GetExtensionVersion().IsEmpty());
			}
		});

		It("adds its sources and guide to the unreal-rql skill", [this]()
		{
			const FString Skill = UnrealMcpRqlTools::SkillMarkdown();
			TestTrue(TEXT("| `controlRigs` |"), Skill.Contains(TEXT("| `controlRigs` |")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("## Control Rig"), Skill.Contains(TEXT("## Control Rig")));
		});
	});

	Describe("source: controlRigs", [this]()
	{
		It("answers a query (count of the project's Control Rig blueprints)", [this]()
		{
			// controlRigs | count
			TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Result;
			const bool bResultOk = UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["controlRigs"]},"stages":[{"op":"count"}]})RQL"), false, &Result);
			TestTrue(TEXT("a well-formed result"), Result.IsValid());
			TestTrue(TEXT("succeeds"), bResultOk);
		});

		It("reads the hierarchy members of every rig", [this]()
		{
			// controlRigs | select Name Elements Controls Bones
			TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Result;
			const bool bResultOk = UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["controlRigs"]},"stages":[{"op":"select","fields":[{"name":"Name","expr":{"path":["Name"]}},{"name":"Elements","expr":{"path":["Elements"]}},{"name":"Controls","expr":{"path":["Controls"]}},{"name":"Bones","expr":{"path":["Bones"]}}]}]})RQL"), false, &Result);
			TestTrue(TEXT("a well-formed result"), Result.IsValid());
			TestTrue(TEXT("succeeds"), bResultOk);
		});
	});

	Describe("members", [this]()
	{
		It("describes ControlRigBlueprint with its hierarchy members", [this]()
		{
			bool bOk = false;
			const FString Schema = UnrealMcpRqlTools::Schema(TEXT("ControlRigBlueprint"), bOk);
			TestTrue(TEXT("schema ok"), bOk);
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists name:Elements"), Schema.Contains(TEXT("\"name\":\"Elements\"")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists name:Hierarchy"), Schema.Contains(TEXT("\"name\":\"Hierarchy\"")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists name:Controls"), Schema.Contains(TEXT("\"name\":\"Controls\"")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists name:Bones"), Schema.Contains(TEXT("\"name\":\"Bones\"")));
		});

		It("describes ControlRigComponent with its BoundRig member", [this]()
		{
			bool bOk = false;
			const FString Schema = UnrealMcpRqlTools::Schema(TEXT("ControlRigComponent"), bOk);
			TestTrue(TEXT("schema ok"), bOk);
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists name:BoundRig"), Schema.Contains(TEXT("\"name\":\"BoundRig\"")));
		});
	});
}

#endif // WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS

`extensions/UnrealAIControlRig/Source/UnrealAIControlRig/Private/UnrealAIControlRigModule.cpp`:

```cpp
// Copyright (c) 2026 IvanMurzak/Unreal-AI-ControlRig. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
// See the LICENSE file in the repository root for more information.

#include "Modules/ModuleManager.h"
#include "Dom/JsonObject.h"
#include "Dom/JsonValue.h"

#include "IUnrealMcpRqlModule.h"

#include "ControlRig.h"
#include "ControlRigBlueprintLegacy.h"          // UControlRigBlueprint (ControlRigDeveloper) — authoring asset + GetHierarchy()
#include "ControlRigComponent.h"                 // UControlRigComponent (ControlRig)
#include "Rigs/RigHierarchy.h"                   // URigHierarchy + element-key getters
#include "Rigs/RigHierarchyDefines.h"            // FRigElementKey / ERigElementType / ERigControlType
#include "Rigs/RigHierarchyElements.h"           // FRigBaseElement / FRigControlElement / FRigControlSettings

namespace UnrealAIControlRigRqlLocal
{
	template <typename TEnum>
	FString EnumName(TEnum Value)
	{
		const UEnum* Enum = StaticEnum<TEnum>();
		return Enum ? Enum->GetNameStringByValue(static_cast<int64>(Value)) : FString(TEXT("Unknown"));
	}

	URigHierarchy* HierarchyOf(UObject* Object)
	{
		UControlRigBlueprint* Blueprint = Cast<UControlRigBlueprint>(Object);
		return Blueprint ? Blueprint->GetHierarchy() : nullptr;
	}
}

/**
 * The extension's RQL module (Unreal-MCP docs/rql.md "Extensions"): Control Rig is queried with rql-query instead of
 * dedicated tools. Reflection exposes the Control Rig blueprint and component properties; the module adds the
 * `controlRigs` asset source, a rig blueprint's element hierarchy (controls, bones, element counts — not reflected
 * properties), a component's bound rig, and the agent guide rendered into the unreal-rql skill.
 *
 * The version is the .uplugin VersionName.
 */
class FUnrealAIControlRigRqlModule : public IUnrealMcpRqlModule
{
public:
	virtual FString GetRqlModuleName() const override { return TEXT("ControlRig"); }
	virtual FString GetExtensionId() const override { return TEXT("com.ivanmurzak.unreal-ai-control-rig"); }
	virtual FString GetExtensionVersion() const override { return UnrealMcpRql::PluginVersion(TEXT("UnrealAIControlRig")); }

	virtual void ConfigureRql(FUnrealMcpRqlModuleContext& Context) override
	{
		using namespace UnrealAIControlRigRqlLocal;
		Context.AddAssetSource(TEXT("controlRigs"), TEXT("Control Rig blueprint assets (ControlRigBlueprint) of the project, at most 200"),
			UControlRigBlueprint::StaticClass());
		Context.AddJsonMember(UControlRigBlueprint::StaticClass(), TEXT("Elements"),
			TEXT("rig element counts: Bones, Nulls, Controls, Curves"),
			[](UObject* Object) -> TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>
			{
				TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Out = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();
				if (URigHierarchy* Hierarchy = HierarchyOf(Object))
				{
					Out->SetNumberField(TEXT("Bones"), Hierarchy->Num(ERigElementType::Bone));
					Out->SetNumberField(TEXT("Nulls"), Hierarchy->Num(ERigElementType::Null));
					Out->SetNumberField(TEXT("Controls"), Hierarchy->Num(ERigElementType::Control));
					Out->SetNumberField(TEXT("Curves"), Hierarchy->Num(ERigElementType::Curve));
				}
				return MakeShared<FJsonValueObject>(Out);
			});
		Context.AddJsonMember(UControlRigBlueprint::StaticClass(), TEXT("Hierarchy"),
			TEXT("every rig element in hierarchy order: Name, Type"),
			[](UObject* Object) -> TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>
			{
				TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>> Elements;
				if (URigHierarchy* Hierarchy = HierarchyOf(Object))
				{
					for (const FRigElementKey& Key : Hierarchy->GetAllKeys(/*bTraverse=*/true))
					{
						TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Entry = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();
						Entry->SetStringField(TEXT("Name"), Key.Name.ToString());
						Entry->SetStringField(TEXT("Type"), EnumName(Key.Type));
						Elements.Add(MakeShared<FJsonValueObject>(Entry));
					}
				}
				return MakeShared<FJsonValueArray>(Elements);
			});
		Context.AddJsonMember(UControlRigBlueprint::StaticClass(), TEXT("Controls"),
			TEXT("the rig's controls: Name, ControlType (Float, Transform, ...)"),
			[](UObject* Object) -> TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>
			{
				TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>> Controls;
				if (URigHierarchy* Hierarchy = HierarchyOf(Object))
				{
					for (const FRigControlElement* Control : Hierarchy->GetControls())
					{
						TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Entry = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();
						Entry->SetStringField(TEXT("Name"), Control->GetName());
						Entry->SetStringField(TEXT("ControlType"), EnumName(Control->Settings.ControlType));
						Controls.Add(MakeShared<FJsonValueObject>(Entry));
					}
				}
				return MakeShared<FJsonValueArray>(Controls);
			});
		Context.AddJsonMember(UControlRigBlueprint::StaticClass(), TEXT("Bones"),
			TEXT("the rig's bones: Name, Parent (empty for a root)"),
			[](UObject* Object) -> TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>
			{
				TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>> Bones;
				if (URigHierarchy* Hierarchy = HierarchyOf(Object))
				{
					for (const FRigBoneElement* Bone : Hierarchy->GetBones())
					{
						const FRigElementKey Parent = Hierarchy->GetFirstParent(Bone->GetKey());
						TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Entry = MakeShared<FJsonObject>();
						Entry->SetStringField(TEXT("Name"), Bone->GetName());
						Entry->SetStringField(TEXT("Parent"), Parent.IsValid() ? Parent.Name.ToString() : FString());
						Bones.Add(MakeShared<FJsonValueObject>(Entry));
					}
				}
				return MakeShared<FJsonValueArray>(Bones);
			});
		// The rig the component already runs, read from its reflected (transient) property: GetControlRig() would
		// instantiate one during a read.
		Context.AddObjectMember(UControlRigComponent::StaticClass(), TEXT("BoundRig"),
			TEXT("the Control Rig the component runs (null when none is instanced)"), UControlRig::StaticClass(),
			[](UObject* Object) -> UObject*
			{
				static const FObjectPropertyBase* Property = FindFProperty<FObjectPropertyBase>(UControlRigComponent::StaticClass(), TEXT("ControlRig"));
				return Property && Object ? Property->GetObjectPropertyValue_InContainer(Object) : nullptr;
			});
		Context.AddGuide(TEXT("Control Rig"), TEXT(R"MD(Control Rig blueprints are assets: `controlRigs`. Their element hierarchy (bones, nulls, controls, curves) is in
`Elements` (counts), `Hierarchy`, `Controls` and `Bones`; Control Rig components are components:
`actors | get Components | where $ is ControlRigComponent` (`BoundRig` is the running rig instance).

```
controlRigs | select $ref Name Elements
controlRigs | where Name == "CR_Mannequin" | select Controls
controlRigs | where Name == "CR_Mannequin" | get Bones | where Parent == "" | select Name
actors | get Components | where $ is ControlRigComponent | select Owner.Label BoundRig
```

The hierarchy is read-only through RQL; author rigs in the Control Rig editor.)MD"));
	}
};

IMPLEMENT_MODULE(TUnrealMcpRqlEditorModule<FUnrealAIControlRigRqlModule>, UnrealAIControlRig)

```

`extensions/UnrealAIControlRig/Source/UnrealAIControlRig/UnrealAIControlRig.Build.cs`:

```cs
// Copyright (c) 2026 IvanMurzak/Unreal-AI-ControlRig. Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
// See the LICENSE file in the repository root for more information.

using UnrealBuildTool;

public class UnrealAIControlRig : ModuleRules
{
	public UnrealAIControlRig(ReadOnlyTargetRules Target) : base(Target)
	{
		PCHUsage = ModuleRules.PCHUsageMode.UseExplicitOrSharedPCHs;

		PublicDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new string[]
		{
			"Core",
		});

		PrivateDependencyModuleNames.AddRange(new string[]
		{
			"CoreUObject",
			"Engine",
			// FJsonValue: the Elements / Hierarchy / Controls / Bones members.
			"Json",
			// The RQL module seam: IUnrealMcpRqlModule.h (sources, operations, members, guides, the editor-module template)
			// and UnrealMcpRqlTools.h (the specs run plans) live in the Unreal-MCP plugin's UnrealMcpRql module; the
			// matching `UnrealMCP` plugin dependency is in the .uplugin "Plugins" array.
			"UnrealMcpRql",

			// The gating engine plugin (its { "Name": "ControlRig" } entry is in the .uplugin "Plugins" array):
			// ControlRig (Runtime) has URigHierarchy and UControlRigComponent (the BoundRig member); ControlRigDeveloper
			// (UncookedOnly) has UControlRigBlueprint, the controlRigs source and the owner of the rig hierarchy.
			"ControlRig",
			"ControlRigDeveloper",
		});
	}
}

`extensions/UnrealAIControlRig/Tests/e2e/tools/control-rig-components-query.e2e.ps1`:

```ps1
# E2E check of the extension's RQL module (Unreal-MCP docs/rql.md). Returned to scripts/run-extension-e2e.ps1, which
# invokes `unreal-mcp-cli run-tool rql-query` against the running project's MCP server and asserts a well-formed success.
@{
    Tool   = "rql-query"
    System = $false
    Input  = '{"query":"actors | get Components | where $ is ControlRigComponent | count"}'
    Assert = {
        param($Result)
        $serialized = $Result | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 20 -Compress
        if ($serialized -notmatch '"text"\s*:\s*"\d+"|value\\?"\s*:\s*\d') {
            throw "expected the count of Control Rig components; got: $serialized"
        }
    }
}

`extensions/UnrealAIEnhancedInput/README.md`:

```md
# EnhancedInput RQL module

RQL module for Unreal's Enhanced Input system: query Input Actions and Mapping Contexts with their key mappings, create actions and contexts, map keys.

An optional editor plugin in the [Unreal MCP monorepository](../../README.md), with its own module, version and release archive.

## Requirements

- Unreal Engine 5.7 or later (the shared extension suite verifies UE 5.7 and 5.8).
- Unreal MCP 1.0.0 or later (the RQL data layer), installed in the same project.
- Engine plugins: `EnhancedInput`. The installer enables these dependencies.
- A C++ toolchain for your Unreal Engine installation. Extension releases contain source files and must be compiled for your project and engine.

## Install

With the Unreal Editor closed:

```sh
npm install -g unreal-mcp-cli
unreal-mcp-cli install-plugin "<UEProject>"
unreal-mcp-cli install-extension com.ivanmurzak.unreal-ai-enhanced-input "<UEProject>"
```

Replace `<UEProject>` with the project directory. The installer selects this extension's latest indexed version independently of the core and other extensions. Use `--version X.Y.Z` to select a published historical version, or `--build` to compile after installation. Otherwise rebuild the project before opening the editor.

The plugin is installed under `Plugins/UnrealAIEnhancedInput/`. Connect Unreal MCP to your AI client to use the RQL module below.

## RQL module

The extension adds its feature to the editor's RQL data layer (`rql-query` / `rql-mutate` / `rql-schema`, [docs/rql.md](../../docs/rql.md)) instead of separate tools; its guide is part of the `unreal-rql` skill.

| Kind | Names |
| --- | --- |
| Sources | `inputActions`, `inputContexts`, `enhancedInput` |
| Operations (`call`) | `CreateAction`, `CreateContext`, `AddMapping`, `RemoveMapping`, `AddActionEvent`, `AddMappingContextOnBeginPlay` |
| Members | `InputMappingContext.KeyMappings` |

```
inputContexts | select Name KeyMappings
enhancedInput | call CreateAction("/Game/Input/IA_Jump", "Boolean")
enhancedInput | call AddMapping("/Game/Input/IMC_Default", "/Game/Input/IA_Jump", "SpaceBar")
enhancedInput | call AddMappingContextOnBeginPlay("/Game/BP_Hero", "/Game/Input/IMC_Default")
enhancedInput | call AddActionEvent("/Game/BP_Hero", "/Game/Input/IA_Jump")      wire its Triggered pin with ref(node) | call Connect(...)
```

`AddActionEvent` places the Blueprint editor's Enhanced Input action event (Triggered, Started, Ongoing, Canceled,
Completed, ActionValue) in an actor Blueprint's event graph; `AddMappingContextOnBeginPlay` adds Event BeginPlay -> Get
Player Controller -> Enhanced Input Local Player Subsystem -> Add Mapping Context ahead of what BeginPlay already runs.
The event node comes from the EnhancedInput plugin's `InputBlueprintNodes` module, a dependency of this extension only.

## Releases and development

Each extension has its own versioned source ZIP in [Unreal MCP Releases](https://github.com/IvanMurzak/Unreal-MCP/releases). The shared release index records the latest version, historical releases and archive checksums; unchanged extensions are not copied into other component releases.

See the [monorepository and test guide](../../docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md) for independent publication, isolated compilation and the combined one-editor test suite. See [extension development](../../docs/EXTENSIONS.md) for the RQL module API.

Licensed under [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).

```

#if WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS

#include "Misc/AutomationTest.h"

#include "IUnrealMcpRqlModule.h"

// ============================================================================================
//  UE Automation spec for the extension's RQL module (Unreal-MCP docs/rql.md "Extensions").
//
//  The spec discovers THIS extension's live module through IModularFeatures (the path Unreal-MCP uses) and runs RQL
//  QueryPlans through the editor's RQL engine (UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan). The C++ runtime has no text parser, so
//  each plan is the one Rql.Parser produces for the query in the comment above it.
//
//  Run via:  Automation RunTests UnrealAIEnhancedInput
// ============================================================================================

BEGIN_DEFINE_SPEC(FUnrealAIEnhancedInputSpec, "UnrealAIEnhancedInput",
	EAutomationTestFlags::EditorContext | EAutomationTestFlags::ProductFilter)

	FString BlueprintPath;
	FString ActionPath;
	FString ContextPath;

	/** Run a plan with @BP@ / @IA@ / @IMC@ (and @Values@) filled in; the QueryResult. */
	TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Run(const FString& Plan, bool bMutate, std::initializer_list<TPair<const TCHAR*, FString>> Values = {})
	{
		FString Filled = Plan.Replace(TEXT("@BP@"), *BlueprintPath).Replace(TEXT("@IA@"), *ActionPath).Replace(TEXT("@IMC@"), *ContextPath);
		for (const TPair<const TCHAR*, FString>& Value : Values)
			Filled = Filled.Replace(*FString::Printf(TEXT("@%s@"), Value.Key), *Value.Value);
		TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Result;
		UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(Filled, bMutate, &Result);
		return Result;
	}

	static bool IsOk(const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject>& Result)
	{
		return Result.IsValid() && Result->GetBoolField(TEXT("ok"));
	}

	static FString Codes(const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject>& Result)
	{
		FString Text;
		if (Result.IsValid())
			FJsonSerializer::Serialize(Result.ToSharedRef(), TJsonWriterFactory<>::Create(&Text));
		return Text.Left(600);
	}

	/** The $ref in the result column of a receipt's first row (the object a call returned). */
	static FString ResultRef(const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject>& Receipt)
	{
		const TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>>* Rows = nullptr;
		if (!Receipt.IsValid() || !Receipt->TryGetArrayField(TEXT("rows"), Rows) || Rows->Num() == 0)
			return FString();
		const TArray<TSharedPtr<FJsonValue>>& Cells = (*Rows)[0]->AsArray();
		FString Ref;
		if (Cells.IsValidIndex(2) && Cells[2]->Type == EJson::Object)
			Cells[2]->AsObject()->TryGetStringField(TEXT("$ref"), Ref);
		return Ref;
	}

	/** A new Blueprint of @p Parent at a fresh path (BlueprintPath), with a fresh action and context (ActionPath, ContextPath). */
	UBlueprint* MakeBlueprint(UClass* Parent)
	{
		const FString Id = FGuid::NewGuid().ToString(EGuidFormats::Digits);
		BlueprintPath = FString::Printf(TEXT("/Game/RqlSpec/BP_Input_%s"), *Id);
		ActionPath = FString::Printf(TEXT("/Game/RqlSpec/IA_Jump_%s"), *Id);
		ContextPath = FString::Printf(TEXT("/Game/RqlSpec/IMC_Default_%s"), *Id);
		// enhancedInput | call CreateAction("@IA@", "Boolean")
		TestTrue(TEXT("action created"), IsOk(Run(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["enhancedInput"]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"CreateAction","args":[{"lit":"@IA@"},{"lit":"Boolean"}]}]})RQL"), true)));
		// enhancedInput | call CreateContext("@IMC@")
		TestTrue(TEXT("context created"), IsOk(Run(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["enhancedInput"]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"CreateContext","args":[{"lit":"@IMC@"}]}]})RQL"), true)));
		UPackage* Package = CreatePackage(*BlueprintPath);
		return FKismetEditorUtilities::CreateBlueprint(Parent, Package, *FPackageName::GetShortName(BlueprintPath), BPTYPE_Normal,
			UBlueprint::StaticClass(), UBlueprintGeneratedClass::StaticClass());
	}

	int32 CompileErrors(UBlueprint* Blueprint)
	{
		FCompilerResultsLog Log;
		FKismetEditorUtilities::CompileBlueprint(Blueprint, EBlueprintCompileOptions::SkipGarbageCollection, &Log);
		for (const TSharedRef<FTokenizedMessage>& Message : Log.Messages)
		{
			if (Message->GetSeverity() == EMessageSeverity::Error)
				AddInfo(Message->ToText().ToString());
		}
		return Log.NumErrors;
	}

END_DEFINE_SPEC(FUnrealAIEnhancedInputSpec)

void FUnrealAIEnhancedInputSpec::Define()
{
	Describe("RQL module", [this]()
	{
		It("registers this extension's RQL module as a modular feature", [this]()
		{
			IUnrealMcpRqlModule* Module = UnrealMcpRqlTools::FindModule(TEXT("com.ivanmurzak.unreal-ai-enhanced-input"));
			if (TestNotNull(TEXT("RQL module is registered"), Module))
			{
				TestEqual(TEXT("module name"), Module->GetRqlModuleName(), FString(TEXT("EnhancedInput")));
				TestFalse(TEXT("version reported"), Module->GetExtensionVersion().IsEmpty());
			}
		});

		It("adds its sources and guide to the unreal-rql skill", [this]()
		{
			const FString Skill = UnrealMcpRqlTools::SkillMarkdown();
			TestTrue(TEXT("| `inputActions` |"), Skill.Contains(TEXT("| `inputActions` |")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("| `inputContexts` |"), Skill.Contains(TEXT("| `inputContexts` |")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("| `enhancedInput` |"), Skill.Contains(TEXT("| `enhancedInput` |")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("## Enhanced Input"), Skill.Contains(TEXT("## Enhanced Input")));
		});
	});

	Describe("sources", [this]()
	{
		It("inputActions answers a query", [this]()
		{
			// inputActions | count
			TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Result;
			const bool bResultOk = UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["inputActions"]},"stages":[{"op":"count"}]})RQL"), false, &Result);
			TestTrue(TEXT("a well-formed result"), Result.IsValid());
			TestTrue(TEXT("succeeds"), bResultOk);
		});

		It("inputContexts answers a query", [this]()
		{
			// inputContexts | count
			TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Result;
			const bool bResultOk = UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["inputContexts"]},"stages":[{"op":"count"}]})RQL"), false, &Result);
			TestTrue(TEXT("a well-formed result"), Result.IsValid());
			TestTrue(TEXT("succeeds"), bResultOk);
		});

		It("describes InputMappingContext with its KeyMappings member", [this]()
		{
			bool bOk = false;
			const FString Schema = UnrealMcpRqlTools::Schema(TEXT("InputMappingContext"), bOk);
			TestTrue(TEXT("schema ok"), bOk);
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists name:KeyMappings"), Schema.Contains(TEXT("\"name\":\"KeyMappings\"")));
		});
	});

	Describe("operations", [this]()
	{
		It("lists the authoring operations", [this]()
		{
			bool bOk = false;
			const FString Schema = UnrealMcpRqlTools::Schema(TEXT("EnhancedInputOperations"), bOk);
			TestTrue(TEXT("schema ok"), bOk);
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists CreateAction("), Schema.Contains(TEXT("CreateAction(")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists CreateContext("), Schema.Contains(TEXT("CreateContext(")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists AddMapping("), Schema.Contains(TEXT("AddMapping(")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists RemoveMapping("), Schema.Contains(TEXT("RemoveMapping(")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists AddActionEvent("), Schema.Contains(TEXT("AddActionEvent(")));
			TestTrue(TEXT("lists AddMappingContextOnBeginPlay("), Schema.Contains(TEXT("AddMappingContextOnBeginPlay(")));
		});

		It("creates an action and a context, maps a key and refuses an unknown key", [this]()
		{
			const FString Id = FGuid::NewGuid().ToString(EGuidFormats::Digits);
			const FString NewActionPath = FString::Printf(TEXT("/Game/RqlSpec/IA_%s"), *Id);
			const FString NewContextPath = FString::Printf(TEXT("/Game/RqlSpec/IMC_%s"), *Id);
			// enhancedInput | call CreateAction("<action>", "Axis2D")
			TestTrue(TEXT("action created"), UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(FString::Printf(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["enhancedInput"]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"CreateAction","args":[{"lit":"%s"},{"lit":"Axis2D"}]}]})RQL"), *NewActionPath), true));
			// unreal.asset("<action>") | select ValueType
			TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Action;
			const bool bActionOk = UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(FString::Printf(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"call":"asset","on":{"path":["unreal"]},"args":[{"lit":"%s"}]},"stages":[{"op":"select","fields":[{"name":"ValueType","expr":{"path":["ValueType"]}}]}]})RQL"), *NewActionPath), false, &Action);
			TestTrue(TEXT("action read"), bActionOk);
			FString ValueType;
			if (Action.IsValid() && Action->HasField(TEXT("rows")) && Action->GetArrayField(TEXT("rows")).Num() == 1)
				ValueType = Action->GetArrayField(TEXT("rows"))[0]->AsArray()[0]->AsString();
			TestEqual(TEXT("value type written"), ValueType, FString(TEXT("Axis2D")));
			// enhancedInput | call CreateContext("<context>")
			TestTrue(TEXT("context created"), UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(FString::Printf(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["enhancedInput"]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"CreateContext","args":[{"lit":"%s"}]}]})RQL"), *NewContextPath), true));
			// enhancedInput | call AddMapping("<context>", "<action>", "SpaceBar")
			TestTrue(TEXT("key mapped"), UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(FString::Printf(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["enhancedInput"]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"AddMapping","args":[{"lit":"%s"},{"lit":"%s"},{"lit":"SpaceBar"}]}]})RQL"), *NewContextPath, *NewActionPath), true));
			// unreal.asset("<context>") | select KeyMappings
			TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Mappings;
			const bool bMappingsOk = UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(FString::Printf(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"call":"asset","on":{"path":["unreal"]},"args":[{"lit":"%s"}]},"stages":[{"op":"select","fields":[{"name":"KeyMappings","expr":{"path":["KeyMappings"]}}]}]})RQL"), *NewContextPath), false, &Mappings);
			TestTrue(TEXT("context read"), bMappingsOk);
			FString Text;
			if (Mappings.IsValid())
				FJsonSerializer::Serialize(Mappings.ToSharedRef(), TJsonWriterFactory<>::Create(&Text));
			TestTrue(TEXT("the mapping is listed"), Text.Contains(TEXT("SpaceBar")));
			// unreal.asset("<context>") | select Mappings — the live mappings on every version (since 5.7 the reflected array is deprecated and empty)
			TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Reflected;
			TestTrue(TEXT("Mappings read"), UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(FString::Printf(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"call":"asset","on":{"path":["unreal"]},"args":[{"lit":"%s"}]},"stages":[{"op":"select","fields":[{"name":"Mappings","expr":{"path":["Mappings"]}}]}]})RQL"), *NewContextPath), false, &Reflected));
			FString ReflectedText;
			if (Reflected.IsValid())
				FJsonSerializer::Serialize(Reflected.ToSharedRef(), TJsonWriterFactory<>::Create(&ReflectedText));
			TestTrue(*FString::Printf(TEXT("Mappings lists the mapping too (%s)"), *ReflectedText.Left(300)), ReflectedText.Contains(TEXT("SpaceBar")));
			// enhancedInput | call AddMapping("<context>", "<action>", "NoSuchKey")
			TestFalse(TEXT("unknown key refused"), UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(FString::Printf(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["enhancedInput"]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"AddMapping","args":[{"lit":"%s"},{"lit":"%s"},{"lit":"NoSuchKeyRqlSpec"}]}]})RQL"), *NewContextPath, *NewActionPath), true));
		});

		It("adds an action event to a Character Blueprint that wires to Jump and compiles; one event per action", [this]()
		{
			UBlueprint* Blueprint = MakeBlueprint(ACharacter::StaticClass());
			if (!TestNotNull(TEXT("character blueprint"), Blueprint))
				return;
			// enhancedInput | call AddActionEvent("@BP@", "@IA@")
			const TCHAR* AddEvent = TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["enhancedInput"]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"AddActionEvent","args":[{"lit":"@BP@"},{"lit":"@IA@"}]}]})RQL");
			const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Added = Run(AddEvent, true);
			TestTrue(*FString::Printf(TEXT("added (%s)"), *Codes(Added)), IsOk(Added));
			const FString Event = ResultRef(Added);
			TestTrue(*FString::Printf(TEXT("returns the node (%s)"), *Event), Event.StartsWith(TEXT("K2Node_EnhancedInputAction#")));
			TArray<UK2Node_EnhancedInputAction*> Nodes;
			FBlueprintEditorUtils::GetAllNodesOfClass(Blueprint, Nodes);
			if (!TestEqual(TEXT("one action event"), Nodes.Num(), 1))
				return;
			for (const TCHAR* Pin : { TEXT("Triggered"), TEXT("Started"), TEXT("Completed"), TEXT("ActionValue") })
				TestNotNull(*FString::Printf(TEXT("pin %s"), Pin), Nodes[0]->FindPin(Pin));

			// unreal.asset("@BP@").EventGraph | call AddCallFunction("Jump")
			const FString Jump = ResultRef(Run(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["EventGraph"],"on":{"call":"asset","on":{"path":["unreal"]},"args":[{"lit":"@BP@"}]}},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"AddCallFunction","args":[{"lit":"Jump"}]}]})RQL"), true));
			// ref("@N@") | call Connect("Triggered", ref("@J@"), "execute")
			const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Wired = Run(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"call":"ref","args":[{"lit":"@N@"}]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"Connect","args":[{"lit":"Triggered"},{"call":"ref","args":[{"lit":"@J@"}]},{"lit":"execute"}]}]})RQL"), true,
				{ { TEXT("N"), Event }, { TEXT("J"), Jump } });
			TestTrue(*FString::Printf(TEXT("Triggered wired to Jump (%s)"), *Codes(Wired)), IsOk(Wired));
			TestEqual(TEXT("compiles without errors"), CompileErrors(Blueprint), 0);

			const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Again = Run(AddEvent, true);
			TestTrue(*FString::Printf(TEXT("a second event for the action is refused (%s)"), *Codes(Again)), !IsOk(Again) && Codes(Again).Contains(TEXT("already has an action event")));
		});

		It("adds the mapping context at BeginPlay, ahead of what BeginPlay ran, once per context", [this]()
		{
			UBlueprint* Blueprint = MakeBlueprint(ACharacter::StaticClass());
			if (!TestNotNull(TEXT("character blueprint"), Blueprint))
				return;
			// unreal.asset("@BP@").EventGraph | call AddEvent("BeginPlay")
			const FString Begin = ResultRef(Run(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["EventGraph"],"on":{"call":"asset","on":{"path":["unreal"]},"args":[{"lit":"@BP@"}]}},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"AddEvent","args":[{"lit":"BeginPlay"}]}]})RQL"), true));
			// unreal.asset("@BP@").EventGraph | call AddCallFunction("PrintString")
			const FString Print = ResultRef(Run(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["EventGraph"],"on":{"call":"asset","on":{"path":["unreal"]},"args":[{"lit":"@BP@"}]}},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"AddCallFunction","args":[{"lit":"PrintString"}]}]})RQL"), true));
			// ref("@E@") | call Connect("then", ref("@P@"), "execute")
			TestTrue(TEXT("BeginPlay runs PrintString"), IsOk(Run(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"call":"ref","args":[{"lit":"@E@"}]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"Connect","args":[{"lit":"then"},{"call":"ref","args":[{"lit":"@P@"}]},{"lit":"execute"}]}]})RQL"), true,
				{ { TEXT("E"), Begin }, { TEXT("P"), Print } })));

			// enhancedInput | call AddMappingContextOnBeginPlay("@BP@", "@IMC@")
			const TCHAR* AddContext = TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["enhancedInput"]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"AddMappingContextOnBeginPlay","args":[{"lit":"@BP@"},{"lit":"@IMC@"}]}]})RQL");
			const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Added = Run(AddContext, true);
			TestTrue(*FString::Printf(TEXT("added (%s)"), *Codes(Added)), IsOk(Added));
			TestTrue(TEXT("returns the Add Mapping Context node"), ResultRef(Added).StartsWith(TEXT("K2Node_CallFunction#")));

			UK2Node_Event* BeginPlay = FBlueprintEditorUtils::FindOverrideForFunction(Blueprint, AActor::StaticClass(), TEXT("ReceiveBeginPlay"));
			const UEdGraphPin* Then = BeginPlay ? BeginPlay->FindPin(UEdGraphSchema_K2::PN_Then) : nullptr;
			const UK2Node_CallFunction* Add = Then && Then->LinkedTo.Num() == 1 ? Cast<UK2Node_CallFunction>(Then->LinkedTo[0]->GetOwningNode()) : nullptr;
			if (!TestNotNull(TEXT("BeginPlay runs Add Mapping Context first"), Add))
				return;
			TestEqual(TEXT("the call"), Add->FunctionReference.GetMemberName(), FName(TEXT("AddMappingContext")));
			const UEdGraphPin* ContextPin = Add->FindPin(TEXT("MappingContext"));
			TestTrue(TEXT("with the context"), ContextPin && ContextPin->DefaultObject && ContextPin->DefaultObject->GetPathName().StartsWith(ContextPath));
			const UEdGraphPin* AddThen = Add->FindPin(UEdGraphSchema_K2::PN_Then);
			TestTrue(TEXT("then what BeginPlay ran before"), AddThen && AddThen->LinkedTo.Num() == 1
				&& Cast<UK2Node_CallFunction>(AddThen->LinkedTo[0]->GetOwningNode())
				&& Cast<UK2Node_CallFunction>(AddThen->LinkedTo[0]->GetOwningNode())->FunctionReference.GetMemberName() == FName(TEXT("PrintString")));
			const UEdGraphPin* Target = Add->FindPin(UEdGraphSchema_K2::PN_Self);
			TestTrue(TEXT("on the local player's Enhanced Input subsystem"), Target && Target->LinkedTo.Num() == 1);
			TestEqual(TEXT("compiles without errors"), CompileErrors(Blueprint), 0);

			const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Again = Run(AddContext, true);
			TestTrue(*FString::Printf(TEXT("the same context again is refused (%s)"), *Codes(Again)), !IsOk(Again) && Codes(Again).Contains(TEXT("already adds")));
		});

		It("keeps a parent Blueprint's BeginPlay: a new BeginPlay in the child calls Parent: BeginPlay first", [this]()
		{
			UBlueprint* Parent = MakeBlueprint(ACharacter::StaticClass());
			if (!TestNotNull(TEXT("parent blueprint"), Parent))
				return;
			// unreal.asset("@BP@").EventGraph | call AddEvent("BeginPlay")
			TestTrue(TEXT("the parent implements BeginPlay"), IsOk(Run(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["EventGraph"],"on":{"call":"asset","on":{"path":["unreal"]},"args":[{"lit":"@BP@"}]}},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"AddEvent","args":[{"lit":"BeginPlay"}]}]})RQL"), true)));
			TestEqual(TEXT("the parent compiles"), CompileErrors(Parent), 0);
			UBlueprint* Child = MakeBlueprint(Parent->GeneratedClass);
			if (!TestNotNull(TEXT("child blueprint"), Child))
				return;
			// enhancedInput | call AddMappingContextOnBeginPlay("@BP@", "@IMC@")
			const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Added = Run(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["enhancedInput"]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"AddMappingContextOnBeginPlay","args":[{"lit":"@BP@"},{"lit":"@IMC@"}]}]})RQL"), true);
			TestTrue(*FString::Printf(TEXT("added (%s)"), *Codes(Added)), IsOk(Added));
			UK2Node_Event* BeginPlay = FBlueprintEditorUtils::FindOverrideForFunction(Child, AActor::StaticClass(), TEXT("ReceiveBeginPlay"));
			const UEdGraphPin* Then = BeginPlay ? BeginPlay->FindPin(UEdGraphSchema_K2::PN_Then) : nullptr;
			TestTrue(TEXT("BeginPlay calls the parent's first"), Then && Then->LinkedTo.Num() == 1
				&& Then->LinkedTo[0]->GetOwningNode()->IsA<UK2Node_CallParentFunction>());
			TestEqual(TEXT("the child compiles"), CompileErrors(Child), 0);
		});

		It("refuses a Blueprint that is not an actor", [this]()
		{
			UBlueprint* Blueprint = MakeBlueprint(UObject::StaticClass());
			if (!TestNotNull(TEXT("object blueprint"), Blueprint))
				return;
			// enhancedInput | call AddActionEvent("@BP@", "@IA@")
			const TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Refused = Run(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["enhancedInput"]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"AddActionEvent","args":[{"lit":"@BP@"},{"lit":"@IA@"}]}]})RQL"), true);
			TestTrue(*FString::Printf(TEXT("refused (%s)"), *Codes(Refused)), !IsOk(Refused) && Codes(Refused).Contains(TEXT("not an actor Blueprint")));
		});

		It("refuses an invalid asset path", [this]()
		{
			// enhancedInput | call CreateAction("/Engine/IA_RqlSpec")
			TSharedPtr<FJsonObject> Result;
			const bool bResultOk = UnrealMcpRqlTools::RunPlan(TEXT(R"RQL({"rql":"0.1","source":{"path":["enhancedInput"]},"stages":[{"op":"call","method":"CreateAction","args":[{"lit":"/Engine/IA_RqlSpec"}]}]})RQL"), true, &Result);
			TestTrue(TEXT("a well-formed result"), Result.IsValid());
			TestFalse(TEXT("fails defensively"), bResultOk);
		});
	});
}

#endif // WITH_DEV_AUTOMATION_TESTS
