`scripts/extension_suite.py`:

```py
"""Build plugins in isolation, then run their Automation tests in ONE editor process.

All writable plugin copies are scoped to engine version + profile. No shared testbed is edited.
Python stdlib only; the host OS's UE toolchain (Windows, macOS or Linux). See docs/EXTENSION-MONOREPO.md.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from contextlib import contextmanager
import hashlib
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import re
import signal
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import time

from extension_release import components as extensions

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
EXCLUDED = {"Binaries", "Intermediate", "Saved", "DerivedDataCache", ".git", ".vs", "node_modules"}
# This host's UBT platform, Build script and editor binary, relative to the engine root.
if os.name == "nt":
    UE_PLATFORM, UE_BUILD, UE_EDITOR = "Win64", "Engine/Build/BatchFiles/Build.bat", "Engine/Binaries/Win64/UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe"
elif sys.platform == "darwin":
    UE_PLATFORM, UE_BUILD, UE_EDITOR = "Mac", "Engine/Build/BatchFiles/Mac/Build.sh", "Engine/Binaries/Mac/UnrealEditor-Cmd"
else:
    UE_PLATFORM, UE_BUILD, UE_EDITOR = "Linux", "Engine/Build/BatchFiles/Linux/Build.sh", "Engine/Binaries/Linux/UnrealEditor-Cmd"
# POSIX: owned processes lead their own process group, so kill_owned can stop the whole tree.
NEW_SESSION = os.name != "nt"


@contextmanager
def machine_lock(already_held: bool = False, *, path: Path | None = None, timeout_seconds: float = 3600):
    """Use the SAME exclusive file handle as CI, including from interactive local runs."""
    if already_held:
        yield
        return
    if os.name != "nt":
        # .github/scripts/ue-machine-lock.ps1 holds an exclusive flock() on this same file.
        import fcntl
        lock_path = path or Path("/var/tmp/UnrealMCP-ci/ue.lock")
        lock_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_seconds
        announced = False
        with lock_path.open("a+b") as handle:
            # Open to every account, as the CI holder does (folder 1777, file 0666): a CI runner under
            # another account must still be able to open a lock this local run created first.
            for target, mode in ((lock_path.parent, 0o1777), (lock_path, 0o666)):
                try:
                    target.chmod(mode)
                except OSError:
                    pass
            while True:
                try:
                    fcntl.flock(handle, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
                    break
                except BlockingIOError:
                    if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                        raise OSError(f"Cannot acquire UE machine lock {lock_path}") from None
                    if not announced:
                        print("Waiting for the machine-wide UE lock (another local/CI build owns it)", flush=True)
                        announced = True
                    time.sleep(1)
            yield  # closing the file releases the flock()
        return
    import ctypes
    from ctypes import wintypes
    lock_path = path or Path(os.environ.get("ProgramData", "C:/ProgramData")) / "UnrealMCP-ci/ue.lock"
    lock_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    kernel = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32", use_last_error=True)
    create = kernel.CreateFileW
    create.argtypes = [wintypes.LPCWSTR, wintypes.DWORD, wintypes.DWORD, ctypes.c_void_p,
                       wintypes.DWORD, wintypes.DWORD, wintypes.HANDLE]
    create.restype = wintypes.HANDLE
    kernel.CloseHandle.argtypes = [wintypes.HANDLE]
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout_seconds
    announced = False
    while True:
        handle = create(str(lock_path), 0xC0000000, 0, None, 4, 0x80, None)
        if handle != wintypes.HANDLE(-1).value:
            break
        error = ctypes.get_last_error()
        if error not in (32, 33) or time.monotonic() > deadline:
            raise OSError(error, f"Cannot acquire UE machine lock {lock_path}")
        if not announced:
            print("Waiting for the machine-wide UE lock (another local/CI build owns it)", flush=True)
            announced = True
        time.sleep(1)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        kernel.CloseHandle(handle)


def default_output() -> Path:
    if os.name == "nt":
        return Path(os.environ.get("SystemDrive", "C:") + "/wt/unreal-tests") / hashlib.sha256(str(ROOT).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
    return ROOT / ".artifacts/tests"


def write_json(path: Path, value: object) -> None:
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    text = json.dumps(value, indent=2) + "\n"
    if not path.exists() or path.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != text:
        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")


def copy_plugin(source: Path, dest: Path, strict: bool = False, *, core_tests: bool = False) -> None:
    """Incremental source sync, preserving ONLY this profile's own build cache."""
    expected: set[Path] = set()
    for file in source.rglob("*"):
        rel = file.relative_to(source)
        if rel.parts[0] == "Tests" or any(part in EXCLUDED for part in rel.parts) or not file.is_file():
            continue
        expected.add(rel)
        data = file.read_bytes()
        if core_tests and file.name == "UnrealMCP.uplugin":
            descriptor = json.loads(data.decode("utf-8-sig"))
            descriptor["Modules"].append({"Name": "UnrealMcpEditorTests", "Type": "Editor", "LoadingPhase": "Default"})
            data = (json.dumps(descriptor, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
        if strict and file.suffix == ".cs" and file.name.endswith(".Build.cs"):
            text = data.decode("utf-8-sig")
            text = re.sub(r"PCHUsage\s*=\s*[^;]+;", "PCHUsage = PCHUsageMode.NoPCHs;", text)
            # Module-scoped overrides keep installed engine build settings untouched.
            text = re.sub(r"(PCHUsage = PCHUsageMode.NoPCHs;)", r"\1\n\t\tbUseUnity = false;", text)
            data = text.encode("utf-8")
        target = dest / rel
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        if not target.exists() or target.read_bytes() != data:
            target.write_bytes(data)
    for file in dest.rglob("*"):
        rel = file.relative_to(dest)
        if file.is_file() and not any(p in EXCLUDED for p in rel.parts) and rel not in expected:
            file.unlink()


def prepare(engine: Path, profile: str, selected: list[str], output: Path, *, strict: bool = False,
            core_tests: bool = False) -> Path:
    version = json.loads((engine / "Engine/Build/Build.version").read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
    engine_key = f"UE-{version['MajorVersion']}.{version['MinorVersion']}-" + hashlib.sha256(str(engine).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
    base = output / engine_key / profile
    base.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    marker = base / ".unreal-mcp-suite"
    identity = str(ROOT)
    if any(base.iterdir()) and (not marker.exists() or marker.read_text() != identity):
        raise ValueError(f"Refusing foreign build directory: {base}")
    if not marker.exists():
        marker.write_text(identity)
    plugins = base / "Plugins"
    allowed = {"UnrealMCP", *selected}
    if plugins.exists() and any(p.name not in allowed for p in plugins.iterdir()):
        raise ValueError(f"Unexpected plugin in isolated profile {plugins}; use a fresh output directory")
    copy_plugin(ROOT / "UnrealMCP", plugins / "UnrealMCP", core_tests=core_tests)
    for name in selected:
        copy_plugin(extensions()[name], plugins / name, strict)
    template = ROOT / "tests/host-project"
    # Do not touch identical Target.cs/Build.cs files: their timestamps invalidate UBT caches.
    for file in template.rglob("*"):
        if file.is_file():
            target = base / file.relative_to(template)
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            data = file.read_bytes()
            if not target.exists() or target.read_bytes() != data:
                target.write_bytes(data)
    project = base / "UnrealMcpTests.uproject"
    write_json(project, {"FileVersion": 3, "EngineAssociation": f"{version['MajorVersion']}.{version['MinorVersion']}",
                        "Modules": [{"Name": "UnrealMcpTests", "Type": "Runtime", "LoadingPhase": "Default"}],
                        "Plugins": [{"Name": n, "Enabled": True} for n in sorted(allowed)],
                        "DisableEnginePluginsByDefault": True})
    filters = ["UnrealMcp."] if core_tests else []
    filters += selected
    config = base / "Config/DefaultEngine.ini"
    config.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    group = ",".join(f'(Contains="{p}",MatchFromStart=True)' for p in filters)
    config_text = ('[/Script/AutomationController.AutomationControllerSettings]\n'
                   f'+Groups=(Name="UnrealMcpSuite",Filters=({group}))\n')
    if not config.exists() or config.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != config_text:
        config.write_text(config_text, encoding="utf-8")
    return project


def build(engine: Path, project: Path) -> None:
    command = [str(engine / UE_BUILD), "UnrealMcpTestsEditor", UE_PLATFORM, "Development",
               f"-Project={project}", "-WaitMutex", "-NoHotReloadFromIDE"]
    print(f"Building {project.parent} (no editor launch)", flush=True)
    log_path = project.parent / "build.log"
    with log_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as log:
        completed = subprocess.run(command, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    if completed.returncode:
        print("\n".join(log_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()[-80:]), flush=True)
        completed.check_returncode()


def check_report(report: Path, selected: list[str], core_tests: bool = True) -> dict:
    data = json.loads(report.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig"))
    tests = data.get("tests", [])
    if not tests or data.get("failed", 0) or data.get("notRun", 0) or data.get("inProcess", 0):
        failures = [t for t in tests if t.get("state") not in ("Success", "SuccessWithWarnings")]
        raise ValueError(f"Incomplete/failed Automation report: {report}; "
                         f"counts={ {k: data.get(k) for k in ('succeeded', 'failed', 'notRun', 'inProcess')} }; "
                         f"nonpassing={json.dumps(failures, ensure_ascii=False)[:16000]}")
    paths: list[str] = []
    for test in tests:
        if test.get("state") not in ("Success", "SuccessWithWarnings"):
            raise ValueError(f"Automation test did not pass: {test}")
        paths.append(test["fullTestPath"])
    inventory = json.loads((ROOT / "tests/automation-inventory.json").read_text())
    required = {prefix: minimum for prefix, minimum in inventory.items()
                if (core_tests and prefix.startswith("UnrealMcp.")) or any(prefix.startswith(n) for n in selected)}
    if any(not any(p == name or p.startswith(name + ".") for p in required) for name in selected):
        raise ValueError("A selected extension is missing from tests/automation-inventory.json")
    for prefix, minimum in required.items():
        count = sum(p == prefix or p.startswith(prefix + ".") for p in paths)
        if count < minimum:
            raise ValueError(f"Missing Automation coverage: {prefix}: expected >= {minimum}, got {count}")
    return {"passed": len(paths), "prefixes": len(required)}


def kill_owned(process: subprocess.Popen) -> None:
    if NEW_SESSION:
        # Even after the leader exited: its group (e.g. ShaderCompileWorker) may still be alive.
        try:
            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        except ProcessLookupError:
            pass
    elif process.poll() is None:
        stopped = subprocess.run(["taskkill", "/PID", str(process.pid), "/T", "/F"], check=False, capture_output=True)
        if stopped.returncode and process.poll() is None:
            print(f"Owned process {process.pid} tree stop failed: {stopped.stdout!r} {stopped.stderr!r}", flush=True)
            process.kill()
    process.wait(timeout=30)


def automation(engine: Path, project: Path, selected: list[str], timeout: int,
               server: Path | None = None, bridge: Path | None = None, result_file: Path | None = None) -> dict:
    report = project.parent / "Reports" / time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    report.mkdir(parents=True)
    if result_file:
        write_json(result_file, {"status": "running", "report": str(report)})
    env = os.environ.copy()
    # Inherit no credentials/remote endpoints from a developer or another task.
    for key in list(env):
        if key.startswith("UNREAL_MCP_"):
            del env[key]
    env.update(UNREAL_MCP_CONNECTION_MODE="Custom", UNREAL_MCP_KEEP_CONNECTED="false")
    server_proc = None
    server_log = None
    if server:
        if not bridge or not server.is_file() or not bridge.is_file():
            raise ValueError("Live E2E needs existing --server and --bridge binaries")
        import connection_smoke as smoke
        with socket.socket() as sock:
            sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
            port = sock.getsockname()[1]
        server_log = (report / "server.log").open("w")
        server_proc = subprocess.Popen([str(server), "--port", str(port), "--client-transport", "streamableHttp"],
                                       stdout=server_log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, cwd=server.parent,
                                       start_new_session=NEW_SESSION)
        print(f"Started owned server PID {server_proc.pid}", flush=True)
        if not smoke.wait_port(port, 40):
            kill_owned(server_proc)
            server_log.close()
            raise ValueError("Local MCP server failed to start")
        env.update(UNREAL_MCP_HOST=f"http://localhost:{port}", UNREAL_MCP_KEEP_CONNECTED="true",
                   UNREAL_MCP_BRIDGE_PATH=str(bridge))
    command = [str(engine / UE_EDITOR), str(project),
               "-nullrhi", "-nosplash", "-unattended", "-NoSound", "-log",
               "-ExecCmds=Automation RunTests Group:UnrealMcpSuite", f"-ReportExportPath={report}",
               f"-abslog={report / 'editor.log'}"]
    editor = None
    try:
        editor = subprocess.Popen(command, env=env, cwd=project.parent, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
                                  start_new_session=NEW_SESSION)
        print(f"Started ONE owned editor PID {editor.pid}; report {report}", flush=True)
        deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
        while not (report / "index.json").exists():
            if editor.poll() is not None or time.monotonic() > deadline:
                raise ValueError(f"Editor exited or timed out without Automation report: {report}")
            time.sleep(1)
        while True:
            try:
                result = check_report(report / "index.json", selected)
                break
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, PermissionError):
                if time.monotonic() > deadline:
                    raise
                time.sleep(0.1)
        if server:
            # Reuse this SAME editor, server and sidecar for every preserved E2E check.
            url = f"http://localhost:{port}"
            while True:
                if editor.poll() is not None or time.monotonic() > deadline:
                    raise ValueError("Editor/MCP connection failed before E2E")
                try:
                    status, sid = smoke.mcp_initialize(url + "/mcp", None)
                    tools = smoke.mcp_list_tools(url + "/mcp", None, sid) if status == 200 else []
                    expected = {t["name"] for n in selected for t in json.loads((extensions()[n] / "extension.json").read_text())["tools"]}
                    if expected.issubset(tools):
                        break
                except (OSError, ValueError):
                    pass
                time.sleep(1)
            subprocess.run(["pwsh", "-NoProfile", "-File", str(ROOT / "scripts/run-extension-e2e.ps1"),
                            "-ProjectDir", str(project.parent), "-Url", url, "-Plugins", ",".join(selected)],
                           env=env, check=True, timeout=max(1, deadline - time.monotonic()))
            result["e2e"] = "passed"
        result.update(editorLaunches=1, editorPid=editor.pid, report=str(report))
        return result
    finally:
        if editor:
            kill_owned(editor)
        if server_proc:
            kill_owned(server_proc)
        if server_log:
            server_log.close()


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--engine", type=Path, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path, default=default_output())
    parser.add_argument("--extensions", nargs="*", help="Plugin names; default all")
    parser.add_argument("--mode", choices=["full", "verification", "isolated", "automation", "prepare"], default="full")
    parser.add_argument("--ue-lock-held", action="store_true", help="CI only: caller already holds the machine-wide lock")
    parser.add_argument("--result-file", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=1800)
    parser.add_argument("--server", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--bridge", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    with machine_lock(args.ue_lock_held):
        engine = args.engine.resolve()
        selected = args.extensions if args.extensions is not None else list(extensions())
        if any(n not in extensions() for n in selected):
            parser.error("Unknown extension")
        output = args.output.resolve()
        if args.result_file:
            write_json(args.result_file, {"status": "running"})
        if args.mode == "full" and (not args.server or not args.bridge):
            from suite_dependencies import resolve
            args.server, args.bridge = resolve(output)
        if args.mode in ("full", "verification", "isolated"):
            # No siblings are present in these copies, including their headers and DLLs.
            for name in [None, *selected]:
                project = prepare(engine, "isolated/" + (name or "core"), [name] if name else [], output, strict=True)
                build(engine, project)
        if args.mode != "isolated":
            profile = "all" if selected == list(extensions()) else "selected-" + hashlib.sha256(",".join(selected).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]
            project = prepare(engine, profile, selected, output, core_tests=True)
            if args.mode != "prepare":
                build(engine, project)
                result = automation(engine, project, selected, args.timeout, args.server, args.bridge, args.result_file)
                write_json(project.parent / "suite-result.json", result)
                if args.result_file:
                    write_json(args.result_file, result)
                print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)
        return 0



if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

```

`scripts/release_dependency_guard.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Release dependency guard: refuse a release that would ship a dependency that is not a published release.

Between test waves the plugin's `main` may consume an UNRELEASED dependency: RQL from its main commit,
as the sidecar's `com.IvanMurzak.Rql 0.3.0-dev.<sha>` (restored from `bridge/prerelease-packages/`
through `bridge/Directory.Build.props`) and as the vendored C++ runtime in
`UnrealMCP/Source/ThirdParty/RQL/`. Fine for CI; a release cut in that state ships unreleased code
nobody can rebuild from published packages. This guard runs as the FIRST step of `release.yml` and
`release_extensions.yml` and fails the run (dry runs too) before anything is built or published.

What it checks (everything the core, extension and CLI releases ship):
  * every NuGet pin of the sidecar (`bridge/src/*.csproj`, the `Directory.Build.props` /
    `Directory.Packages.props` above it, MSBuild `$(Property)` versions resolved): a pre-release
    version (any `-` suffix) or a version not listed on nuget.org fails, and so does a local
    (non-URL) restore source (`RestoreAdditionalProjectSources`, `nuget.config`), e.g. `prerelease-packages`;
  * the vendored RQL C++ runtime: its README must record the published `com.IvanMurzak.Rql` release it
    was copied from (`com.IvanMurzak.Rql` <version>: not a pre-release, listed on nuget.org), that version must
    equal the sidecar's `com.IvanMurzak.Rql` pin (the C++ runtime executes the plans the sidecar's RQL
    parses), and its recorded commit must be the `<repository commit>` of that package's nuspec. The
    copied sources carry no version of their own, so the README is what is checked;
  * the vendored Code-Exec Python runtime (`_vendor/code_exec/VENDORED.md`): a published
    `com.IvanMurzak.CodeExec` release;
  * every extension's `minCoreVersion` (`extensions/*/extension.json`) and the npm dependencies of
    `unreal-mcp-cli` (`cli/package.json`): pre-release or non-registry specs fail.

Usage:
    python scripts/release_dependency_guard.py [--root <repo>]
Exit 0 = every pin is a published release; exit 1 = problems listed (file:line: message).
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from dataclasses import dataclass
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Iterable, Optional

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
NUGET_INDEX_URL = "https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/{id}/index.json"
NUGET_NUSPEC_URL = "https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/{id}/{version}/{id}.nuspec"

# MSBuild item types that pin a NuGet package version.
PACKAGE_ITEMS = {"PackageReference", "PackageVersion", "GlobalPackageReference", "PackageDownload"}
# MSBuild properties that add NuGet restore sources.
RESTORE_SOURCE_PROPERTIES = {"RestoreSources", "RestoreAdditionalProjectSources", "RestoreFallbackFolders"}
SKIP_DIRS = {"bin", "obj", "node_modules", "publish", "prerelease-packages"}
PROPERTY_RE = re.compile(r"\$\(([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)\)")
NPM_PRERELEASE_RE = re.compile(r"\d+\.\d+\.\d+-")
# A registry semver spec (`1.2.3`, `^1.2`, `~1`, `>=1 <2`, `v1.2.3`); dist-tags, paths, git and URLs are not.
NPM_REGISTRY_SPEC_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*[0-9^~<>=v]")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Pin:
    """One dependency version as written in a shipped file."""

    ecosystem: str  # "nuget": pre-release + nuget.org check; "semver": pre-release check only
    package: str
    version: str
    file: Path
    line: int


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Problem:
    file: Path
    line: int
    message: str


class RegistryError(Exception):
    """nuget.org could not be queried (network / HTTP error other than 404)."""


class NuGetRegistry:
    """Listed versions per package id from the nuget.org flat container (cached; 404 = unknown package)."""

    def __init__(self, fetch: Optional[Callable[[str], Optional[bytes]]] = None) -> None:
        self._fetch = fetch or _http_get
        self._cache: dict[str, Optional[set[str]] | RegistryError] = {}

    def versions(self, package: str) -> Optional[set[str]]:
        key = package.lower()
        if key not in self._cache:
            try:
                body = self._fetch(NUGET_INDEX_URL.format(id=key))
                self._cache[key] = None if body is None else {
                    normalize_nuget_version(v) for v in json.loads(body.decode("utf-8")).get("versions", [])
                }
            except RegistryError as error:  # remembered: one retry cycle per package, not per pin
                self._cache[key] = error
        cached = self._cache[key]
        if isinstance(cached, RegistryError):
            raise cached
        return cached

    def source_commit(self, package: str, version: str) -> Optional[str]:
        """The `<repository commit>` a published package was packed from (None: no nuspec / no commit)."""
        key = package.lower()
        body = self._fetch(NUGET_NUSPEC_URL.format(id=key, version=normalize_nuget_version(version)))
        if body is None:
            return None
        repository = next((e for e in ET.fromstring(body).iter() if _local(e.tag) == "repository"), None)
        return None if repository is None else repository.get("commit")


def _http_get(url: str) -> Optional[bytes]:
    """GET with retries; None on 404; RegistryError when nuget.org stays unreachable."""
    last: Exception | None = None
    for attempt in range(3):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=30) as response:
                return response.read()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
            if error.code == 404:
                return None
            last = error
        except (urllib.error.URLError, TimeoutError, OSError) as error:
            last = error
        if attempt < 2:
            time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
    raise RegistryError(f"{url}: {last}")


# --- versions ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def is_prerelease(version: str) -> bool:
    """SemVer/NuGet pre-release: any `-` suffix on the version (build metadata `+x` alone is not)."""
    return "-" in version.split("+", 1)[0]


def normalize_nuget_version(version: str) -> str:
    """NuGet's normalized form: `1.0` -> `1.0.0`, `1.0.0.0` -> `1.0.0`, leading zeros dropped, metadata dropped."""
    core, _, prerelease = version.split("+", 1)[0].strip().partition("-")
    parts = [str(int(p)) if p.isdigit() else p for p in core.split(".")]
    while len(parts) < 3:
        parts.append("0")
    if len(parts) == 4 and parts[3] == "0":
        parts.pop()
    normalized = ".".join(parts)
    return (normalized + "-" + prerelease if prerelease else normalized).lower()


def nuget_versions_in(spec: str) -> tuple[list[str], Optional[str]]:
    """The concrete versions named by a NuGet version spec (`1.2.3`, `[1.2.3]`, `[1.0,2.0)`), or an error."""
    spec = spec.strip()
    if not spec:
        return [], "empty version"
    if "*" in spec:
        return [], f"floating version '{spec}' is not a pin"
    if spec[0] in "[(":
        if spec[-1] not in "])":
            return [], f"malformed version range '{spec}'"
        lower, _, upper = (b.strip() for b in spec[1:-1].partition(","))
        if "," not in spec:  # `[1.2.3]`: exactly that version
            return [lower], None
        # The lower bound is what restore picks; an exclusive upper bound need not exist (yet).
        return [b for b in (lower, upper if spec[-1] == "]" else "") if b], None
    return [spec], None


# --- MSBuild ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _local(tag: str) -> str:
    return tag.rsplit("}", 1)[-1]


def line_of(text: str, *needles: str) -> int:
    """1-based line of the first line containing every needle (0 when none does)."""
    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        if all(n in line for n in needles):
            return number
    return 0


def rel(path: Path, root: Path) -> str:
    try:
        return path.resolve().relative_to(root.resolve()).as_posix()
    except ValueError:
        return path.as_posix()


def ancestors(start: Path, root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """`start` and its parents up to and including `root`, outermost first."""
    root = root.resolve()
    chain = []
    current = start.resolve()
    while True:
        chain.append(current)
        if current == root or current.parent == current:
            break
        current = current.parent
    return list(reversed(chain))


def msbuild_chain(project: Path, root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """The `Directory.*.props/targets` above a project (outermost first), the project, and the
    `.props`/`.targets`/`.nuspec` files packed from its folder."""
    files: list[Path] = []
    for directory in ancestors(project.parent, root):
        for name in ("Directory.Build.props", "Directory.Packages.props", "Directory.Build.targets"):
            if (directory / name).is_file():
                files.append(directory / name)
    files.append(project)
    for path in walk(project.parent):
        if path.suffix in (".props", ".targets", ".nuspec") and path not in files:
            files.append(path)
    return files


def walk(directory: Path) -> Iterable[Path]:
    """Files of a project's folder, not descending into build output or another project's folder."""
    for entry in sorted(directory.iterdir()):
        if entry.is_dir():
            if entry.name not in SKIP_DIRS and not entry.name.startswith(".") and not any(entry.glob("*.csproj")):
                yield from walk(entry)
        else:
            yield entry


def read_properties(files: list[Path]) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """Every static `<PropertyGroup>` definition over the chain (Conditions are not evaluated, so a
    property set more than once keeps every value it may take)."""
    properties: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for path in files:
        try:
            tree = ET.parse(path)
        except ET.ParseError:
            continue
        for group in tree.getroot().iter():
            if _local(group.tag) != "PropertyGroup":
                continue
            for prop in group:
                if isinstance(prop.tag, str) and prop.text is not None:
                    values = properties.setdefault(_local(prop.tag), [])
                    if prop.text.strip() not in values:
                        values.append(prop.text.strip())
    return properties


def resolve(value: str, properties: dict[str, list[str]], file: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Every expansion of the `$(Name)`s in `value` over the static definitions; an unknown name stays
    as `$(Name)` (the caller reports it)."""
    builtins = {"MSBuildThisFileDirectory": str(file.parent) + os.sep, "MSBuildProjectDirectory": str(file.parent)}
    results: set[str] = set()
    pending = [(value, 0)]
    while pending:
        current, depth = pending.pop()
        match = PROPERTY_RE.search(current)
        name = match.group(1) if match else ""
        options = [builtins[name]] if name in builtins else properties.get(name)
        if not match or not options or depth >= 16:
            results.add(current)
            continue
        pending += [(current[:match.start()] + option + current[match.end():], depth + 1) for option in options]
    return sorted(results)


def is_url(source: str) -> bool:
    return re.match(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*://", source, re.IGNORECASE) is not None and not source.lower().startswith("file:")


def item_version(element: ET.Element) -> Optional[str]:
    """The version an item pins; `VersionOverride` wins over `Version` (central package management)."""
    for name in ("VersionOverride", "Version", "version"):
        if element.get(name) is not None:
            return element.get(name)
    for name in ("VersionOverride", "Version"):
        child = next((c for c in element if isinstance(c.tag, str) and _local(c.tag) == name), None)
        if child is not None and child.text:
            return child.text.strip()
    return None


def scan_msbuild(projects: list[Path], root: Path) -> tuple[list[Pin], list[Problem]]:
    pins: list[Pin] = []
    problems: list[Problem] = []
    for project in (p.resolve() for p in projects):
        chain = msbuild_chain(project, root)
        properties = read_properties(chain)
        for path in chain:  # a shared props file is read per project: its `$(X)` may differ per project
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
            try:
                document = ET.fromstring(text)
            except ET.ParseError as error:
                problems.append(Problem(path, 1, f"cannot parse MSBuild/nuspec XML: {error}"))
                continue
            for element in document.iter():
                if not isinstance(element.tag, str):
                    continue
                name = _local(element.tag)
                if name in PACKAGE_ITEMS or (name == "dependency" and path.suffix == ".nuspec"):
                    package = element.get("Include") or element.get("Update") or element.get("id")
                    raw = item_version(element)
                    if not package or raw is None:
                        continue  # a version-less reference takes its pin from a PackageVersion scanned here too
                    line = line_of(text, f'"{package}"', raw) or line_of(text, package, raw)
                    for version in resolve(raw, properties, path):
                        if PROPERTY_RE.search(version):
                            problems.append(Problem(path, line, f"{package}: cannot resolve version '{raw}'"))
                            continue
                        versions, error = nuget_versions_in(version)
                        if error:
                            problems.append(Problem(path, line, f"{package}: {error}"))
                        pins.extend(Pin("nuget", package, v, path, line) for v in versions)
                elif name in RESTORE_SOURCE_PROPERTIES and element.text:
                    for entry in element.text.split(";"):
                        entry = entry.strip()
                        if not entry or entry == f"$({name})":
                            continue
                        if not all(is_url(source) for source in resolve(entry, properties, path)):
                            problems.append(Problem(path, line_of(text, f"<{name}"),
                                                    f"{name} adds the local NuGet feed '{entry}' "
                                                    f"(a release must restore from nuget.org only; delete the "
                                                    f"pre-release feed when the pins return to published versions)"))
    return pins, problems


def scan_nuget_configs(projects: list[Path], root: Path) -> list[Problem]:
    problems: list[Problem] = []
    directories = {d for project in projects for d in ancestors(project.parent, root)}
    for directory in sorted(directories):
        for entry in directory.iterdir():
            if entry.is_file() and entry.name.lower() == "nuget.config":
                text = entry.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
                try:
                    tree = ET.fromstring(text)
                except ET.ParseError as error:
                    problems.append(Problem(entry, 1, f"cannot parse nuget.config: {error}"))
                    continue
                for sources in tree.iter("packageSources"):
                    for add in sources.iter("add"):
                        value = add.get("value", "")
                        if value and not is_url(value):
                            problems.append(Problem(entry, line_of(text, value),
                                                    f"package source '{add.get('key')}' is the local feed '{value}'"))
    return problems


# --- other pin sources ------------------------------------------------------------------------


def scan_package_json(path: Path) -> tuple[list[Pin], list[Problem]]:
    """`dependencies` / `optionalDependencies` (what installs with the package; dev dependencies do not)."""
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    data = json.loads(text)
    pins: list[Pin] = []
    problems: list[Problem] = []
    for section in ("dependencies", "optionalDependencies"):
        for package, spec in (data.get(section) or {}).items():
            line = line_of(text, f'"{package}"')
            if not isinstance(spec, str) or not NPM_REGISTRY_SPEC_RE.match(spec):
                problems.append(Problem(path, line, f"{package}: '{spec}' is not a registry version"))
            else:
                pins.append(Pin("semver", package, spec, path, line))
    return pins, problems


def check_pins(pins: list[Pin], registry: NuGetRegistry) -> list[Problem]:
    problems: list[Problem] = []
    for pin in pins:
        prerelease = is_prerelease(pin.version) if pin.ecosystem == "nuget" else bool(NPM_PRERELEASE_RE.search(pin.version))
        if prerelease:
            problems.append(Problem(pin.file, pin.line, f"{pin.package} {pin.version} is a pre-release version"))
            continue
        if pin.ecosystem != "nuget":
            continue
        try:
            listed = registry.versions(pin.package)
        except RegistryError as error:
            problems.append(Problem(pin.file, pin.line, f"{pin.package} {pin.version}: cannot verify on nuget.org ({error})"))
            continue
        if listed is None:
            problems.append(Problem(pin.file, pin.line, f"{pin.package} is not a package on nuget.org"))
        elif normalize_nuget_version(pin.version) not in listed:
            problems.append(Problem(pin.file, pin.line, f"{pin.package} {pin.version} is not published on nuget.org"))
    return problems


def require(path: Path, problems: list[Problem]) -> bool:
    """A shipped file the guard expects; missing = the guard is out of date, which must fail too."""
    if path.is_file():
        return True
    problems.append(Problem(path, 1, f"expected file is missing (update {Path(__file__).name})"))
    return False


# --- this repository --------------------------------------------------------------------------

RQL_PACKAGE = "com.IvanMurzak.Rql"
RQL_VENDORED = Path("UnrealMCP/Source/ThirdParty/RQL/README.md")
CODE_EXEC_VENDORED = Path("UnrealMCP/Content/Python/unreal_mcp/_vendor/code_exec/VENDORED.md")
RQL_COMMIT_RE = re.compile(r"commit\s+`([0-9a-fA-F]{7,40})`")
RQL_MARKER_RE = re.compile(r"`com\.IvanMurzak\.Rql`\s*`?\s*([0-9][0-9A-Za-z.+-]*[0-9A-Za-z])")
VENDORED_RELEASE_RE = re.compile(r"release\s+\*\*([^*\s]+)\*\*")


def scan_vendored(path: Path, package: str, marker: re.Pattern[str] = VENDORED_RELEASE_RE) -> tuple[list[Pin], list[Problem]]:
    """A vendored source copy records the package release it came from (`marker` captures the version)."""
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    match = marker.search(text)
    if not match:
        return [], [Problem(path, 1, f"vendored {package}: no release version marker (copy it from a published release)")]
    return [Pin("nuget", package, match.group(1), path, text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1)], []


def collect(root: Path) -> tuple[list[Pin], list[Problem]]:
    """Every dependency pin Unreal-MCP's core, extension and CLI releases ship."""
    problems: list[Problem] = []
    projects = sorted(root.glob("bridge/src/*.csproj"))
    if not projects:
        problems.append(Problem(root / "bridge" / "src", 1, f"no sidecar csproj found (update {Path(__file__).name})"))
    pins, msbuild_problems = scan_msbuild(projects, root)
    problems += msbuild_problems + scan_nuget_configs(projects, root)
    bridge_rql = {p.version for p in pins if p.package.lower() == RQL_PACKAGE.lower()}
    if require(root / RQL_VENDORED, problems):
        rql_pins, rql_problems = scan_vendored(root / RQL_VENDORED, RQL_PACKAGE, RQL_MARKER_RE)
        pins += rql_pins
        problems += rql_problems
        for pin in rql_pins:
            if bridge_rql and pin.version not in bridge_rql:
                problems.append(Problem(pin.file, pin.line, f"vendored RQL C++ runtime is {RQL_PACKAGE} {pin.version} "
                                        f"but the sidecar pins {', '.join(sorted(bridge_rql))}"))
    if require(root / CODE_EXEC_VENDORED, problems):
        code_exec_pins, code_exec_problems = scan_vendored(root / CODE_EXEC_VENDORED, "com.IvanMurzak.CodeExec")
        pins += code_exec_pins
        problems += code_exec_problems
    for descriptor in sorted(root.glob("extensions/*/extension.json")):
        text = descriptor.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
        minimum = json.loads(text).get("minCoreVersion")
        if minimum:
            pins.append(Pin("semver", "Unreal-MCP core (minCoreVersion)", minimum, descriptor, line_of(text, '"minCoreVersion"')))
    cli_package = root / "cli" / "package.json"
    if require(cli_package, problems):
        npm_pins, npm_problems = scan_package_json(cli_package)
        pins += npm_pins
        problems += npm_problems
    if not any(p.ecosystem == "nuget" for p in pins):
        problems.append(Problem(root / "bridge", 1, f"no NuGet pins found (update {Path(__file__).name})"))
    return pins, problems


def check_vendored_rql_commit(root: Path, pins: list[Pin], registry: NuGetRegistry) -> list[Problem]:
    """The README's commit must be the one the published package was packed from: a re-vendor from an
    unreleased commit that keeps the old version marker would otherwise pass."""
    readme = root / RQL_VENDORED
    marker = next((p for p in pins if p.file == readme and p.package == RQL_PACKAGE), None)
    if marker is None or is_prerelease(marker.version):
        return []  # no marker / a pre-release marker is already reported
    text = readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
    commit = RQL_COMMIT_RE.search(text)
    if not commit:
        return [Problem(readme, marker.line, "vendored RQL C++ runtime: no source commit (commit `<sha>`) recorded")]
    try:
        published = registry.source_commit(RQL_PACKAGE, marker.version)
    except (RegistryError, ET.ParseError) as error:
        return [Problem(readme, marker.line, f"{RQL_PACKAGE} {marker.version}: cannot read the nuspec on nuget.org ({error})")]
    if published is None:
        return []  # an unpublished version is reported by check_pins; a nuspec without a commit cannot be compared
    if not published.lower().startswith(commit.group(1).lower()):
        return [Problem(readme, text.count("\n", 0, commit.start()) + 1,
                        f"vendored RQL C++ runtime is commit {commit.group(1)} but {RQL_PACKAGE} {marker.version} "
                        f"was packed from {published[:12]} (copy the sources of that release)")]
    return []


def run(root: Path, registry: NuGetRegistry) -> tuple[list[Pin], list[Problem]]:
    pins, problems = collect(root)
    pins = list(dict.fromkeys(pins))
    problems += check_pins(pins, registry) + check_vendored_rql_commit(root, pins, registry)
    unique = sorted(set(problems), key=lambda p: (rel(p.file, root), p.line, p.message))
    return pins, unique


def main(argv: Optional[list[str]] = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n", 1)[0])
    parser.add_argument("--root", type=Path, default=ROOT, help="repository root (default: this checkout)")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    root = args.root.resolve()
    pins, problems = run(root, NuGetRegistry())
    files = sorted({rel(p.file, root) for p in pins})
    print(f"Release dependency guard: {len(pins)} pins in {len(files)} shipped files")
    for name in files:
        print(f"  {name}")
    if not problems:
        print("OK: every dependency pin is a published release.")
        return 0
    annotate = os.environ.get("GITHUB_ACTIONS") == "true"
    print(f"\nFAIL: {len(problems)} problem(s); this release would ship dependencies users cannot restore:")
    for problem in problems:
        location, line = rel(problem.file, root), problem.line or 1
        print(f"  {location}:{line}: {problem.message}")
        if annotate:
            print(f"::error file={location},line={line}::{problem.message}")
    print("\nSwitch every pin back to a published release (and delete local pre-release feeds) before releasing.")
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

`scripts/run-extension-e2e.ps1`:

```ps1
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$ProjectDir,
    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Url,
    [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Plugins
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$root = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot
$cli = Join-Path $root 'cli/dist/index.js'
$failures = @()
foreach ($plugin in $Plugins.Split(',')) {
    $checks = @(Get-ChildItem (Join-Path $root "extensions/$plugin/Tests/e2e/tools") -Filter '*.e2e.ps1')
    if ($checks.Count -eq 0) { throw "Missing E2E checks for $plugin" }
    foreach ($file in $checks) {
        $check = & $file.FullName
        $verb = if ($check.System) { 'run-system-tool' } else { 'run-tool' }
        $callArgs = @($cli, $verb, $check.Tool, '--path', $ProjectDir, '--url', $Url)
        if ($check.Input) { $callArgs += @('--input', $check.Input) }
        try {
            $out = & node @callArgs 2>&1
            $code = $LASTEXITCODE
            $text = ($out | Out-String).Trim()
            if ($code -ne 0 -and -not $check.ExpectError) { throw "CLI failed: $text" }
            # A transport failure must not count as a defensive tool error.
            if ($text -match '\(network\)|\(timeout\)|ECONNREFUSED|ENOTFOUND') { throw "Transport failure: $text" }
            $result = $null
            try { $result = $text | ConvertFrom-Json } catch { $result = $text }
            if (-not $check.ExpectError -and ($result -is [string] -or $result.isError -eq $true)) { throw "Invalid success: $text" }
            if ($check.ExpectError -and -not $check.Assert) { throw 'Expected-error checks must assert the specific tool error' }
            if ($check.Assert) { & $check.Assert $result }
            Write-Host "PASS $plugin/$($check.Tool)"
        } catch {
            $failures += "$plugin/$($check.Tool): $_"
            Write-Host "FAIL $($failures[-1])"
        }
    }
}
if ($failures.Count) { throw ($failures -join "`n") }
```

`scripts/server_smoke.py`:

```py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
server_smoke.py — LIVE end-to-end smoke for the in-UI local gamedev-mcp-server launch (issue #95).

This is the operator complement to window_smoke.py. window_smoke.py asserts the dock-side CONTRACT
(gating + the start/stop toggle the dev-control bridge exposes) without a real process; THIS script
drives the REAL launch lifecycle against a live GUI editor and verifies the actual OS process + TCP
port, covering the parts a contract test cannot:

  (1) Custom+http: Start -> a local gamedev-mcp-server process actually launches and the port LISTENS.
  (2) Stop -> the server process terminates and the port is FREE again (no orphan).
  (3) Start, then CLOSE the editor -> the server process is ALSO gone (no orphan after editor exit).
  (4) Gating: Start is a no-op (no process, no listener) in Cloud mode and in Custom + stdio.
  (5) Repeated Start/Stop cycles + an external kill leave NO orphaned gamedev-mcp-server processes.

It drives the SAME Start/Stop the Slate button fires, over the dev-control HTTP bridge
(`/control/click` targets `start-server` / `stop-server`, gated to Custom+http by the view-model).

Requirements
------------
- A GUI editor (UnrealEditor.exe, not -Cmd) it launches with UNREAL_MCP_DEV_CONTROL=1 + a port.
- The Custom host must point at a free local port (the server listens there) — pass --server-port,
  which this script writes into the dock via /control/server-url before starting.
- Windows: uses `netstat -ano` + `tasklist` to check the port + process. (Linux/mac: lsof/ps.)

Usage
-----
    python scripts/server_smoke.py --project <.uproject> --port 5177 --server-port 5244 \
        --out-dir tmp/server-smoke

Exit code 0 = every row passed; non-zero = a FAIL or the bridge never came up. NOT a CI gate
(needs a GUI editor + a real server binary) — it is operator evidence for the issue #95 DoD matrix.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import platform
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

DEFAULT_EDITOR = r"C:/Program Files/Epic Games/UE_5.7/Engine/Binaries/Win64/UnrealEditor.exe"
SERVER_PROCESS_NEEDLE = "gamedev-mcp-server"


def _req(port: int, method: str, path: str, body: dict | None = None) -> tuple[int, dict]:
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{port}{path}"
    data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8") if body is not None else None
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, data=data, method=method)
    if data is not None:
        req.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as resp:
            return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read().decode("utf-8"))
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        try:
            return e.code, json.loads(e.read().decode("utf-8"))
        except Exception:
            return e.code, {}


def _wait_health(port: int, timeout_s: float) -> bool:
    deadline = time.time() + timeout_s
    while time.time() < deadline:
        try:
            code, body = _req(port, "GET", "/health")
            if code == 200 and body.get("ok"):
                return True
        except Exception:
            pass
        time.sleep(2.0)
    return False


def _is_windows() -> bool:
    return platform.system() == "Windows"


def port_listening(port: int) -> bool:
    """True when SOME process is LISTENING on the TCP port (cross-platform)."""
    try:
        if _is_windows():
            out = subprocess.run(["netstat", "-ano", "-p", "tcp"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15).stdout
            suffix = f":{port}"
            for line in out.splitlines():
                t = line.strip()
                if "LISTENING" not in t:
                    continue
                parts = t.split()
                if len(parts) >= 5 and parts[1].endswith(suffix):
                    return True
            return False
        else:
            r = subprocess.run(["lsof", "-ti", f"tcp:{port}", "-sTCP:LISTEN"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15)
            return bool(r.stdout.strip())
    except Exception:
        return False


def server_process_count() -> int:
    """Count of running processes whose image name contains gamedev-mcp-server."""
    try:
        if _is_windows():
            out = subprocess.run(["tasklist"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15).stdout
            return sum(1 for ln in out.splitlines() if SERVER_PROCESS_NEEDLE in ln.lower())
        else:
            out = subprocess.run(["ps", "-eo", "comm"], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=15).stdout
            return sum(1 for ln in out.splitlines() if SERVER_PROCESS_NEEDLE in ln.lower())
    except Exception:
        return -1


def wait_for(cond, timeout_s: float, interval: float = 1.0) -> bool:
    deadline = time.time() + timeout_s
    while time.time() < deadline:
        if cond():
            return True
        time.sleep(interval)
    return cond()


class Runner:
    def __init__(self, port: int, server_port: int) -> None:
        self.port = port
        self.server_port = server_port
        self.passed = 0
        self.failed = 0

    def check(self, label: str, cond: bool, detail: str = "") -> None:
        mark = "PASS" if cond else "FAIL"
        (setattr(self, "passed", self.passed + 1) if cond else setattr(self, "failed", self.failed + 1))
        print(f"  [{mark}] {label}" + (f" — {detail}" if detail else ""))

    def set_custom_http(self) -> None:
        _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/connection-mode", {"mode": "Custom"})
        _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/server-url", {"url": f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.server_port}"})
        _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/transport", {"transport": "http"})

    def run(self) -> None:
        baseline = server_process_count()
        print(f"Baseline gamedev-mcp-server processes: {baseline}")

        # (4) Gating: Cloud -> Start no-op (no listener, no new process).
        _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/connection-mode", {"mode": "Cloud"})
        _, b = _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/click", {"target": "start-server"})
        time.sleep(2.0)
        self.check("(4) Cloud: Start is a no-op (port not listening)", not port_listening(self.server_port))
        self.check("(4) Cloud: no server process spawned", server_process_count() <= max(baseline, 0))

        # (4) Gating: Custom + stdio -> Start no-op.
        _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/connection-mode", {"mode": "Custom"})
        _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/transport", {"transport": "stdio"})
        _, b = _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/click", {"target": "start-server"})
        time.sleep(2.0)
        self.check("(4) Custom+stdio: Start is a no-op (port not listening)", not port_listening(self.server_port))

        # (1) Custom + http: Start -> process launches + port listens.
        self.set_custom_http()
        _, b = _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/click", {"target": "start-server"})
        self.check("(1) Start reported serverRunning", b.get("serverRunning") is True, str(b))
        listening = wait_for(lambda: port_listening(self.server_port), timeout_s=30.0)
        self.check(f"(1) Custom+http: port {self.server_port} is LISTENING after Start", listening)
        self.check("(1) a gamedev-mcp-server process is running", server_process_count() > max(baseline, 0))

        # (2) Stop -> process terminates, port freed (no orphan).
        _, b = _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/click", {"target": "stop-server"})
        self.check("(2) Stop reported not running", b.get("serverRunning") is False, str(b))
        freed = wait_for(lambda: not port_listening(self.server_port), timeout_s=20.0)
        self.check(f"(2) port {self.server_port} FREE after Stop (no orphan)", freed)
        gone = wait_for(lambda: server_process_count() <= max(baseline, 0), timeout_s=20.0)
        self.check("(2) gamedev-mcp-server process gone after Stop", gone)

        # (5) Repeated Start/Stop cycles leave no orphan.
        for i in range(3):
            _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/click", {"target": "start-server"})
            wait_for(lambda: port_listening(self.server_port), timeout_s=30.0)
            _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/click", {"target": "stop-server"})
            wait_for(lambda: not port_listening(self.server_port), timeout_s=20.0)
        self.check("(5) repeated Start/Stop: no orphan after 3 cycles",
                   server_process_count() <= max(baseline, 0))

        # (3) Start, then close the editor -> server dies. (Caller closes the editor after run() returns;
        # the post-close port/process check happens in main() so we can observe it AFTER editor exit.)
        _req(self.port, "POST", "/control/click", {"target": "start-server"})
        self.started_for_close_test = wait_for(lambda: port_listening(self.server_port), timeout_s=30.0)
        self.check("(3) pre-close: server launched and listening", self.started_for_close_test)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--project", required=True, help="Path to the host .uproject.")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, required=True, help="UNREAL_MCP_DEV_CONTROL_PORT (from .worktree.env).")
    ap.add_argument("--server-port", type=int, required=True, help="Local port the gamedev-mcp-server listens on.")
    ap.add_argument("--editor", default=DEFAULT_EDITOR, help="UnrealEditor.exe (GUI, not -Cmd).")
    ap.add_argument("--out-dir", default="tmp/server-smoke")
    ap.add_argument("--boot-timeout", type=float, default=600.0)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    Path(args.out_dir).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    env = dict(os.environ)
    env["UNREAL_MCP_DEV_CONTROL"] = "1"
    env["UNREAL_MCP_DEV_CONTROL_PORT"] = str(args.port)
    print(f"Launching editor: {args.editor}\n  project={args.project}\n  dev-control={args.port} server-port={args.server_port}")
    proc = subprocess.Popen([args.editor, args.project], env=env)

    runner = Runner(args.port, args.server_port)
    try:
        print(f"Waiting for dev-control /health on {args.port} (up to {args.boot_timeout:.0f}s)...")
        if not _wait_health(args.port, args.boot_timeout):
            print("FAIL: dev-control bridge never came up. Is UNREAL_MCP_DEV_CONTROL=1 set and the dock open?")
            return 2
        print("Bridge up. Driving server lifecycle...\n")
        runner.run()
    finally:
        print("\nClosing the editor (row 3: server must die with it)...")
        proc.terminate()
        try:
            proc.wait(timeout=60)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            proc.kill()
            proc.wait(timeout=30)

    # (3) After the editor has fully exited, the server it spawned must be gone (force-stop on shutdown).
    gone = wait_for(lambda: not port_listening(args.server_port), timeout_s=30.0)
    runner.check(f"(3) post-close: port {args.server_port} FREE (server died with the editor)", gone)
    runner.check("(3) post-close: no gamedev-mcp-server process survives editor exit",
                 server_process_count() <= 0)

    print(f"\n=== Summary: {runner.passed} passed, {runner.failed} failed ===")
    return 0 if runner.failed == 0 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

`scripts/suite_dependencies.py`:

```py
"""Reuse published bridge/server binaries for E2E; never rebuild or republish core."""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import zipfile

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def resolve(output: Path) -> tuple[Path, Path]:
    import connection_smoke as smoke
    core = json.loads((ROOT / "UnrealMCP/UnrealMCP.uplugin").read_text())["VersionName"]
    folder = output / "dependencies" / f"core-{core}"
    folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # The bridge ships for win-x64, osx-arm64, osx-x64 and linux-x64; Windows on ARM runs win-x64.
    rid = {"win-arm64": "win-x64"}.get(smoke.server_rid(), smoke.server_rid())
    bridge = folder / ("unreal-mcp-bridge.exe" if os.name == "nt" else "unreal-mcp-bridge")
    if not bridge.exists():
        subprocess.run(["gh", "release", "download", f"v{core}", "--repo", "IvanMurzak/Unreal-MCP",
                        "--pattern", f"unreal-mcp-bridge-{rid}.zip", "--dir", str(folder), "--clobber"], check=True)
        with zipfile.ZipFile(folder / f"unreal-mcp-bridge-{rid}.zip") as archive:
            entries = [n for n in archive.namelist() if Path(n).name == bridge.name]
            if len(entries) != 1:
                raise ValueError("Published bridge archive must contain exactly one executable")
            bridge.write_bytes(archive.read(entries[0]))
        if os.name != "nt":
            bridge.chmod(bridge.stat().st_mode | 0o111)
    version = re.search(r"SERVER_VERSION = '([^']+)'", (ROOT / "cli/src/lib/server-version.ts").read_text())[1]
    server = smoke.resolve_server(folder / "Suite.uproject", None, version)
    if not server or not server.is_file():
        raise ValueError("Cannot obtain the pinned MCP server")
    return server.resolve(), bridge.resolve()
```

`scripts/test_extension_monorepo.py`:

```py
import copy
import json
from pathlib import Path
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch
import zipfile

import extension_release as release
import extension_suite as suite


class MonorepoTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_bad_uploaded_archive_never_promotes_index_and_draft_retry_recovers(self):
        class FakeGitHub:
            def __init__(self):
                self.index = release.read(release.ROOT / 'extensions-index.json')
                self.releases = {}
                self.index_writes = 0
                self.corrupt_download = True

            def __call__(self, *args):
                if args[0] == 'api':
                    return 'sha' if 'commits/HEAD' in args[1] else json.dumps(list(self.releases.values()))
                verb, tag = args[1:3]
                if verb == 'create':
                    self.releases[tag] = {'tag_name': tag, 'draft': True, 'bytes': Path(args[-1]).read_bytes().hex()}
                elif verb == 'download':
                    output = Path(args[args.index('--dir') + 1])
                    name = args[args.index('--pattern') + 1]
                    if tag == release.INDEX_TAG:
                        release.write(output / name, self.index)
                    else:
                        data = b'corrupted' if self.corrupt_download else bytes.fromhex(self.releases[tag]['bytes'])
                        (output / name).write_bytes(data)
                elif verb == 'edit':
                    self.releases[tag]['draft'] = False
                elif verb == 'upload':
                    if tag == release.INDEX_TAG:
                        self.index = release.read(Path(args[3]))
                        self.index_writes += 1
                    else:
                        self.releases[tag]['bytes'] = Path(args[3]).read_bytes().hex()
                else:
                    raise AssertionError(args)
                return ''

        github = FakeGitHub()
        original = copy.deepcopy(github.index)
        version = release.validate('UnrealAINiagara')['version']
        tag = f'niagara-v{version}'
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            archive = release.package('UnrealAINiagara', Path(temporary))
            with patch.object(release, 'gh', github), patch.object(release.subprocess, 'check_output', return_value='sha\n'):
                with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'Uploaded archive differs'):
                    release.publish('UnrealAINiagara', archive)
                self.assertEqual(github.index_writes, 0)
                self.assertEqual(github.index, original)
                self.assertTrue(github.releases[tag]['draft'])
                github.corrupt_download = False
                release.publish('UnrealAINiagara', archive)
                self.assertEqual(github.index_writes, 1)
                self.assertFalse(github.releases[tag]['draft'])
                entry = next(e for e in github.index['extensions'] if e['pluginName'] == 'UnrealAINiagara')
                self.assertEqual(entry['releases'][version]['tag'], tag)
                # A full retry retains the initial workflow's bootstrap input.
                # The now-live index must be downloaded, preserving all history.
                with patch.object(release.subprocess, 'run') as probe:
                    probe.return_value.returncode = 0
                    release.publish('UnrealAINiagara', archive, bootstrap=True)
                self.assertEqual(github.index_writes, 2)
                self.assertIn('0.1.0', next(e for e in github.index['extensions']
                                          if e['pluginName'] == 'UnrealAINiagara')['releases'])
                with patch.object(release.subprocess, 'run') as probe:
                    probe.return_value.returncode = 1
                    probe.return_value.stderr = b'HTTP 503: temporarily unavailable'
                    with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'Cannot determine'):
                        release.publish('UnrealAINiagara', archive, bootstrap=True)
                self.assertEqual(github.index_writes, 2)

    def test_misnested_new_extension_cannot_silently_escape_discovery(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            (root / 'extensions/UnrealAINew').mkdir(parents=True)
            release.write(root / 'extensions/UnrealAINew/extension.json', {'pluginName': 'UnrealAINew'})
            with patch.object(release, 'ROOT', root), self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'no matching top-level plugin'):
                release.components()

    def test_default_output_is_absolute(self):
        self.assertTrue(suite.default_output().is_absolute())

    def test_local_ue_lock_excludes_a_second_holder_and_releases(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            path = Path(temporary) / 'ue.lock'
            with suite.machine_lock(path=path):
                with self.assertRaises(OSError):
                    with suite.machine_lock(path=path, timeout_seconds=0):
                        self.fail('A second holder acquired the lock')
            with suite.machine_lock(path=path, timeout_seconds=0):
                pass

    def test_package_is_deterministic_source_only_and_contains_one_plugin(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            output = Path(temporary)
            package = release.package('UnrealAINiagara', output)
            first = package.read_bytes()
            self.assertEqual(first, release.package('UnrealAINiagara', output).read_bytes())
            with zipfile.ZipFile(package) as archive:
                names = archive.namelist()
                self.assertTrue(any(n.endswith('UnrealAINiagara.uplugin') for n in names))
                self.assertEqual(archive.read('UnrealAINiagara/README.md'),
                                 (release.ROOT / 'extensions/UnrealAINiagara/README.md').read_bytes())
                self.assertTrue(any(n.endswith('UnrealAINiagaraSpec.cpp') for n in names))
                self.assertTrue(all(n.startswith('UnrealAINiagara/') for n in names))
                self.assertFalse(any('/Binaries/' in n or '/Intermediate/' in n for n in names))

    def test_independent_publication_preserves_other_packages_and_history(self):
        index = release.read(release.ROOT / 'extensions-index.json')
        before = copy.deepcopy(index)
        metadata = release.validate('UnrealAINiagara')
        metadata['version'] = '0.2.0'
        result = release.update_index(index, metadata, 'niagara-v0.2.0', 'a' * 64)
        self.assertEqual(index, before)
        old = {e['pluginName']: e for e in before['extensions']}
        new = {e['pluginName']: e for e in result['extensions']}
        for plugin in old:
            if plugin != 'UnrealAINiagara':
                self.assertEqual(old[plugin], new[plugin])
        self.assertEqual(new['UnrealAINiagara']['version'], '0.2.0')
        self.assertIn('0.1.0', new['UnrealAINiagara']['releases'])
        self.assertEqual(new['UnrealAINiagara']['releases']['0.2.0']['tag'], 'niagara-v0.2.0')

    def test_published_versions_cannot_be_overwritten(self):
        index = release.read(release.ROOT / 'extensions-index.json')
        meta = release.validate('UnrealAINiagara')
        tag = f"niagara-v{meta['version']}"
        index = release.update_index(index, meta, tag, 'a' * 64)
        self.assertEqual(index, release.update_index(index, meta, tag, 'a' * 64))
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'immutable'):
            release.update_index(index, meta, tag, 'b' * 64)

    def test_isolated_profiles_have_no_sibling_files_and_preserve_spec_sources(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            engine = root / 'engine'
            suite.write_json(engine / 'Engine/Build/Build.version', {'MajorVersion': 5, 'MinorVersion': 8})
            project = suite.prepare(engine, 'isolated/Niagara', ['UnrealAINiagara'], root / 'out', strict=True)
            plugins = project.parent / 'Plugins'
            self.assertEqual({p.name for p in plugins.iterdir()}, {'UnrealMCP', 'UnrealAINiagara'})
            self.assertTrue(list((plugins / 'UnrealAINiagara').rglob('*Spec.cpp')))
            rules = next((plugins / 'UnrealAINiagara').rglob('*.Build.cs')).read_text()
            self.assertIn('bUseUnity = false', rules)
            self.assertIn('PCHUsageMode.NoPCHs', rules)
            self.assertNotIn('UnrealMcpEditorTests', (plugins / 'UnrealMCP/UnrealMCP.uplugin').read_text())
            # Plant an unexpected plugin: a reused dirty profile must fail closed.
            (plugins / 'UnrealAIPCG').mkdir()
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'Unexpected plugin'):
                suite.prepare(engine, 'isolated/Niagara', ['UnrealAINiagara'], root / 'out', strict=True)

    def test_unchanged_profile_does_not_invalidate_ubt_caches(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            engine = root / 'engine'
            suite.write_json(engine / 'Engine/Build/Build.version', {'MajorVersion': 5, 'MinorVersion': 8})
            project = suite.prepare(engine, 'all', ['UnrealAINiagara'], root / 'out', core_tests=True)
            files = [p for p in project.parent.rglob('*') if p.is_file()]
            stamps = {p: p.stat().st_mtime_ns for p in files}
            suite.prepare(engine, 'all', ['UnrealAINiagara'], root / 'out', core_tests=True)
            self.assertEqual(stamps, {p: p.stat().st_mtime_ns for p in files})
            descriptor = suite.extensions()['UnrealAINiagara'] / 'UnrealAINiagara.uplugin'
            copied = project.parent / 'Plugins/UnrealAINiagara/UnrealAINiagara.uplugin'
            self.assertEqual(descriptor.read_bytes(), copied.read_bytes())

    def test_report_gate_catches_missing_extension_and_missing_individual_test(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            report = Path(temporary) / 'index.json'
            minimum = release.read(release.ROOT / 'tests/automation-inventory.json')['UnrealAINiagara']
            tests = [{'fullTestPath': f'UnrealAINiagara.case{i}', 'state': 'Success'} for i in range(minimum)]
            suite.write_json(report, {'failed': 0, 'tests': tests})
            self.assertEqual(suite.check_report(report, ['UnrealAINiagara'], core_tests=False)['passed'], minimum)
            suite.write_json(report, {'failed': 0, 'tests': tests[:-1]})
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'Missing Automation coverage'):
                suite.check_report(report, ['UnrealAINiagara'], core_tests=False)
            suite.write_json(report, {'failed': 0, 'tests': tests})
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'Missing Automation coverage'):
                suite.check_report(report, ['UnrealAINiagara', 'UnrealAIPCG'], core_tests=False)

    def test_missing_report_and_nonpassing_tests_are_failures(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            report = Path(temporary) / 'index.json'
            with self.assertRaises(FileNotFoundError):
                suite.check_report(report, [])
            suite.write_json(report, {'failed': 0, 'tests': [{'fullTestPath': 'UnrealAINiagara.case', 'state': 'NotRun'}]})
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, 'did not pass'):
                suite.check_report(report, ['UnrealAINiagara'], core_tests=False)

    def test_every_extension_has_inventory_and_unique_tools(self):
        inventory = release.read(release.ROOT / 'tests/automation-inventory.json')
        ids, tools = set(), set()
        for plugin in release.components():
            metadata = release.validate(plugin)
            self.assertIn(plugin, inventory)
            self.assertNotIn(metadata['extensionId'], ids)
            ids.add(metadata['extensionId'])
            for tool in metadata['tools']:
                self.assertNotIn(tool['name'], tools)
                tools.add(tool['name'])

    def test_migrated_catalog_names_remain_valid_cli_install_aliases(self):
        seed = release.read(release.ROOT / 'extensions-index.json')
        for entry in seed['extensions']:
            metadata = release.validate(entry['pluginName'])
            self.assertEqual(metadata['extensionId'], entry['extensionId'])
            self.assertEqual(metadata['name'], entry['name'])


if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main()
```

```py
"""Cases for scripts/release_dependency_guard.py: which pins a release may ship (hermetic: a fake nuget.org)."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import tempfile
import textwrap
import unittest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
import release_dependency_guard as guard

PUBLISHED = {
    "com.ivanmurzak.reflectornet": ["5.5.0"],
    "com.ivanmurzak.rql": ["0.1.0", "0.2.0"],
    "com.ivanmurzak.codeexec": ["0.3.0"],
}
RQL_COMMITS = {"0.1.0": "aaaa1111", "0.2.0": "b36b8e44f5952ea808af0918347774de5da69b6f"}
NUSPEC = '<package xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/packaging/2013/05/nuspec.xsd"><metadata>' \
         '<id>com.IvanMurzak.Rql</id><repository type="git" commit="%s" /></metadata></package>'

BRIDGE_CSPROJ = """<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
  <PropertyGroup><Version>0.25.0</Version><RqlVersion>%s</RqlVersion></PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.ReflectorNet" Version="5.5.0" />
    <PackageReference Include="com.IvanMurzak.Rql" Version="$(RqlVersion)" />
  </ItemGroup>
</Project>
"""

FEED_PROPS = """<Project>
  <PropertyGroup>
    <RestoreAdditionalProjectSources>$(RestoreAdditionalProjectSources);$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)prerelease-packages</RestoreAdditionalProjectSources>
  </PropertyGroup>
</Project>
"""

RQL_PUBLISHED = ("- Source: https://github.com/IvanMurzak/RQL, commit `b36b8e44f5952ea808af0918347774de5da69b6f` "
                 "(`com.IvanMurzak.Rql` %s).\n")
RQL_UNRELEASED = ("- Source: https://github.com/IvanMurzak/RQL, commit `602ce7c` (main, unreleased; the\n"
                  "  sidecar pins the matching pre-release package `com.IvanMurzak.Rql` 0.3.0-dev.602ce7c).\n")


def fake_registry(published=PUBLISHED, fail=False):
    def fetch(url):
        if fail:
            raise guard.RegistryError("offline")
        if url.endswith(".nuspec"):
            package, version = url.split("/")[-3:-1]
            commit = RQL_COMMITS.get(version) if package == "com.ivanmurzak.rql" else None
            return None if commit is None else (NUSPEC % commit).encode()
        versions = published.get(url.split("/")[-2])
        return None if versions is None else json.dumps({"versions": versions}).encode()
    return guard.NuGetRegistry(fetch)


class GuardTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(self.temp.name)
        self.fixture()

    def write(self, relative, text):
        path = self.root / relative
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")

    def fixture(self, rql="0.2.0", vendored_rql=None, code_exec="0.3.0", min_core="1.0.0", feed=False):
        self.write("bridge/src/com.IvanMurzak.Unreal.MCP.Bridge.csproj", BRIDGE_CSPROJ % rql)
        self.write("bridge/tests/com.IvanMurzak.Unreal.MCP.Bridge.Tests.csproj",
                   '<Project><ItemGroup><PackageReference Include="xunit" Version="3.0.0-pre.1" /></ItemGroup></Project>')
        if feed:
            self.write("bridge/Directory.Build.props", FEED_PROPS)
        self.write(guard.RQL_VENDORED, "# RQL C++ runtime (vendored)\n\n" + (vendored_rql or RQL_PUBLISHED % rql))
        self.write(guard.CODE_EXEC_VENDORED, f"copied verbatim from Code-Exec at release **{code_exec}** (tag `nuget-v{code_exec}`).\n")
        self.write("extensions/UnrealAIGAS/extension.json", json.dumps({"version": "0.1.1", "minCoreVersion": min_core}, indent=2))
        self.write("cli/package.json", json.dumps({"dependencies": {"fflate": "^0.8.3"}}, indent=2))

    def problems(self, registry=None):
        _, problems = guard.run(self.root, registry or fake_registry())
        return [(guard.rel(p.file, self.root), p.message) for p in problems]

    def test_published_pins_pass(self):
        pins, problems = guard.run(self.root, fake_registry())
        self.assertEqual([], problems)
        self.assertEqual({"bridge/src/com.IvanMurzak.Unreal.MCP.Bridge.csproj", guard.RQL_VENDORED.as_posix()},
                         {guard.rel(p.file, self.root) for p in pins if p.package == "com.IvanMurzak.Rql"})

    def test_current_main_shape_fails_on_every_leg(self):
        self.fixture(rql="0.3.0-dev.602ce7c", vendored_rql=RQL_UNRELEASED, feed=True)
        problems = self.problems()
        self.assertIn(("bridge/src/com.IvanMurzak.Unreal.MCP.Bridge.csproj",
                       "com.IvanMurzak.Rql 0.3.0-dev.602ce7c is a pre-release version"), problems)
        self.assertIn((guard.RQL_VENDORED.as_posix(), "com.IvanMurzak.Rql 0.3.0-dev.602ce7c is a pre-release version"), problems)
        self.assertTrue(any(f == "bridge/Directory.Build.props" and "prerelease-packages" in m for f, m in problems))
        self.assertFalse(any("xunit" in m for _, m in problems))  # the test project ships nothing

    def test_vendored_rql_must_match_the_sidecar_pin_and_be_published(self):
        self.fixture(vendored_rql=RQL_PUBLISHED % "0.1.0")
        self.assertIn((guard.RQL_VENDORED.as_posix(),
                       "vendored RQL C++ runtime is com.IvanMurzak.Rql 0.1.0 but the sidecar pins 0.2.0"), self.problems())
        self.fixture(vendored_rql=RQL_PUBLISHED % "0.3.0-dev.1")
        self.assertIn((guard.RQL_VENDORED.as_posix(), "com.IvanMurzak.Rql 0.3.0-dev.1 is a pre-release version"), self.problems())
        self.fixture(vendored_rql="- Source: https://github.com/IvanMurzak/RQL, commit `abc`.\n")
        self.assertEqual([(guard.RQL_VENDORED.as_posix(),
                           "vendored com.IvanMurzak.Rql: no release version marker (copy it from a published release)")],
                         self.problems())

    def test_vendored_rql_commit_must_be_the_released_one(self):
        self.fixture(vendored_rql=(RQL_PUBLISHED % "0.2.0").replace("b36b8e44f5952ea808af0918347774de5da69b6f", "602ce7c"))
        self.assertEqual([(guard.RQL_VENDORED.as_posix(), "vendored RQL C++ runtime is commit 602ce7c but "
                           "com.IvanMurzak.Rql 0.2.0 was packed from b36b8e44f595 (copy the sources of that release)")],
                         self.problems())
        self.fixture(vendored_rql=(RQL_PUBLISHED % "0.2.0").replace("b36b8e44f5952ea808af0918347774de5da69b6f", "b36b8e4"))
        self.assertEqual([], self.problems())  # a short sha of the released commit is fine
        self.fixture(vendored_rql="- Source: RQL (`com.IvanMurzak.Rql` 0.2.0).\n")
        self.assertEqual([(guard.RQL_VENDORED.as_posix(),
                           "vendored RQL C++ runtime: no source commit (commit `<sha>`) recorded")], self.problems())

    def test_npm_unresolved_property_and_missing_file(self):
        self.write("cli/package.json", json.dumps({"dependencies": {"fflate": "next"}}))
        self.write("bridge/src/com.IvanMurzak.Unreal.MCP.Bridge.csproj", BRIDGE_CSPROJ.replace("$(RqlVersion)", "$(Nope)") % "0.2.0")
        (self.root / guard.CODE_EXEC_VENDORED).unlink()

                          ("bridge/src/com.IvanMurzak.Unreal.MCP.Bridge.csproj", "com.IvanMurzak.Rql: cannot resolve version '$(Nope)'"),
                          (guard.CODE_EXEC_VENDORED.as_posix(), "expected file is missing (update release_dependency_guard.py)")},
                         set(self.problems()))

    def test_unpublished_stable_pin_fails(self):

    def test_registry_outage_fails_closed(self):

        self.assertTrue(all("cannot verify on nuget.org" in m or "cannot read the nuspec" in m for _, m in problems))

    def test_code_exec_and_extension_core_floor(self):

        problems = self.problems()

        self.assertIn(("extensions/UnrealAIGAS/extension.json",
                       "Unreal-MCP core (minCoreVersion) 1.1.0-beta is a pre-release version"), problems)

    def test_nuget_config_local_feed_fails(self):
        self.write("bridge/nuget.config", textwrap.dedent("""\
            <configuration><packageSources>
              <add key="nuget.org" value="https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json" />

        self.assertEqual([("bridge/nuget.config", "package source 'pre' is the local feed './prerelease-packages'")],
                         self.problems())
```
